--------

Features
--------

.. hlist::
   :columns: 3

   * Finite difference method
   * Scattering loss
   * Bend modes
   * Symmetries
   * Perfectly matched layers
   * Sub-pixel averaging
   * General anisotropy
   * Magnetic materials
   * Non-uniform meshing
   * Eigenmode expansion (EME)
   * Multi-physics (thermal, electrostatic)
   * Second-order nonlinear optics

Finite difference method
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

The finite difference method (FDM) is used to solve the waveguide eigenmodes. The electric and magnetics fields are solved in a Yee grid, and they are subsequently interpolated to common grid points. Features are added to support subpixel averaging, bend modes, anisotropic materials, non-uniform meshing, and mode symmetries.

    Z. Zhu and T. G. Brown, ''Full-vectorial finite-difference analysis of microstructured optical fibers,'' Opt. Express **10**, 853 (2002).

Boundary conditions
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Symmetric or anti-symmetric boundary conditions can be applied to the south and west sides of the simulation window with the setting parameter ``boundary_condition``. By explicitly setting the symmetry with an 'S' (symmetric) or 'A' (anti-symmetric), the refractive index profile is forced to be symmetric in the specified vertical or horizontal direction. Another option is to set the boundary condition to 'TE' or 'TM' and the solver will decide if vertical, horizontal, or both symmetries exist in the specified refractive index profile. These options will choose the appropriate 'S' or 'A' boundaries to solve the fundamental TE or TM mode with the maximum available symmetry.

Meshing
^^^^^^^

Shapes define the refractive index profile of the waveguide and a meshing algorithm using contour-path effective permittivities is implemented. On the Yee grid, the permittivity and permeability arrays are unique for each x, y, and z direction. The plot of the refractive index shows the exact shapes that are defined, and the actual permittivity and permeability arrays are available using the ``get`` method. Calculated fields correspond to the center points of the meshed grid (``x`` and ``y``).

    A. Mohammadi, H. Nadgaran, and M. Agio, ''Contour-path effective permittivities for the two-dimensional finite-difference time-domain method,'' Opt. Express **13**, 10367 (2005).

Non-uniform mesh
""""""""""""""""

A non-uniform mesh can be specified to increase the grid spacing in the perimeter area of the simulation window. This is helpful to reduce the simulation time when using a fine grid mesh. The primary simulation window is defined by the ``window_width``, ``window_height``, ``x_resolution``, and ``y_resolution`` parameters. To add a non-uniform grid, the parameters ``expansion_size`` and ``expansion_resolution`` must be defined. Expanded regions taper the resolution from the primary window to a maximum value of the ``expansion_resolution``. However, the tapering is terminated if the ``expansion_size`` is reached before the resolution has reached the ``expansion_resolution`` value. Unique values for the ``expansion_size`` can be defined for each edge of the simulation window. The user must investigate convergence of the effective index and loss values by varying the window size, expanded area size, and grid resolutions.

Citing EMode
^^^^^^^^^^^^

If you use EMode for design or analysis in a publication, please use the following citation.

    EMode [Software] from EMode Photonix. Available at `emodephotonix.com <https://www.emodephotonix.com>`_.



File management
---------------

Simulation data are stored in an EMode Photonix file with the extension '.eph'. This file is created when a simulation is initialized, and existing simulation files can be opened by EMode for further analysis.

.. data:: init

    Create a simulation instance with an associated '.eph' file to run the simulation and store data. This function is automatically called when the emodeconnection class is initialized.

    :param str save_path: path to save the simulation file relative to the current working directory, default: '.'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name. It becomes the file name, so it must be a valid file name on Linux, macOS and Windows alike: not empty, none of the characters ``< > : " / \ | ? *`` or control characters, no trailing dot or space, and not a device name Windows reserves (``CON``, ``PRN``, ``AUX``, ``NUL``, ``COM1`` to ``COM9`` or ``LPT1`` to ``LPT9``, also with an extension). Any other name raises an error. Default: 'emode'

.. data:: open

    Open an existing simulation '.eph' file. This can be used to retrieve previous simulation data or to run a simulation based on a template.

    :param str save_path: path to open the simulation file relative to the current working directory, default: '.'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'
    :param new_simulation_name: new simulation name so the old file is not over-written, under the same naming rules as ``simulation_name`` in :data:`init`, default: False (the original ``simulation_name`` is reused)
    :type new_simulation_name: bool or str
    :param bool force: if a file with the target name is already open elsewhere, open it anyway instead of auto-renaming to an available filename, default: False

.. data:: get
    :no-index:

    Extract data from an existing simulation to your Python environment.

    :param str key: name of the variable or parameter to extract. This can also be a list of fields of any combination of [``Ex``, ``Ey``, ``Ez``, ``Hx``, ``Hy``, ``Hz``, ``Sx``, ``Sy``, ``Sz``]. See :doc:`Variable Descriptions </emodeguide/variables>` for a complete list and description of all available variables, settings included (``get('num_modes')``). Use ``'S_matrix'`` (EMode\ :sup:`3D`\  only) to retrieve the scattering matrix from a solved EME chain as an :class:`SMatrix` object.
    :param str profile: name of the profile to extract the data defined by ``key`` from, default: '_default'. A multi-wavelength profile returns a dict keyed by wavelength.
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: inspect

    Return the names :data:`get` can read (see :doc:`Variable Descriptions </emodeguide/variables>`): the top-level variables in the simulation file, followed by the per-profile variables and settings of ``profile``. Names beginning with an underscore are internal.

    :param str profile: name of the profile whose variables and settings to list, default: '_default'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: get_fields

    Extract field data from an existing simulation to your Python environment.

    :param str key: name of the field to extract a list of fields of any combination of [``Ex``, ``Ey``, ``Ez``, ``Hx``, ``Hy``, ``Hz``, ``Sx``, ``Sy``, ``Sz``].
    :type key: str or list[str]
    :param bool include_expand: whether to include the expanded region, default: True
    :param bool include_pml: whether to include the PML region, default: True
    :param bool unfold: whether to include the full window (unfolded) or strictly the solved window (potentially smaller due to applied symmetries), default: True
    :param str profile: name of the profile to extract the data defined by ``key`` from, default: '_default'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'
    :return: a Field object for a single-wavelength profile, or a FieldSet (a Field for each wavelength, indexable/iterable like a dict[float, Field]) for a multi-wavelength profile.
    :rtype: Field | FieldSet

.. data:: get_grid

    Extract grid data from an existing simulation to your Python environment.

    :param bool include_expand: whether to include the expanded region, default: True
    :param bool include_pml: whether to include the PML region, default: True
    :param bool unfold: whether to include the full window (unfolded) or strictly the solved window (potentially smaller due to applied symmetries), default: True
    :param str profile: name of the profile to extract the grid from, default: '_default'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'
    :return: a Grid object for a single-wavelength profile, or a GridSet (a Grid for each wavelength, indexable/iterable like a dict[float, Grid]) for a multi-wavelength profile.
    :rtype: Grid | GridSet

.. data:: get_shape

    Extract shape data from an existing simulation. Returns the shape object with a ``metadata`` dictionary attached (scattering and confinement results for that shape).

    :param str key: name of the shape to extract
    :param str profile: name of the profile to extract the shape from, default: '_default'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: get_profile

    Extract a full profile object from an existing simulation. Returns a Profile object containing the settings, shapes, grid, and field data associated with the named profile.

    :param str profile: name of the profile to extract, default: '_default'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: create_profile_set

    Group several single-wavelength profiles into one named multi-wavelength profile set, keyed internally by wavelength. All named profiles must share identical shapes, and each must be at a distinct wavelength. The original individual profiles are deleted once grouped. The default ``profile_set_name`` replaces the ``'_default'`` profile. One member of the set is ``profile='SET.WAVELENGTH'`` (``'wg.1550'``) or ``profile='SET.MEMBER'`` by its original name.

    :param profiles: names of the profiles to group
    :type profiles: str or list[str]
    :param str profile_set_name: name of the resulting profile set, default: '_default'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: delete_profile

    Delete a named profile (or reset the ``_default`` profile's settings) from the simulation file.

    :param str profile: name of the profile to delete
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: clear_field_data

    Deletes the following data from one profile, or from every profile including the default profile, to reduce the '.eph' file size: ``Fx``, ``Fy``, ``Ex``, ``Ey``, ``Ez``, ``Hx``, ``Hy``, ``Hz``, ``Sx``, ``Sy``, ``Sz``, ``x``, ``y``, ``permittivity``, ``permeability``. A profile that does not exist raises an error.

    :param str profile: name of the profile to clear (``'NAME.WAVELENGTH'`` for one wavelength of a multi-wavelength profile), default: None (every profile)
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: save

    Saves a simulation file and keeps the simulation file in the 'open' state.

    :param bool save_all_fields: whether to save each solved profile's full ``E`` and ``H`` fields as well as its raw field data (``Fx`` and ``Fy``). A file saved this way opens with the fields ready, which take about five times the space of the raw field data. Each save decides again, so a plain save of a reopened file leaves them out, default: False
    :param str file_type: file type to save the simulation file as, either 'eph' or 'mat', default: 'eph'
    :param bool close: whether to close the simulation file after saving, default: False
    :param str new_save_path: if set, saves the simulation file in this new path, default: None
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: close

    Saves or deletes a simulation file. This function is called through the "close" method of emodeconnection, and these optional parameters can be passed directly to the "close" method.

    :param bool save: saves simulation file if True and deletes the simulation file if False, default: True
    :param bool save_all_fields: whether to save each solved profile's full ``E`` and ``H`` fields as well as its raw field data (``Fx`` and ``Fy``). A file saved this way opens with the fields ready, which take about five times the space of the raw field data. Each save decides again, so a plain save of a reopened file leaves them out, default: False
    :param str file_type: file type to save the simulation file as, either 'eph' or 'mat', default: 'eph'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'



EME
---

Every section function below accepts a ``ports`` argument, which names, windows, or displaces the ports on either end of the section, in place of its default left and right ports. Sections are otherwise connected in the order they are declared. Use :data:`connect_ports` to wire named ports explicitly instead, including into branching topologies. See :ref:`ports` for the port model, the ``Port`` and ``Bounds`` classes, and :func:`make_angled_facet_port` for declaring an angled facet on a port.

.. data:: EME_settings

    Declare global EME defaults that are inherited by sections created afterward. Each parameter left unspecified leaves the corresponding stored default unchanged. A section's own ``settings`` argument at creation still overrides these globals. Sections created before this call are not affected.

    :param apply_scattering: whether interfacial scattering loss is automatically applied to the S-matrix, either for every wavelength (True), no wavelengths (False), or only the listed wavelengths, default: False
    :type apply_scattering: bool or list[float]
    :param str beta_interpolation: either 'uniform' or 'linear' to specify how the propagation constant is interpolated between z-slices of a taper/gds section, default: 'uniform'
    :param junction_normalization: controls how junction S-matrices are power-normalized. It takes either a single bool/'gain' value applied to both junction kinds, or a dict with 'inter_section' and 'intra_section' keys, each accepting True (full SVD unitarization), False (raw, unnormalized), or 'gain' (clip singular values at 1 while keeping the raw lossy mode-matching), default: 'gain' for inter-section junctions and True for intra-section junctions. It applies to junctions with a plane-wave side (:data:`pwd_section`) or an angled facet. A junction between two mode-solved cross-sections conserves power by construction and is not normalized.
    :type junction_normalization: bool or str or dict
    :param float overlap_variation: threshold of mode-list overlap between z-slices used by the automatic z-slicing bisection for taper/gds sections, default: 0.01
    :param float minimum_z_step: [nm] the minimum allowed z-step for the automatic z-slicing bisection, default: 0.1
    :param float snap_window: the fraction of a slice's length around its midpoint within which the automatic z-slicing bisects at a cross-section already solved elsewhere (for the same settings, mesh and wavelength) instead of at the midpoint, which saves a mode solve wherever two tapers or GDS sections share widths. 0 always bisects at the midpoint, default: 0.25
    :param str initial_slices: how a taper or GDS section is sliced before the automatic z-slicing bisection refines it, either 'auto' (boundaries placed where the cross-section changes, from its rasterized refractive index: none along a straight run, evenly along a linear taper, densely inside a short fast feature, and at every corner of a GDS outline) or 'single' (one slice, the behavior before EMode 1.0.6). Refinement still runs afterward and decides the final slicing, so the choice moves results only within its tolerance and changes how many rounds it takes. A ``warm_start`` in :data:`EME` takes its slices from the previous solve instead, default: 'auto'
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

    A section's own ``settings`` dictionary accepts the keys above (except ``simulation_name``), and five more that tune the slicing. They are rarely needed, and ``EME_settings`` does not take them.

    * ``schedule_samples``: the number of positions along the section at which the refractive index is rasterized (no mode solve) to find where it changes, at least 2, default: 128
    * ``schedule_change_per_slice``: the relative change in the rasterized index that one initial slice spans, so a smaller value starts with more slices, default: 0.05
    * ``schedule_max_slices``: the largest number of initial slices, default: 64
    * ``schedule_coarsen``: how many times coarser than the profile's mesh the index is rasterized, at least 1, default: 4
    * ``slice_phase_limit``: a slice over which the cross-section changes is kept shorter than ``slice_phase_limit * wavelength / (2 n_max)``, where ``n_max`` is the largest effective index of its modes. Equal slices longer than about ``wavelength / (2 n_max)`` act as a grating and reflect in phase, which refinement cannot see. The initial slices are cut evenly under this limit, up to ``schedule_max_slices``. Refinement then estimates how much power each guided mode loses to the steps' in-phase reflections and conversions, and cuts a slice under the limit only where that power is significant, so a long, slow taper keeps about ``schedule_max_slices`` slices. Between 0 and 1, or None to turn it off, default: 0.8

    For example, ``taper_section(..., settings={'schedule_change_per_slice': 0.02})``. Initial slice boundaries closer together than ``minimum_z_step`` are merged.

.. data:: straight_section

    Define a uniform-cross-section waveguide section for the EME solver. Sections are placed sequentially in the z-direction in the order they are declared (or updated, if ``name`` already exists).

    :param str name: section name, default: an auto-generated number
    :param str profile: name of the profile that defines the section's cross-section
    :param float length: [nm] the length of the section
    :param offset: [nm] transverse displacement of this section relative to whatever its ports connect to. A single value is taken as the x-offset, default: (0, 0). **Legacy**: this is the same displacement as :class:`Port`'s own ``offset`` applied to every port of the section at once, and setting both on one section raises an error. Prefer declaring ``offset`` on the specific port that sits off-axis.
    :type offset: float or tuple[float, float]
    :param ports: replace the section's default ``[Port('left', None, 'left'), Port('right', None, 'right')]`` on a per-side basis, where a supplied port replaces every existing port on the same side, and multiple ports may share a side. See :class:`Port`, default: None (keep existing/default ports)
    :type ports: list[Port] or None
    :param nonlinear: declare a :math:`\chi^{(2)}` process on this section (EMode\ :sup:`3D`\  only), one of ``SHGProcess(pump_wavelength=...)``, ``SFGProcess(pump_wavelength_1=..., pump_wavelength_2=...)`` or ``DFGProcess(pump_wavelength=..., signal_wavelength=...)`` from ``emodeconnection``. You name the process's *input* wavelength(s), and the remaining one follows from energy conservation and is matched against the section's own profile wavelengths. Quasi-phase matching is declared on the process with ``poling_period`` [nm], plus ``duty_cycle`` (default: 0.5) and ``qpm_order`` (default: 1). Setting ``inverted=True`` instead flips the local :math:`\chi^{(2)}` sign for this section alone, the building block for poling assembled by hand from alternating sections. The two routes agree. Omitting ``nonlinear`` (or passing ``None``) when updating an existing section leaves the declared process in place, passing a new one replaces it, and ``nonlinear=False`` removes it, so the section propagates linearly again. A pump must also be declared, see ``excitation`` in :data:`settings`, and the power-dependent result is read back with ``get('response')``. The process also carries ``z_samples`` (default: 100), the number of points at which the forward amplitudes are recorded along each slice of this section once the driven solve converges. Those reach the caller as ``get('response').power_vs_z(wavelength)``, which returns the pump or signal power against position from a single solve rather than one solve per length. Set it to 0 to skip the sampling. A pulse's nonlinearity is declared instead with a ``PulsedProcess``, see :ref:`pulsed nonlinear propagation <pulsed-propagation>`. Default: None
    :type nonlinear: SHGProcess or SFGProcess or DFGProcess or PulsedProcess or False or None
    :param settings: per-section overrides of the :data:`EME_settings`, merged onto the current global EME settings (or onto the section's existing settings, when updating), e.g. ``settings={'overlap_variation': 0.005}``, default: None
    :type settings: dict or None
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: pwd_section

    Define a free space section, in which the field is expanded in plane waves (a plane-wave decomposition, PWD) over a uniform material, rather than in the guided modes of a cross-section. This is intended for gaps, facets, and free space propagation between waveguide sections. The junctions between a free space section and its neighbors are computed analytically instead of from a mode solve.

    The basis is the set of plane-wave harmonics of the section window, with transverse wavevectors ``kx = 2*pi*m/window_width`` and ``ky = 2*pi*n/window_height``, each harmonic carrying both a TE and a TM polarization. At least one of ``max_order``, ``max_kt``, or ``num_modes`` is required to truncate the basis. When more than one is given, they are applied in the order ``max_order``, ``max_kt``, ``num_modes``.

    :param str name: section name, default: an auto-generated number
    :param float length: [nm] the length of the section
    :param material: the material filling the section, either a material name (from the material database) or a ~MaterialProperties or ~MaterialSpec object. It must be isotropic, default: "Vacuum"
    :type material: str or ~MaterialProperties or ~MaterialSpec
    :param str profile: name of the profile that supplies the default window and the wavelength(s) of the section, default: '_default'
    :param window: [nm] the (width, height) of the plane-wave window, which overrides the window of ``profile``, default: None (use the ``window_width`` and ``window_height`` of ``profile``)
    :type window: tuple[float, float] or None
    :param offset: [nm] transverse displacement of the window's origin, which is its horizontal center and bottom edge, default: (0, 0)
    :type offset: tuple[float, float]
    :param max_order: the largest harmonic order to keep in the x- and y-directions, so that ``|m| <= max_order[0]`` and ``|n| <= max_order[1]``, default: None
    :type max_order: tuple[int, int] or None
    :param float max_kt: [1/nm] the largest transverse wavevector magnitude to keep, default: None
    :param int num_modes: the largest number of modes to keep, counting both polarizations of each harmonic, and applied after ``max_order`` and ``max_kt``. The basis always keeps a harmonic together with its opposite-direction pair, so the resulting count can land slightly below the requested value. Default: None
    :param ports: replace the section's default ``[Port('left', None, 'left'), Port('right', None, 'right')]`` on a per-side basis, where a supplied port replaces every existing port on the same side, and multiple ports may share a side. See :class:`Port`, default: None (keep existing/default ports)
    :type ports: list[Port] or None
    :param settings: per-section overrides of the :data:`EME_settings`, default: None
    :type settings: dict or None
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

    .. note::
       A junction with a free space section matches the two continuity conditions (for E and for H) against the modes of the side the light arrives from. When the other side has fewer modes, the junction cannot represent every incident field, and some incident modes leave it with almost none of their power: they are dropped by the truncated basis, not attenuated by any physics. EMode warns when an incident mode keeps less than 1 % of its power, naming the dropped modes and the reflected plus transmitted power over all of the incident modes. Raise the mode count on the side with fewer modes, ``num_modes`` of the waveguide section or ``max_order``, ``max_kt`` or ``num_modes`` of the free space section.

    .. note::
       The reflection of a confined mode at a facet into free space is not the modal Fresnel value ``((n_eff - n) / (n_eff + n))^2``. That formula gives the free space the admittance of a single plane wave at normal incidence. A mode confined to a fraction of a wavelength is a spread of plane waves, and those at an angle see a different admittance: smaller for the field component normal to their plane of incidence, larger for the one in it. A quasi-TE mode therefore reflects more than its modal Fresnel value and a quasi-TM mode less, more so the tighter the confinement. A 2640 x 816 nm Si guide meeting SiO2 reflects 0.216 of its quasi-TE fundamental, 1.35 times its modal Fresnel value of 0.160, and an independent solve with an empty section in place of the free space agrees within 1.4 %. Give the waveguide section periodic walls (``boundary_condition='PP'``) and the free space section the same window, so that both describe the same far side. Walls on a section that stands in for free space raise the reflection when they are close to the guide (by 35 % with walls 1 µm from that guide's core).

.. data:: taper_section

    Define a section that linearly interpolates its cross-section between two profiles for the EME solver, automatically slicing the z-direction to track the mode evolution.

    :param str name: section name, default: an auto-generated number
    :param str profile: name of the profile that defines the section beginning
    :param str profile_end: name of the profile that defines the section ending
    :param float length: [nm] the length of the section
    :param ports: replace the section's default ``[Port('left', None, 'left'), Port('right', None, 'right')]`` on a per-side basis, where a supplied port replaces every existing port on the same side, and multiple ports may share a side. See :class:`Port`, default: None (keep existing/default ports)
    :type ports: list[Port] or None
    :param nonlinear: declare a :math:`\chi^{(2)}` process on this section (EMode\ :sup:`3D`\  only), one of ``SHGProcess(pump_wavelength=...)``, ``SFGProcess(pump_wavelength_1=..., pump_wavelength_2=...)`` or ``DFGProcess(pump_wavelength=..., signal_wavelength=...)`` from ``emodeconnection``. You name the process's *input* wavelength(s), and the remaining one follows from energy conservation and is matched against the section's own profile wavelengths. Quasi-phase matching is declared on the process with ``poling_period`` [nm], plus ``duty_cycle`` (default: 0.5) and ``qpm_order`` (default: 1). Setting ``inverted=True`` instead flips the local :math:`\chi^{(2)}` sign for this section alone, the building block for poling assembled by hand from alternating sections. The two routes agree. Omitting ``nonlinear`` (or passing ``None``) when updating an existing section leaves the declared process in place, passing a new one replaces it, and ``nonlinear=False`` removes it, so the section propagates linearly again. A pump must also be declared, see ``excitation`` in :data:`settings`, and the power-dependent result is read back with ``get('response')``. The process also carries ``z_samples`` (default: 100), the number of points at which the forward amplitudes are recorded along each slice of this section once the driven solve converges. Those reach the caller as ``get('response').power_vs_z(wavelength)``, which returns the pump or signal power against position from a single solve rather than one solve per length. Set it to 0 to skip the sampling. A pulse's nonlinearity is declared instead with a ``PulsedProcess``, see :ref:`pulsed nonlinear propagation <pulsed-propagation>`. Default: None
    :type nonlinear: SHGProcess or SFGProcess or DFGProcess or PulsedProcess or False or None
    :param settings: per-section overrides of the :data:`EME_settings` (notably ``overlap_variation`` and ``minimum_z_step``, which control the automatic z-slicing), default: None
    :type settings: dict or None
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: bend_section

    Define a circular bend for the EME solver: the cross-section of ``profile`` swept along an arc. The bend is placed in the layout like any other section, and sections declared after it continue from its end, turned by ``sweep_angle``.

    An anisotropic crystal is fixed in the chip, so the guide sees it turn along the bend. When a material is anisotropic in the plane of the chip (x-cut lithium niobate, for example), the bend is sliced along its heading and refined like a taper, and every section placed after a turn sees the crystal turned with it. A bend of an isotropic material, or of a crystal whose optic axis is vertical (z-cut thin film), is a single slice and a single mode solve. A :data:`copy_section` reuses its source's S-matrix, so it raises an error when its own placement would show the crystal differently, and asks for the copy to be declared as its own section.

    A bend has no mirror symmetry about x, so an x symmetry wall in the profile's ``boundary_condition`` (such as '0S' or 'SA') is replaced by '0' with a warning, and 'TE' and 'TM' keep only the vertical fold. In a circuit that also has straight sections, the x fold then applies to none of them (see :data:`EME`). Updating an existing bend changes only the arguments given.

    :param str name: section name, default: an auto-generated number
    :param str profile: name of the profile that defines the cross-section
    :param float radius: [nm] the bend radius, measured to the origin of the profile's x axis, must be positive, required for a new bend
    :param float sweep_angle: [rad] the angle the bend turns through, positive toward +x and negative toward -x, not zero, required for a new bend
    :param str method: how each slice is solved, either 'cylindrical' (the bend in cylindrical coordinates, as ``bend_radius`` in :data:`settings`) or 'TO' (transformation optics, see ``bend_method`` in :data:`settings`), default: 'cylindrical'
    :param ports: replace the section's default ``[Port('left', None, 'left'), Port('right', None, 'right')]`` on a per-side basis, where a supplied port replaces every existing port on the same side, and multiple ports may share a side. See :class:`Port`, default: None (keep existing/default ports)
    :type ports: list[Port] or None
    :param settings: per-section overrides of the :data:`EME_settings` (notably ``overlap_variation`` and ``minimum_z_step``, which control the automatic z-slicing), default: None
    :type settings: dict or None
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: gds_section

    Define a section whose cross-section varies along z according to a mask imported from a GDS file, for more complex geometries defined with third-party layout tools.

    :param str name: section name, default: an auto-generated number
    :param str profile: name of the profile that defines the section's cross-section outside of the GDS mask
    :param str gds_path: path to the GDS file used to mask the section
    :param layer_map: mapping of profile shape names to GDS layer numbers, used to determine which shapes in ``profile`` are masked by which GDS layer
    :type layer_map: dict[str, int]
    :param float length: [nm] the length of the section, default: derived from the GDS bounding box
    :param cell_index: the cell index (or name) in the specified GDS file, default: 0
    :type cell_index: int or str
    :param float scale: unit scale factor applied to the GDS coordinates (e.g. use 1000 if the GDS file is drawn in microns but the simulation is in nanometers), default: 1
    :param port_poses: explicit port positions/orientations at the section boundaries, default: derived from the GDS bounding box (left port at w=0, right port at w=length)
    :type port_poses: dict
    :param bool heal: whether to heal small gaps/self-intersections in the imported GDS polygons before meshing, default: True
    :param float grow: amount to grow imported GDS polygons by, to close small gaps, default: 1e-3
    :param nonlinear: declare a pulse's nonlinearity on this section as a ``PulsedProcess`` (see :ref:`pulsed nonlinear propagation <pulsed-propagation>`), ``False`` to remove one. The CW :math:`\chi^{(2)}` processes are not available on a GDS section. Default: None
    :type nonlinear: PulsedProcess or False or None
    :param ports: replace the section's default ``[Port('left', None, 'left'), Port('right', None, 'right')]`` on a per-side basis, where a supplied port replaces every existing port on the same side, and multiple ports may share a side. See :class:`Port`, default: None (keep existing/default ports)
    :type ports: list[Port] or None
    :param settings: per-section overrides of the :data:`EME_settings`, default: None
    :type settings: dict or None
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. note::
    Once sections are declared, call ``plot()`` with ``plane='z-x'`` or ``plane='z-y'`` to preview a geometry-only 'Outline' of the section layout before running :data:`EME`.

.. data:: copy_section

    Place a second instance of an already-declared section in the chain, reusing its already-computed S-matrix instead of re-solving it.

    :param str name: section name, default: an auto-generated number
    :param str section_name: name of the existing section to copy
    :param bool mirror: whether to reverse the placement along the propagation direction (swapping the left/right ports), default: False
    :param port_swap: explicit port-name mapping to use instead of the automatically computed left/right swap when ``mirror`` is True, default: None
    :type port_swap: dict
    :param ports: relabel/window this copy's own left/right boundary, with the same semantics as any other section's ``ports``, independent of ``port_swap`` and of the source section's own ports. See :class:`Port`, default: None (keep existing/default ports)
    :type ports: list[Port] or None
    :param settings: per-section overrides of the :data:`EME_settings`, default: None
    :type settings: dict or None
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: connect_ports

    Override the default left/right adjacency wiring between named ports declared with the ``ports`` argument of any section function.

    Connecting two ports also **pins their coordinate systems together**: the two ports' origins (the horizontal center and bottom edge of each cross-section) are made to coincide, so the connection is what positions one section relative to the other. Use :class:`Port`'s ``offset`` to displace a section off that shared origin, and its ``window`` to choose which part of a wider cross-section the port exposes. The first section you declare defines the global frame that plots are drawn in.

    :param pairs: a list of ``('<section_name>.<port_name>', '<section_name>.<port_name>')`` pairs to connect, e.g. ``[('a.right', 'b.left'), ('c.right', 'd.left')]``. A port can only have one connection, so declaring a new connection for a port that already had one supersedes it. Names are resolved against the actual declared sections/ports at :data:`EME` build time. An entry may carry an optional **third** element, a :class:`JunctionOverride`, configuring the junction that connection forms, e.g. ``[('a.right', 'b.left', JunctionOverride(junction_normalization=False))]``.
    :type pairs: list[tuple[str, str]] or list[tuple[str, str, JunctionOverride]]
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. class:: JunctionOverride

    Settings for a single junction, passed as the optional third element of a :data:`connect_ports` entry. Every parameter left unspecified inherits the value the junction's sections resolved, so setting one does not disturb the others.

    These settings belong to the *connection* rather than to either port because each one describes the interface between the two sections, not one side of it: which algebra joins their mode sets and how the resulting scattering matrix is normalized.

    Only an explicitly connected junction can carry these. A junction formed by the default left/right adjacency has nowhere to declare them, so name that pair in :data:`connect_ports` to configure it, which supersedes the adjacency. The internal junctions of a taper or GDS section's automatic z-slicing are controlled by that section's ``settings`` instead.

    :param junction_normalization: how this junction's scattering matrix is power-normalized, one of True (full SVD unitarization), False (raw, unnormalized), or 'gain' (clip singular values at 1 while keeping the raw lossy mode-matching), for a junction with a plane-wave side or an angled facet, default: None (inherit)
    :type junction_normalization: bool or str or None

.. data:: EME

    Calculate the complete scattering matrix of all defined sections using the eigenmode expansion method (EME). Before solving anything it checks the layout (see :data:`check_layout`) and raises an error when two sections overlap or a loop of connected sections misses closing (its two ports more than ``minimum_z_step`` apart, or more than 1e-6 rad from facing each other), and warns when a section's outline crosses itself or a section is reached by no connection.

    A ``boundary_condition`` of 'TE', 'TM', 'TE-h', 'TE-v', 'TM-h' or 'TM-v' folds a cross-section only about a middle it is mirror symmetric about (see :data:`settings`). In a circuit, a fold applies only when every section is symmetric about it, because a folded section has no modes of the other parity, and where it meets an unfolded section the power those modes would carry is lost. When some sections fold about a middle and others cannot, ``EME()`` warns and solves the circuit again with that fold taken out of every section. Set a boundary condition without it (for example 'TE-v' instead of 'TE' for a circuit with offset or bent guides) to solve once.

    :param bool warm_start: whether to seed each taper/gds section's automatic z-slice refinement from the previously solved chain (when available), instead of re-refining from scratch, default: False
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: check_layout

    Check the layout of the declared sections without solving. Every section is placed where its connections put it and drawn top down from its shapes that do not span the window. Returns a ``LayoutReport`` with ``overlaps`` (pairs of sections whose outlines overlap, as ``(section, section, area)`` with the area in nm\ :sup:`2`, where sections that only share a port edge do not overlap), ``self_intersecting`` (sections whose own outline crosses itself, such as a bend swept past a full turn), ``closures`` (for each connection that closes a loop, how far apart its two ports are in nm and how far from facing each other in radians), and ``unplaced`` (sections no connection reaches, which are placed after the section declared before them). ``max_closure()`` returns the largest closure distance and angle, or zeros without a loop. ``plot(view='layout')`` draws the same layout. ``LayoutReport`` is defined in ``emodeconnection``.

    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: chi2_spectrum

    Conversion spectrum of a :math:`\chi^{(2)}` section, solved sparsely in wavelength (EMode\ :sup:`3D`\  only). Returns the signal power out over the pump power in at every wavelength in ``values``.

    A nonlinear spectrum oscillates with the phase mismatch, so it cannot be interpolated. At any useful resolution it has to be evaluated point by point. What *can* be interpolated is what the coupled-mode equations consume: the coupling and the propagation constants, which vary smoothly with wavelength. So the modes are solved at a handful of wavelengths chosen by how fast the mode list is actually moving, and the response is then evaluated at every requested wavelength from interpolated coupling. Against a directly solved 13-point spectrum across a phase-matching peak, five solves reproduce every point to four decimals, sidelobes included.

    Quasi-phase matching is included: the grating enters as a wavevector shift and a Fourier coefficient built from ``poling_period``, ``duty_cycle`` and ``qpm_order``, none of which depend on wavelength, so a poled section keeps its exact grating while its phase mismatch moves with the interpolated propagation constants.

    Requires a chain with a declared :math:`\chi^{(2)}` section (see ``nonlinear`` on :data:`straight_section`/:data:`taper_section`) and a declared pump (``excitation`` in :data:`settings`).

    :param values: pump wavelengths [nm] to report at (the signal wavelength follows from the declared process)
    :type values: list or array
    :param str section: which nonlinear section to scan, default: the only one declared
    :param float tolerance: the largest mode-list change tolerated between adjacent solves, default: 1e-3
    :param float minimum_step: [nm] the smallest wavelength gap the sampler will bisect into, default: the output spacing, since resolving finer than you asked to see cannot change the reported curve
    :param int initial_points: solves to place before any bisection, default: 5
    :param float power: [W] pump power, default: the declared excitation's
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

    Returns a dictionary with ``values``, ``conversion`` (signal out over pump in), ``solved_wavelengths`` (where the solver actually ran), and ``unconverged`` (the intervals, if any, that the sampler could not resolve to ``tolerance`` before reaching ``minimum_step``).

.. data:: free_space_field

    Declare, or update, a free-space field: a Gaussian beam, or a combination of the port's own modes, launched into a port of the chain. This is an *excitation*, not a section. It does not appear in the scattering matrix or in the layout.

    After :data:`EME`, ``plot(excitation=name)`` (or the plot window's Mode menu, ``'<name> (free space)'``) renders the field the beam launches, projected onto the target port's modes with the same pairing the junctions use. Re-declaring an existing ``name`` updates only the arguments you give.

    :param str name: free-space field name, default: the next number
    :param str port: the external port the beam enters, either a bare side ``'left'`` (default) or ``'right'``, or a qualified ``'<section>.<port>'`` name. The beam travels inbound from that port.
    :param waist: [nm] the 1/e field radius :math:`w_0` in :math:`\exp(-r^2/w_0^2)` at the beam's waist, required when declaring a new Gaussian beam. A pair ``(w_x, w_y)`` declares an elliptical beam, :math:`\exp(-x^2/w_x^2 - y^2/w_y^2)` at its waist
    :type waist: float or tuple[float, float]
    :param center: [nm] beam center ``(x, y)`` in the port's cross-section coordinates, default: (0, 0)
    :type center: tuple[float, float]
    :param tilt: [degrees] ``(theta_x, theta_y)``, where a positive ``theta_x`` steers the beam toward +x. This is the angle **inside the medium the beam travels through**, default: (0, 0)
    :type tilt: tuple[float, float]
    :param str component: the one transverse E component the beam carries, ``'Ex'`` (default) or ``'Ey'``
    :param float amplitude: peak field value at the waist, default: 1
    :param float wavelength: [nm], default: None (each port's own wavelength)
    :param waist_position: [nm] the distance from the port to the beam's waist, along the direction the beam travels. A positive value focuses the beam inside the chain, a negative one puts the waist behind the port (a diverging beam). The launched beam carries the wavefront curvature and Gouy phase of that distance, with the Rayleigh range :math:`z_R = \pi n w_0^2/\lambda` of the port's background index :math:`n`. A pair ``(z_x, z_y)`` puts the waist along x and along y at different distances (an astigmatic beam). With a pair in ``waist`` or ``waist_position``, each axis has its own Rayleigh range, wavefront curvature and half of the Gouy phase, and the beam's power does not depend on either distance. Default: 0 (the waist on the port)
    :type waist_position: float or tuple[float, float]
    :param float phase: [radians] global phase of the launched field, default: 0
    :param modes: launch a combination of the target port's own modes instead of a beam: their indices. Giving a beam's ``name`` a list of ``modes`` (or a mode combination's ``name`` a ``waist``) replaces it with the other kind
    :type modes: list[int]
    :param powers: one power per entry of ``modes``, default: 1 each. Each mode is launched with the amplitude :math:`\sqrt{P}\,e^{j\phi}`, as a ``Source`` is
    :type powers: list[float]
    :param phases: [radians] one phase per entry of ``modes``, default: 0 each
    :type phases: list[float]
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: free_space_field_diagnostics

    How much of a declared free-space field's power the target port's modal basis actually captures, after :data:`EME` has solved the chain. The solver already warns when this falls below 90%. This returns it as a value a script can check or plot instead of parsing a log line.

    A low captured fraction means the port's modes cannot represent the beam. Raise that section's ``num_modes``, or widen its window, before trusting a coupling number computed from it.

    :param str name: the free-space field to diagnose
    :param float wavelength: [nm] which of a multi-wavelength chain's ports to diagnose, default: None (the lowest wavelength present)
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

    Returns a ``FreeSpaceProjection`` with ``captured_fraction``, its complement ``dropped_fraction``, the resolved ``port`` and ``wavelength``, and the launch basis's ``num_modes``.

.. data:: plot_S_matrix

    Colormap plot of the transmission or reflection component of the EME scattering matrix.

    :param input: input field (first number of the scattering matrix identifier), default: 0
    :type input: int or str
    :param output: output field (second number of the scattering matrix identifier), default: 1
    :type output: int or str
    :param plot_function: specify the function to apply to the plot data ('abs^2', 'angle', 'real', 'imag'), default: 'abs^2'
    :type plot_function: str or None
    :param str file_name: if specified, forces the function to save a file with the given parameters and will not display the interactive plot, file is saved under a directory called EM_figures, default: None
    :param str file_type: file type for saving a plot, ‘pdf’ or ‘png’, default: '' (no extension is added to ``file_name`` unless a file type is given)
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. _monitors:

Monitors
^^^^^^^^

A monitor is a plane inside the chain on which the solved field is sampled after :data:`EME`. It is output only: it is not a port, does not enter the scattering matrix and does not change the solve, so monitors can be added, moved or removed without solving again. The plane runs across the full window in x and is tilted about x, so it can sample the light a grating coupler radiates upward. :data:`monitor_field` returns the field on it, and :data:`monitor_coupling` its coupling to a tilted Gaussian beam, such as the mode of a fiber above a grating. ``plot()`` draws each monitor's plane on the 'z-y' panel, and ``sweep(result='monitor_coupling')`` sweeps the coupling (see :data:`sweep`). The 'EME: Grating Coupler' example uses all three.

.. data:: monitor

    Declare a monitor. Declaring the same name again replaces it.

    :param str name: the monitor's name
    :param float w: [nm] the position along the chain, from its left port, that the plane passes through
    :param float y: [nm] the height that the plane passes through at ``w``. An untilted plane must lie inside the window, between 0 and ``window_height``
    :param float angle: [degrees] the tilt of the plane about x from horizontal, strictly between -90 and 90, where a positive angle tips the far end of the plane up, default: 0
    :param length: [nm] the extent along the plane, centered on (``w``, ``y``), default: None (as far as the chain and the window allow)
    :type length: float or None
    :param resolution: [nm] the sampling step along the plane, default: None (the window's ``x_resolution``)
    :type resolution: float or None
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

.. data:: monitor_field

    The field on a monitor's plane after :data:`EME`, for 1 W launched in one mode of one port.

    :param str name: the monitor's name
    :param str port: the external port the chain is excited from, default: 'left'
    :param int mode: the launched mode, default: 0
    :param wavelength: [nm] which of a multi-wavelength chain's wavelengths to use, the nearest one present, default: None (the chain's first)
    :type wavelength: float or None
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

    Returns a ``PlaneField`` with ``fields``, a dictionary of the six components ('Ex', 'Ey', 'Ez', 'Hx', 'Hy', 'Hz') on the plane, each a complex array of shape (len(x), len(s)), where ``x`` [nm] runs across the plane and ``s`` [nm] along it, at chain positions ``w`` and heights ``y`` [nm]. ``Sn`` is the time-averaged Poynting flux through the plane (positive along its upward normal), ``power_through_plane`` [W] its integral, and ``power_in`` the 1 W launched, so ``power_through_plane`` is also the fraction of the launched power that crosses the plane.

.. data:: monitor_coupling

    The coupling between a launched waveguide mode and a Gaussian beam through a monitor's plane, after :data:`EME`. It is the fraction of the launched power crossing the plane times the normalized overlap of the field's ``polarization`` component with the beam. By reciprocity the same number is the coupling from the beam into the launched mode, which is the figure a grating coupler is designed for. Only the overlap is computed, so trying other beams costs no solve.

    :param str name: the monitor's name
    :param float mode_field_diameter: [nm] the beam's mode field diameter, for example 10.4e3 for SMF-28 at 1550 nm
    :param float angle: [degrees] the beam's angle from the plane's normal, positive toward +s (along the chain), default: 0
    :param center: [nm] the beam's center (x, s) on the plane, default: None (centered on the plane)
    :type center: tuple[float, float] or None
    :param index: the refractive index of the medium the beam travels in, default: None (the profile's background material)
    :type index: float or None
    :param str polarization: the field component the beam couples to, 'x', 'y', or 's' (along the plane), default: 'x'
    :param str port: the launching port, default: 'left'
    :param int mode: the launched mode, default: 0
    :param wavelength: [nm] which of a multi-wavelength chain's wavelengths to use, default: None (the chain's first)
    :type wavelength: float or None
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

    Returns a ``BeamCoupling`` with ``coupling``, its two factors ``power_fraction`` and ``overlap``, and the beam it was computed for (``mode_field_diameter``, ``center``, ``angle``, ``index``, ``polarization``) at ``wavelength``.

.. _pulsed-propagation:

Pulsed nonlinear propagation
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

A femtosecond pulse is declared as the excitation, ``settings(excitation=PulsedSource(...))``, and a section's nonlinearity with ``nonlinear=PulsedProcess(...)`` on :data:`straight_section`, :data:`taper_section` or :data:`gds_section` (EMode\ :sup:`3D`\  only). :data:`EME` refines the chain at the pulse's center wavelength, solves each distinct cross-section at ``dispersion_samples`` wavelengths across the pulse's band, and propagates the pulse forward through every slice and junction with :math:`\chi^{(2)}`, Kerr (:math:`\chi^{(3)}`), Raman and two-photon absorption. Reflections and power scattered into modes that are not tracked are discarded and reported, with a warning where that is not safe. The classes below are imported from ``emodeconnection``.

The nonlinear coefficients come from the materials: :math:`\chi^{(2)}` from the material's :math:`d` tensor, :math:`\chi^{(3)}` from its nonlinear index :math:`n_2` as :math:`\chi^{(3)} = \tfrac{4}{3}\varepsilon_0 c n^2 n_2`, the Raman response from the material that holds most of the Kerr overlap, and two-photon absorption from its coefficient :math:`\beta_\mathrm{TPA}`, active only for photon pairs above the material's bandgap. In the material database, ``SiO2``, ``SiN``, ``LN`` and ``LN_MgO`` carry :math:`n_2`, ``SiO2`` (Blow and Wood) and ``LN``/``LN_MgO`` (four A\ :sub:`1`\ (TO) lines, Bache and Schiek) a Raman response, and ``Si``, ``AlGaAs``, ``LN`` and ``LN_MgO`` a two-photon coefficient, each with its reference. A material of your own takes the same through ``MaterialProperties(n=..., n2=..., raman=(fraction, [(weight, position, half_width), ...]), tpa=..., bandgap=...)``, with :math:`n_2` in m\ :sup:`2`/W, the Raman line positions and half widths in cm\ :sup:`-1`, :math:`\beta_\mathrm{TPA}` in m/W and the bandgap in eV. ``PulsedProcess(chi3=True)`` raises an error naming a material that has no :math:`n_2` (silicon, for one).

.. class:: PulsedSource

    A pulse launched into one port of the circuit, for ``settings(excitation=...)``.

    :param float center_wavelength: [nm] the carrier wavelength, inside ``wavelength_range``
    :param float duration: [fs] the intensity FWHM, required except for ``shape='cw'`` and ``shape='measured'``
    :param float energy: [pJ] the pulse energy, give exactly one of ``energy`` and ``peak_power`` (a measured pulse is scaled to either, as an analytic one is)
    :param float peak_power: [W] the peak power
    :param str port: the launch port, default: 'left'
    :param mode: the tracked mode that carries the pulse, or a dictionary ``{mode: amplitude}`` of complex amplitudes that splits it between tracked modes (normalized, so only their ratios matter), default: 0
    :type mode: int or dict
    :param str shape: 'sech', 'gaussian', 'cw' (a continuous wave of ``peak_power`` at ``center_wavelength``, with no ``duration`` or ``energy``), or 'measured' (the pulse of ``measurement``, with no ``duration`` or ``chirp``), default: 'sech'
    :param float chirp: the chirp :math:`C` of :math:`\exp(j C t^2 / 2 T_0^2)`, where a positive value raises the instantaneous frequency across the pulse, default: 0
    :param measurement: a measured pulse for ``shape='measured'``, see :class:`PulseMeasurement`. A measured spectrum is launched at its own wavelengths, and ``center_wavelength`` stays the wavelength at which the circuit is refined. A measured temporal trace is centered on ``center_wavelength``. Default: None
    :type measurement: PulseMeasurement or None
    :param float repetition_rate: [Hz] for average powers, default: None
    :param wavelength_range: [nm] the span of the frequency grid, default: (450, 3500)
    :type wavelength_range: tuple[float, float]
    :param int num_points: frequency points, even and at least 16, which with ``wavelength_range`` set the time window (the number of points over the frequency span, 28 ps at the defaults), default: 16384
    :param int alias: oversampling of the real-field products, 1, 2 or 3 (2 suffices for :math:`\chi^{(2)}`, 3 for :math:`\chi^{(3)}`), default: 2

.. class:: PulseMeasurement

    A measured pulse, for ``PulsedSource(shape='measured', measurement=...)``: a sampled spectrum (as from a spectrometer, often with a phase retrieved by FROG or SPIDER) or a sampled temporal trace. Give exactly one of ``wavelength`` and ``time``.

    The samples are never launched as they are. :data:`settings` fits them first, so noise and sparse sampling do not reach the propagation, and refuses the source with an error when the fit is not good enough. The fit's quality is 1 minus its normalized residual: the :math:`R^2` of the intensity, less the intensity-weighted mean of :math:`1 - \cos` of the phase error when a phase is given. Below ``min_fit_quality`` the error states the quality reached, the model and where the residual is largest, so you can choose another model, clean the data, or lower ``min_fit_quality`` knowingly. The accepted pulse is resampled onto the frequency grid, centered in the time window and scaled to the source's ``energy`` or ``peak_power``. The fit is reported on the result as ``get('pulse_response').measured_fit``, with its ``model``, ``quality``, ``fwhm`` [fs], ``center_wavelength`` [nm], ``gdd`` [fs\ :sup:`2`], ``tod`` [fs\ :sup:`3`], ``chirp`` (for 'sech' and 'gaussian'), ``transform_limited``, ``energy_outside`` (the fraction of the energy cut by the window), ``residual_peak`` and ``background`` (the constant background subtracted, as a fraction of the samples' peak).

    Data that stops while the pulse is still bright (above 5 % of its peak), or whose pulse lies mostly outside the source's ``wavelength_range``, is refused. A spectrometer's dark counts or stray light put a constant background under the whole trace, which reads as a pulse that never reaches zero: give ``background`` to subtract it before the fit and this check. Data that reaches past ``wavelength_range`` (or past the time window) is cut with a smooth window, with a warning giving the fraction of the energy outside.

    :param wavelength: [nm] the wavelengths of a measured spectrum
    :type wavelength: list[float] or numpy array or None
    :param time: [fs] the times of a measured temporal trace
    :type time: list[float] or numpy array or None
    :param intensity: the intensity at each sample, on any scale. A spectrum's intensity is per unit wavelength, as a spectrometer records it.
    :type intensity: list[float] or numpy array
    :param phase: [rad] the retrieved spectral or temporal phase at each sample, in the convention of FROG and SPIDER retrievals: the group delay is :math:`d\varphi/d\omega`, so a positive quadratic spectral phase is a positive group delay dispersion, and the instantaneous angular frequency is :math:`\omega_0 - d\varphi/dt`. Without a phase the pulse is taken as transform limited, with a warning. Default: None
    :type phase: list[float] or numpy array or None
    :param str fit: the model fitted to the samples: 'smooth' (a smoothing spline of the intensity, with a polynomial phase of order 2 to 4 chosen by the fit, or a smoothing spline of the phase weighted by the intensity when no polynomial reaches ``min_fit_quality``, as for a pulse shaper's output or a pulse broadened by self-phase modulation), 'sech' or 'gaussian' (the analytic shapes of :class:`PulsedSource`, fitted for width, center and chirp), default: 'smooth'
    :param float min_fit_quality: the lowest fit quality accepted, in [0, 1], default: 0.99
    :param background: a constant background subtracted from ``intensity`` before the fit, on the same scale as ``intensity`` (per unit wavelength for a spectrum), at least 0 and below the samples' peak. 'auto' takes it as the mean of the outer 5 % of the samples at each end, and refuses the measurement when those ends slope or sit at different levels (by more than 1 % of the peak, or four times their noise), since they are then the pulse's wings rather than a background. None subtracts nothing. Default: None
    :type background: float or 'auto' or None

.. class:: PulsedProcess

    The nonlinear optics of one section for a pulsed simulation, for a section's ``nonlinear=``.

    :param bool chi2: include :math:`\chi^{(2)}`, default: True
    :param bool chi3: include the Kerr effect, default: True
    :param bool raman: include the delayed Raman part of the Kerr response, default: True
    :param str raman_mode: 'dominant' (the response of the strongest field pattern, fast) or 'full', default: 'dominant'
    :param tpa: two-photon absorption on (True), off (False), or on wherever a material has a coefficient (None), default: None
    :type tpa: bool or None
    :param modes: the tracked mode indices at the center wavelength, default: None (the source's mode or modes)
    :type modes: list[int] or None
    :param poling: the section's domain pattern, default: None (unpoled)
    :type poling: Poling or None
    :param int dispersion_samples: wavelengths at which each cross-section is solved, Chebyshev nodes over the source's ``wavelength_range``, at least 4, default: 24
    :param float pattern_threshold: singular value, relative to the first, below which field patterns are dropped, in [0, 1), default: 1e-3
    :param int max_rank: the largest number of field patterns, default: 12

.. class:: Poling

    The domain pattern of a poled section. Give exactly one of ``period``, ``z_knots`` with ``periods``, ``domain_walls``, and ``domain_lengths``.

    :param float period: [nm] a constant poling period
    :param z_knots: [nm] positions along the section at which ``periods`` are given, interpolated between them (a chirp), at least 2
    :type z_knots: list[float]
    :param periods: [nm] the local period at each knot
    :type periods: list[float]
    :param domain_walls: [nm] explicit domain wall positions along the section, strictly increasing
    :type domain_walls: list[float]
    :param domain_lengths: [nm] the length of every domain in order, each > 0, the signs alternating from the first. The walls are the running sum: a wall at or past the end of the section is dropped, and when the domains end before the section does, the sign flips once more and the last domain runs to the end. This is the form :data:`optimize` varies, every domain on its own
    :type domain_lengths: list[float]
    :param float duty_cycle: the fraction of each period in the first domain, default: 0.5
    :param str interpolation: 'linear' or 'spline' between the knots, default: 'linear'
    :param bool inverted_first: start with an inverted domain, default: False
    :param float jitter_rms: [nm] rms of a Gaussian random displacement of every wall, for fabrication tolerance studies, default: 0
    :param int seed: the seed of the jitter, default: None

    ``walls(section_length)`` returns the domain walls [nm] of any form over a section of that length, and ``to_domain_lengths(section_length)`` the length of every domain, which sum to the section length, so a design can start from a fixed or chirped poling.

.. class:: PulseResponse

    Returned by ``get('pulse_response')`` after :data:`EME` or :data:`pulse_propagate`. ``spectrum`` is (records, modes, points), the root-energy spectrum of every tracked mode in :math:`\sqrt{\mathrm{J/Hz}}` on ``frequency`` [Hz], with ``wavelength`` [nm] the same axis, ``z`` [nm] the record positions and ``energy`` [pJ] per record and mode. ``junction_loss`` is, per junction, the fraction of the arriving energy that left the tracked modes there, and ``rank_per_slice`` and ``samples_per_slice`` report the field patterns and mode solves of each slice. ``window_gap`` is, per record, the longest stretch of the time window (as a fraction of it) that holds almost none of the energy of all the tracked modes together. The window is periodic, so below about 0.05 the pulse's leading and trailing parts have met around it and wrapped onto each other, and ``num_points`` should grow (the solver warns). It does not depend on the comoving frame. ``edge_energy`` is, per record, the fraction of the energy in the outer 5 % of the time window around the comoving frame (the first tracked mode's group delay), which says where the pulse sits relative to that frame, not whether it wraps. ``domain_walls`` [nm] the positions along the chain of the domain walls the run used (jitter included), and ``steps`` and ``rejected_steps`` count the propagation steps. For a measured source, ``measured_fit`` is the fit that was launched (see :class:`PulseMeasurement`), and None otherwise.

    ``band_energy(wavelength_min, wavelength_max, z=None, mode=None)`` returns the energy [pJ] in a band at the record nearest ``z`` (default: the output), summed over the tracked modes unless ``mode`` is given. ``band_power(...)`` returns the average power [W] of a pulse train, with ``repetition_rate`` taken from the source unless given. ``psd(z, mode)`` returns the spectral density in dB relative to 1 pJ/nm, ``envelope(z, mode)`` the time [fs] and complex envelope [:math:`\sqrt{\mathrm{W}}`], ``smallest_window_gap()`` the smallest ``window_gap`` at any record (None for a response saved before it was reported), and ``energy_outside_window()`` the largest ``edge_energy``.

.. data:: pulse_propagate

    Propagate the pulse again through the chain the last :data:`EME` prepared, without any mode solve (EMode\ :sup:`3D`\  only). Use it to try another poling, for example a chirp or fabrication jitter on the domain walls, at the cost of the propagation alone.

    :param poling: a new domain pattern for every section with a ``PulsedProcess`` (a single ``Poling``), or for the named sections (a dictionary of section name to ``Poling``), default: None (keep the declared poling)
    :type poling: Poling or dict or None
    :param int records: number of evenly spaced positions along the chain at which the spectrum is recorded, default: 100
    :param float local_error: relative error allowed per propagation step, default: 1e-6
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'

    The prepared chain lives for the session. After ``open()`` of a saved file, run :data:`EME` again first. The result is read back with ``get('pulse_response')``.



Multi-Physics
-------------

.. data:: FEM

    Calculate the waveguide modes with the full-vector finite-element method. Requires a '3D' license. The cross-section is meshed with triangles that follow every material interface, and the mesh is refined where the modes are under-resolved, as set by the ``fem_*`` settings in ``settings()``. The saved fields, effective indices, losses and TE fractions are the same quantities, with the same normalization, as described under ``FDM()``, so ``get()``, ``get_fields()``, ``report()``, ``plot()`` and ``EME()`` work the same way. Calling ``FEM()`` sets the profile's ``solver`` setting to 'FEM'.

    All ``boundary_condition`` values, PMLs, expansion regions, bends, lossy and anisotropic materials (including crystals tilted out of the cross-section with ``theta``), and ``heat()`` and ``electrostatic()`` perturbations are supported. A symmetric or antisymmetric boundary on an axis whose mirror a crystal's orientation breaks raises an error, since it would describe a different structure. Field plots sample the FEM solution at ``x_resolution`` and ``y_resolution``, and ``plot(mesh_display=True)`` shows the triangle mesh.

    :param profile: profile name to save the solved profile under, default: '_default'
    :type profile: str or int
    :param str section: name of an EME section to solve a slice from, instead of the profile's own settings/shapes, default: None
    :param float propagation_distance: [nm] where along ``section`` to take the cross-section, default: None
    :param bool include_heat: whether to include the temperature change from the most recent ``heat()`` solve, default: True
    :param bool include_static: whether to apply the electro-optic (Pockels) permittivity perturbation from the most recent ``electrostatic()`` solve, default: True
    :param bool verbose: print progress, default: True
    :param str simulation_name: simulation name, default: 'emode'
    :return: a dict with ``field`` (a Field object), ``n_eff_tilde``, ``TE_fraction``, ``TE_indices``, ``TM_indices``, ``PML_indices``, ``mesh`` (``vertices``, ``triangles`` and ``region``, the triangle mesh solved on), and ``refinement`` (``n_eff_history``, ``num_dofs`` and ``num_elements`` per refinement level, and ``stopped_by``, the rule that ended refinement). For a multi-wavelength profile, a ``WavelengthDict`` of these dicts, one per wavelength, indexable like a ``dict[float, dict]``.

.. data:: heat

    Run a steady-state thermal simulation of a waveguide cross-section. Requires a '3D' license.

    .. note::
        Each ``shape()`` now accepts an input parameter called ``heat_only`` (default: False), which can be used to set additional shapes on top or bottom of the photonic layer stack. For example, common ``heat_only`` shapes are the substrate and metal heater layers.

        Each ``shape()`` also now accepts an input parameter called ``fem_resolution`` (default: 500), which is used to refine the triangular mesh within certain shapes.

        Every material carries ``thermal_conductivity`` (W/m·K), ``resistivity`` (Ohm·nm), ``dn_dT`` (1/K), and ``eps_r_dc``. The defaults are ``1e-10``, infinity, ``0``, and ``1.0`` where no reliable published value has been entered. ``dn_dT`` and ``eps_r_dc`` are one value for every axis or three for the crystal's x, y and z axes, and each principal index shifts by its own ``dn_dT``. The mesh covers the shapes, so a region the shapes enclose without covering takes the background material's properties. See the :doc:`Material Database </emodeguide/materials>` page for values and sources.

    :param float min_angle: Minimum angle for triangular mesh. Smaller values result in a finer mesh, but can prevent the meshing algorithm from converging. Default: 30.
    :param float boundary_temperature: Fixed temperature boundary condition in 'K' set along each perimeter indicated by ``boundaries``. Default: 298.
    :param list[str] boundaries:  'top', 'bottom', 'left', or 'right'. Indicates which boundaries are set to the fixed temperature ``boundary_temperature``. Default: ['bottom'].
    :param bool verbose: Control the display of the progress bar. Default: True.
    :param str simulation_name: Simulation name. Default: 'emode'.
    :return: A dictionary/struct with the mesh points (``p``), mesh triangles (``t``), ``temperature``, ``thermal_conductivity``, and ``heat_generation`` arrays. It also includes the ``boundary_temperature`` and ``boundaries`` settings.

.. data:: electrostatic

    Run a steady-state electrostatic simulation of a waveguide cross-section. Requires a '3D' license.

    .. note::
        Each ``shape()`` also now accepts an input parameter called ``voltage`` (default: None), which is set to create electric field sources. Shapes with ``voltage`` left as None do not get a voltage boundary condition applied.

        Each ``shape()`` also now accepts an input parameter called ``fem_resolution`` (default: 500), which is used to refine the triangular mesh within certain shapes.

        Each material in the EMode material database now has ``eps_r_dc`` (relative permittivity at ~1 kHz), one value or three for the crystal's x, y and z axes. The solve uses the in-plane (x, y) block of each material's turned ``eps_r_dc`` tensor.

        The DC field derived here perturbs the permittivity through each material's linear electro-optic (Pockels) tensor ``r`` (``get('<material>')['r']``, m/V): :math:`\Delta(1/n^2)_{ij} = \sum_k r_{ijk} E_k`, then :math:`\Delta\varepsilon = -\varepsilon \cdot \Delta(1/n^2) \cdot \varepsilon`. ``FDM()`` applies this automatically on the next solve (``include_static=False`` to skip it), the same way ``heat()``'s temperature field perturbs the permittivity through ``dn_dT``.

    :param float min_angle: Minimum angle for triangular mesh. Smaller values result in a finer mesh, but can prevent the meshing algorithm from converging. Default: 30.
    :param bool verbose: Control the display of the progress bar. Default: True.
    :param str simulation_name: Simulation name. Default: 'emode'.
    :return: A dictionary/struct with the mesh points (``p``), mesh triangles (``t``), ``voltage``, ``eps_dc_grid`` (the in-plane DC permittivity of each element, shape (2, 2, number of elements)), the per-element electric field (``Ex``, ``Ey``, in V/nm), and ``centroids`` (element centers, in the optical window's frame).



Material Database
-----------------

Descriptions of all materials available in built-in material database. This information is also accessible from ``refractive_index`` and ``material_explorer``. Unless specified otherwise, all materials have :math:`\mu = 1.0`. Each equation for the refractive index assumes that the wavelength :math:`\lambda` has units of :math:`\mu\mathrm{m}`.

.. data:: Air
    
    .. math:: n = \left(1 + \frac{5.79211 \times 10^{-2}}{238.019 - \lambda^{-2}} + \frac{1.67917 \times 10^{-3}}{57.3620 - \lambda^{-2}}\right)
    
    Wavelength range: 200 nm to 2000 nm
    
        | P. E. Ciddor, "Refractive index of air: new equations for the visible and near infrared," Appl. Opt. 35, 1566 (1996).

.. data:: Al

    .. math:: n = 1.5355 + 15.331i

    Wavelength range: 1000 nm to 2000 nm

        | A. D. Rakic, A. B. Djurisic, J. M. Elazar, and M. L. Majewski, "Optical properties of metallic films for vertical-cavity optoelectronic devices," Appl. Opt. 37, 5271 (1998).
        | Notes: Lorentz-Drude model evaluated at 1550 nm. Constant near 1550 nm only.

.. data:: Al2O3
    
    .. math:: n = \left( 1 + \frac{1.43135}{1 - (7.26631 \times 10^{-2}/ \lambda)^2} + \frac{0.650547}{1 - (0.119324/ \lambda)^2} + \frac{5.34140}{1 - (18.0283/ \lambda)^2} \right)^{0.5}
    
    Wavelength range: 200 nm to 5000 nm
    
        | (1) I. H. Malitson and M. J. Dodge, "Refractive Index and Birefringence of Synthetic Sapphire," J. Opt. Soc. Am. 62, 1405 (1972).
        | (2) M. J. Dodge, "Refractive Index" in Handbook of Laser Science and Technology, Volume IV, Optical Materials: Part 2, CRC Press, Boca Raton, 1986, p. 30.

.. data:: AlGaAs
    
    .. math::
        
        \mathrm{Al}_x &\mathrm{Ga}_{1-x}\mathrm{As} \\\ \\
        E_0 &= 3.65 + 0.871 x + 0.179 x^2 \\
        E_\mathrm{d} &= 36.1 - 2.45 x \\
        E_\Gamma &= 1.424 + 1.266 x + 0.26 x^2 \\
        E_\mathrm{f} &= (2 E_0^2 - E_\Gamma^2)^{0.5} \\
        \eta &= \pi E_\mathrm{d}/(2 E_0^3 (E_0^2 - E_\Gamma^2)) \\
        M_1 &= \frac{\eta}{2 \pi} (E_\mathrm{f}^4 - E_\Gamma^4) \\
        M_3 &= \frac{\eta}{\pi} (E_\mathrm{f}^2 - E_\Gamma^2) \\
        E &= h c/ \lambda ,\\
        &\mathrm{where}\:h\:\mathrm{is\:Planck's\:constant\:and}\:c\:\mathrm{is\:the\:speed\:of\:light\:in\:vacuum.} \\
        \chi &= M_1 + M_3 E^2 + \frac{\eta}{\pi} E^4 \mathrm{ln}((E_\mathrm{f}^2 - E^2)/(2 E_\Gamma - E^2)) \\
        n &= (\chi + 1)^{0.5} \\
        
    
    Wavelength range: 689 nm to 1033 nm
    
        | M. A. Afromowitz, "Refractive index of Ga_{1-x}Al_{x}As," Solid State Commun. 15, 59 (1974).
        | Notes: requires Al fraction input (x between 0 and 1), which defaults to x=1: "AlGaAs, x".

.. data:: AlN
    
    .. math:: n = \left(1 + \frac{2.80729}{1 - \left(0.147012/\lambda\right)^2} + \frac{0.231236}{1 - \left(1.58561 \times 10^{-4}/\lambda\right)^2} + \frac{1.56250 \times 10^{-2}}{1 - \left(1139.06/\lambda\right)^2}\right)^{0.5}
    
    Wavelength range: 210 nm to 1690 nm
    
        | (1) L. Y. Beliaev, E. Shkondin, A. V. Lavrinenko, and O. Takayama, "Thickness-dependent optical properties of aluminum nitride films for mid-infrared wavelengths," J. Vac. Sci. Technol. A 39, 043408 (2021).
        | (2)  L. Y. Beliaev, E. Shkondin, A. V. Lavrinenko, and O. Takayama, "Erratum: Thickness-dependent optical properties of aluminum nitride films for mid-infrared wavelengths," J. Vac. Sci. Technol. A 40, 027001 (2022).

.. data:: Au

    .. math:: n = 0.5747 + 9.664i

    Wavelength range: 1000 nm to 2000 nm

        | A. D. Rakic, A. B. Djurisic, J. M. Elazar, and M. L. Majewski, "Optical properties of metallic films for vertical-cavity optoelectronic devices," Appl. Opt. 37, 5271 (1998).
        | Notes: Lorentz-Drude model evaluated at 1550 nm. Constant near 1550 nm only.

    Wavelength range: 207 nm to 12400 nm
    
        | A. B. Djurišić, E. H. Li, D. Rakić, and M. L. Majewski, "Modeling the optical properties of AlSb, GaSb, and InSb," Appl Phys A 70, 29 (2000).

.. data:: Ge
    
    .. math:: n = \left( 1 + \frac{0.488633}{1 - (1.39396/ \lambda)^2} + \frac{14.5143}{1 - (0.162643/ \lambda)^2}  + \frac{9.12240 \times 10^{-3}}{1 - (752.190/ \lambda)^2} \right)^{0.5}
    
    Wavelength range: 2000 nm to 14000 nm
    
        | J. H. Burnett, S. G. Kaplan, E. Stover, and A. Phenis, "Refractive index measurements of Ge," Proc. SPIE 9974, 99740X (2016).

.. data:: GGG

    Wavelength range: 360 nm to 6000 nm
    
        | D. L. Wood and K. Nassau, "Optical properties of gadolinium gallium garnet," Appl. Opt. 29, 3704 (1990).

.. data:: H2O
    
    .. math:: n = \left(1 + \frac{0.760520}{1 - \left(8.59042 \times 10^{-2}/\lambda\right)^2} + \frac{3.99325 \times 10^{-2}}{1 - \left(2.83879/\lambda\right)^2} + \frac{1.56214 \times 10^{-2}}{1 - \left(2.83887/\lambda\right)^2}\right)^{0.5}

    See citation for refractive index equation.
    
    Wavelength range: 207 nm to 12400 nm
    
        | S. Adachi, "Optical dispersion relations for GaP, GaAs, GaSb, InP, InAs, InSb, AlxGa1−xAs, and In1−xGaxAsyP1−y," J. Appl. Phys. 66, 6030 (1989).

.. data:: InGaAs
    
    .. math::
        
        &\mathrm{In}_x\mathrm{Ga}_{1-x}\mathrm{As} \\\ \\
        &E_\mathrm{g,GaAs} = 1.424 \\
        &E_\mathrm{g,InGaAs} = E_\mathrm{g,GaAs} - 1.501 x + 0.436 x^2 \\\ \\
        &n = \left( 1 + 4.37251 + \frac{5.46674}{1 - \left( \frac{E_\mathrm{g,GaAs}}{E_\mathrm{g,InGaAs}}\frac{0.443131}{\lambda} \right)^2} + \frac{0.0242996}{1 - \left( \frac{E_\mathrm{g,GaAs}}{E_\mathrm{g,InGaAs}}\frac{0.874645}{\lambda} \right)^2} + \frac{1.95752}{1 - \left( \frac{36.9166}{\lambda} \right)^2} \right)^{0.5} \\
    
    Wavelength range: 970 nm to 17000 nm
    
        | Index calculated by shifting the bandgap relative to the refractive index of GaAs. The bandgap of InGaAs is reference from:
        | R. E. Nahory, M. A. Pollack, W. D. Johnston Jr., R. L. Barns, "Band gap versus composition and demonstration of Vegard’s law for In1−xGaxAsyP1−y lattice matched to InP," Appl. Phys. Lett. 33, 659 (1978).
        | Notes: requires In fraction input (x between 0 and 1), which defaults to x=0: "InGaAs, x".

.. data:: InGaP

    Wavelength range: 700 nm to 1550 nm
    
        | M. Schubert, V. Gottschalch, C. M. Herzinger, H. Yao, P. G. Snyder, and J. A. Woollam, "Optical constants of GaxIn1−xP lattice matched to GaAs," J. Appl. Phys. 77, 3416 (1995)
