    effective_index
        (*list*) The real part of the effective index for each mode.

        Alias: ``n_eff``

    Ex, Ey, Ez, Hx, Hy, Hz
        (*complex arrays*) The electric (E [V/nm]) and magnetic (H [A/nm]) fields in the x-, y-, and z-directions. These calculated fields are interpolated to the center point of each mesh grid (defined by ``xc`` and ``yc``). The fields are normalized to the equation below.

        .. math::
            \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Re} \iint \left( \vec E \times \vec H^* \right) \! \cdot \! \hat{z} \, \mathrm{d}x \, \mathrm{d}y = 1 \, \mathrm{W}

        Deprecated: fetching these through ``get()`` (rather than :data:`get_fields`) prints a deprecation warning.

    Fx, Fy
        (*complex arrays*) Raw fields that are solved. They either correspond to the electric or magnetic fields depending on ``field_to_solve``. However, these raw fields are defined on the Yee mesh grid, not the center points of the mesh grid. An internal function extracts all other field components from ``Fx``, ``Fy``, ``permittivity``, and ``permeability``.

    Gx, Gy
        (*complex arrays*) The auxiliary longitudinal raw field components present for a bend or an anisotropic solve. Present only when the corresponding basis actually carries them.

    convergence
        (*dict*) The last :data:`converge` run on this profile, as plain data: the arguments it ran with, its ``status``, the settings it chose (``chosen``), one ``stages`` entry per setting it varied and one ``history`` row per solve (the setting's value, the target quantity, its change and estimated error, and the solve time).

    confinement_window
        (*list*) The confinement factor for each specified mode is saved under this variable only when the confinement region is specified with a list of vertices, instead of a specific shape.

    effective_area
        (*list*) The effective area of each waveguide mode in units of square microns (:math:`\mu \mathrm{m}^2`), calculated by the following equation.

        .. math::
            A_\mathrm{eff} = \frac{\left( \iint \left| \vec E \right|^2 \, \mathrm{d}x \, \mathrm{d}y \right)^2}{\iint \left| \vec E \right|^4 \, \mathrm{d}x \, \mathrm{d}y}

    extent, pml_extent
        (*list*) ``[xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax]`` of the full simulation window, and of the window with the pml region excluded.

    group_index
        (*list*) The group refractive index calculated for each mode.

        Alias: ``n_g``

    loss_dB_per_m
        (*float*) [dB/m] The power loss coefficient (:math:`\alpha`), which relates to the imaginary part of the effective index (:math:`\kappa`) by the following equation with the wavelength (:math:`\lambda`).

        Alias: ``alpha``

        .. math::
            \kappa = \frac{\alpha \lambda}{(4 \pi) 10 \, \mathrm{log}_{10}(e)} \approx \frac{\alpha \lambda}{54.575}

        Loss is positive and gain negative. Under a PML, a guided mode of a lossless structure can show a small loss or a small gain (a negative ``loss_dB_per_m``). Neither is physical. It is the error from truncating the mode's evanescent tail at the window and its PML, of the same size as the error in its effective index, and it vanishes as the window widens or the PML thickens (``converge(setting='pml')``). The solve warns when such a mode gains more than 1e-6 of its index.

    maximum_overlap
        (*float*) Largest overlap in the mode list, calculated from the ``orthogonality()`` function.

    overlap
        (*list*) The overlap integral in ``overlap`` uses the following formula to calculate the modal excitation of :math:`\vec E_2` by :math:`\vec E_1`.

            Coldren, Larry A., Scott W. Corzine, and Milan L. Mashanovitch, ''Diode lasers and photonic integrated circuits,'' John Wiley \& Sons, 2012.

        .. math::
            \mathrm{overlap} = \frac{4 n_\mathrm{eff,1} n_\mathrm{eff,2}}{(n_\mathrm{eff,1} + n_\mathrm{eff,2})^2} \frac{\left| \iint \vec E_2^* \cdot \vec E_1 \, \mathrm{d}x \, \mathrm{d}y \right|^2}{\iint \left| \vec E_1 \right|^2 \, \mathrm{d}x \, \mathrm{d}y \, \iint \left| \vec E_2 \right|^2 \, \mathrm{d}x \, \mathrm{d}y}

        Stored on the profile named by ``profile_b``. It holds the result of the latest :data:`overlap` call against that profile, and ``overlaps`` keeps them all.

    overlaps
        (*list*) One record per :data:`overlap` call against this profile (as ``profile_b``), each a dict with ``simulation_name_a``, ``profile_a``, ``mode_a``, ``mode_b`` and ``overlap``. Repeating the same pair of modes replaces its record.

    permittivity, permeability
        (*list*) The permittivity and permeability arrays are defined by ``mesh`` from the current shapes and settings. Each is a list of arrays defining the corresponding parameters in the x-, y-, and z-directions.

    PML_indices
        (*list*) Indices of modes that carry less than 75% of their power inside the simulation window. These are modes of the pml (absorbing) region rather than of the device. Present only when the profile was solved with a pml. See ``window_confinement``, and ``remove_pml_modes_bool``/``pml_seed_bool`` under Settings.

    scattering_sum, scattering_loss
        (*list*) Total per-mode scattering loss [dB/m] summed over shape edges: ``scattering_sum`` is a list of per-shape contributions, ``scattering_loss`` their sum. Populated after ``scattering()`` runs.

    shapes
        (*list*) The list of :data:`Shape` objects making up the profile, background included. Prefer :data:`get_shape` to read a single shape's attributes and metadata.

    Sx, Sy, Sz
        (*arrays*) [W/nm] The Poynting vector in the x-, y-, and z-directions.

    TE_fraction
        (*list*) Fractions representing how much the mode is like a TE mode, calculated with the following equation.

        .. math::
            \mathrm{{TE_fraction}} = \frac{\iint \left| \vec E_\mathrm{x} \right|^2 \, \mathrm{d}x \, \mathrm{d}y}{\iint \left| \vec E_\mathrm{x} \right|^2 + \left| \vec E_\mathrm{y} \right|^2 \, \mathrm{d}x \, \mathrm{d}y}

    TE_indices, TM_indices
        (*list*) Indices for the corresponding TE or TM modes in the modes list.

    wavelength
        (*float*) [nm] Free-space wavelength.

    window_confinement
        (*list*) Fraction of each mode's power inside the simulation window (inset by one grid cell on every side), only present when the profile has a pml. A mode below 75% is a mode of the absorbing region rather than of the device (the modes that ``remove_pml_modes_bool`` discards and ``PML_indices`` designates).

    xc, yc
        (*complex arrays*) Cell-center coordinates of the mesh grid, in the x- and y-directions. These can be complex when pml layers are introduced.

        Deprecated: ``x``, ``y``. Read through :data:`get_grid` instead.

Simulation-level variables
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Read with ``get(key)`` (no ``profile=``). Listed by :data:`inspect`.

.. glossary::

    emode_version
        (*str*) The version of EMode that wrote the simulation file.

    EMode_simulation_file
        (*str*) The file name the simulation was created with. It also serves as a marker that this is a valid EMode simulation file.

    file_type
        (*str*) The simulation file's extension, ``'.eph'``.

    serialized
        (*bool*) Internal bookkeeping for the file's on-disk (de)serialization state.

    eme_scattering
        (*bool*) Legacy key, found only in simulation files written before EMode 1.0.5, which still load. It has no effect: EME scattering is controlled by ``EME_settings(apply_scattering=...)``, and ``settings(eme_scattering=...)`` is deprecated and no longer stores it. On a newer file ``get('eme_scattering')`` returns False with a deprecation warning.

    materials
        (*list*) Names of every material in the database, built-in and user-added. A user-added material's own properties are returned by ``get(NAME)``. See ``user_material_NAME`` below.

    priority_indices
        (*list*) A list of indices corresponding to the priorities of the shapes in the current profile.

    profiles
        (*dict*) The named profiles saved in this file (see "How the simulation file is organized" above). It does not include ``'_default'``.

    propagation_resolution
        (*float*) [nm] Sampling resolution used along the propagation direction for EME field reconstruction.

    pulse_response
        (*PulseResponse*) The spectrum of every tracked mode along the chain from the most recent :data:`EME` or :data:`pulse_propagate` with a ``PulsedSource`` excitation. It is returned by ``get('pulse_response')`` (EMode\ :sup:`3D`\  only). See :class:`PulseResponse`.

    pulsed_source
        (*PulsedSource*) The declared pulsed excitation. It is returned by ``get('pulsed_source')``.

    response
        (*CircuitResponse*) The power-dependent nonlinear response from the most recent EME solve with a declared excitation. It is returned by ``get('response')`` and also carries ``trajectories``, the forward amplitudes recorded along each :math:`\chi^{(2)}` slice, read with ``power_vs_z(wavelength)`` or ``amplitude_vs_z(wavelength)``.

    S_matrix
        (*SMatrix*) The scattering matrix from a solved EME chain. It is returned by ``get('S_matrix')`` (EMode\ :sup:`3D`\  only).

    sources
        (*list*) The declared excitation sources for the EME chain. It is returned by ``get('sources')``.

    sweep_data
        (*dict*) Results from the most recent ``sweep()`` call.

    user_material_NAME
        (*str*) The name of a user defined material.

Settings
^^^^^^^^

Read with ``get(key, profile=NAME)``, like the per-profile variables above. A
multi-wavelength profile returns a ``dict[float, ...]`` keyed by wavelength. A setting
reads back under the name it was set by, so an alias given to :data:`settings` (such as
``radius`` or ``N_pml``) works here too. Each is also a field of
``get_profile(NAME).settings``.

.. glossary::

    bend_radius
        (*float*) [nm] Bend radius of the waveguide. A value of 0 indicates that no bend is applied.

        Alias: ``radius``

    bend_method
        (*str*) How a nonzero ``bend_radius`` is solved. ``'cylindrical'`` (the default) adds the bend factor 1 + x/R to the mode solver. ``'TO'`` solves the straight cross-section with its material transformed by the bend's conformal map (transformation optics). Both work with the FDM and the FEM. The two methods' effective indices differ by about 6e-4 at R = 10 um, and their bend losses by about 1 % on a fine grid. With a PML, a bend's spectrum starts with PML modes, so set ``max_effective_index`` just above the guided mode. An under-resolved bend shows up as spurious bend loss. The 'Bend Mode Solvers' example compares the four combinations.

    boundary_condition
        (*str*) Boundary condition for the simulation window. A value of 0 indicates a metal boundary (driving all fields to zero at the boundary) and A or S indicate anti-symmetric or symmetric Ex. The first character indicates south boundary condition and the second character indicates the west boundary condition. ``get('boundary_condition')`` returns the string as given (for example ``'TE'``), and ``BC`` below is the resolved boundary condition.

        Alias: ``BC``, as a :data:`settings` argument only. ``get('BC')`` returns the resolved value.

    BC
        (*str*) A copy of the boundary_condition before running FDM(). After running FDM(), this variable represents the actual boundary condition string as a combination of '0', 'A', or 'S'. For example, setting the boundary_condition to 'TE' and running FDM() will result in BC changing to either 'SS', '0S', 'S0', or '00', depending on the index profile cross-section symmetry.

    expansion_resolution
        (*list*) List of the desired mesh step size in the x- and y-directions in the expanded regions around the perimeter of the simulation window.

    expansion_size
        (*list*) List of the size of the expanded regions in the x- and y-directions.

    fem_max_dofs
        (*int*) The FEM solver stops refining before the problem exceeds this many unknowns.

    fem_max_refinements
        (*int*) Maximum number of adaptive FEM refinement passes. 0 disables refinement.

    fem_mesh_wavelength
        (*float*) [nm] The FEM solver builds and refines its mesh at this wavelength and solves every wavelength on it. 0 meshes each solve at its own wavelength.

    fem_min_angle
        (*float*) [degrees] Minimum triangle angle of the FEM mesh, at most 34.

    fem_neff_tolerance
        (*float*) The FEM solver stops refining once no requested mode's effective index moves by more than this relative amount.

    fem_order
        (*int*) FEM element order, 1 or 2. Order 2 converges much faster in the effective index.

    fem_points_per_wavelength
        (*float*) Initial FEM mesh density, as mesh points per wavelength in each material. :data:`converge` chooses it for the FEM with ``setting='resolution'``.

    fem_refine_fraction
        (*float*) Share of the estimated error each adaptive FEM refinement pass targets, in (0, 1].

    field_to_solve
        (*str*) Desired transverse field component to solve: either 'Et' or 'Ht'.

    generate_chi2
        (*bool*) Generate the second-order nonlinear susceptibility (:math:`\chi^{(2)}`) tensor for the simulation window when meshing.

    include_heat
        (*bool*) Include the temperature change from the most recent ``heat()`` solve in the material properties.

    include_scattering
        (*bool*) Compute the interfacial scattering loss of every rough shape after each solve of this profile. Set with ``settings(include_scattering=True)``.

    max_effective_index
        (*float*) Upper limit for the effective index, which is the eigensolver's shift unless ``pml_seed_bool`` derives one automatically.

    mesh_complete_bool
        Removed. Use ``get_profile(NAME).status.meshed``.

    num_modes
        (*int*) Total number of modes to solve. :data:`converge` chooses it with ``setting='modes'``.

    num_pml_layers
        (*int* or *list*) Either an integer or a list of integers indicating the number of perfectly matched layers for all or each boundary: [North, South, East, West]. The FDM's pml is this many grid cells thick where ``pml_thickness`` is 0. For the FEM it refines the pml's mesh (10, the default, meshes it at its material's resolution, 20 twice as finely), and it does not set the thickness.

    pml_thickness
        (*float* or *list*) Either a float or a list of floats indicating the perfectly matched layer thickness in nm for all or each boundary: [North, South, East, West]. In the FDM, 0 means the boundary uses ``num_pml_layers`` instead. The FEM delivers exactly this thickness, and where it is 0 the FEM chooses twice the pml's imaginary depth (see ``pml_thickness`` under :data:`settings`). Unlike a layer count, this holds the absorber's physical size fixed as the resolution changes. :data:`converge` chooses it with ``setting='pml'``.

    pml_alpha_max
        (*float*) The complex-frequency-shifted (CFS) term of the pml profile, where 0 disables it.

    pml_kappa_max
        (*float*) The maximum real coordinate stretch of the pml profile, reached at the outer pml face, in both the FDM and the FEM.

    pml_NSEW_bool
        (*list*) List of booleans indicating if a perfectly matched layer (pml) boundary condition is applied to each boundary: [North, South, East, West].

    pml_order
        (*float*) The polynomial grading exponent of the pml stretch profile.

    pml_reflection
        (*float*) The target round-trip reflection that the pml is designed for, which sets the maximum pml conductivity.

    pml_seed_bool
        (*bool*) Seed the pml eigensolve with the fundamental mode of the same structure solved without a pml, so the guided fundamental lands at mode 0 without a hand-tuned ``max_effective_index``.

    remove_pml_modes_bool
        (*bool*) Indicates whether or not to automatically remove artificial modes found in the pml layers.

    shape_list, shape_materials
        Removed. Use ``get_profile(NAME).shapes`` (or the per-profile ``shapes`` variable above).

    solver
        (*str*) The mode solver for this profile: ``'default'``, ``'FDM'`` or ``'FEM'``. ``'default'`` is the FDM in every session. The FEM runs only when asked for, with ``solver='FEM'`` or ``FEM()``.

    solver_threads
        (*int*) Maximum number of threads the sparse solver uses to factor this profile's systems. 0 lets the solver choose, up to every core.

    sparse_solver
        (*str*) The sparse direct solver for this profile's solves: ``'auto'``, ``'rslab'`` or ``'pardiso'``. ``'auto'`` uses MKL PARDISO on the x86 installers (Linux, Windows and Intel Mac) and rslab on the Apple silicon installer. ``'pardiso'`` is available only in the x86 installers.

    subpixel_avg
        (*bool*) Use sub-pixel averaging of the permittivity and permeability at shape boundaries.

    tolerance
        (*float*) Numerical tolerance for convergence of the effective indices.

    window_height
        (float) [nm] Total height (y-direction) of the simulation window. The mesh is a whole even number of ``y_resolution`` cells, starting at the window's bottom (y = 0), so a layer stacked from there in whole cells has its faces on grid lines. A window that is not a whole even number of cells grows to the next even count at the top. Under a y fold of ``boundary_condition`` it grows by the same amount above and below instead, so its middle, where the symmetry wall sits, stays a grid line. ``settings`` warns when the window grows, and ``get('window_height')`` then reads the height that was meshed. A ``window_height`` that is a multiple of twice ``y_resolution`` is meshed as given. The FEM meshes the same window. :data:`converge` chooses it with ``setting='window'``.

    window_width
        (float) [nm] Total width (x-direction) of the simulation window. The mesh is a whole even number of ``x_resolution`` cells with a grid line at x = 0, the window's middle. A width that is not grows to the next even count, by the same amount on each side, which keeps x = 0 a grid line, and ``get('window_width')`` then reads the width that was meshed. :data:`converge` chooses it with ``setting='window'``.

    x_resolution, y_resolution
        (*float*) [nm] Mesh grid step in the x- and y-directions. :data:`converge` chooses them with ``setting='resolution'``.

Shape attributes
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Read with :data:`get_shape` (or ``get('shape_SHAPE')``), which returns a Shape object with
these attributes, plus a ``metadata`` dict populated once ``scattering()``/``confinement()``
have run for that shape.

.. glossary::

    SHAPE['correlation_length']
        (*list*) A list of two values describing the correlation length of the roughness on the vertical and horizontal edges of the shape.

        Alias: ``Lc_nm``

    SHAPE['fill_material']
        (*float* or *str*) Either a value or a material name to define the refractive index in the etched region of a 'planar' shape.

    SHAPE['geometry']
        (*dict*) A dictionary of the parameters of the shapes geometry

    SHAPE['geometry']['etch_depth']
        (*float*) The etch depth associated with a 'planar' shape that also has a defined ``SHAPE['geometry']['mask']``. The shape will have a thickness outside the mask definition equal to the difference between the ``SHAPE['geometry']['height']`` and ``SHAPE['geometry']['etch_depth']`` (or zero if this is negative).

    SHAPE['geometry']['height']
        (*float*) Maximum size of the shape in the y-direction.

    SHAPE['geometry']['mask']
        (*list*) The masks for this shape

    SHAPE['geometry']['mask_offset']
        (*list*) The mask offsets for this shape

    SHAPE['geometry']['position']
        (*list*) The x- and y-positions of the center point of the shape, constrained by the ``SHAPE['geometry']['width']`` and ``SHAPE['geometry']['height']``.

    SHAPE['geometry']['shape_type']
        (*str*) The shape type is either 'planar', 'conformal', 'polygon', or 'ellipse'.

    SHAPE['geometry']['sidewall_angle']
        (*float*) [degrees] Angle of the side wall for a 'planar' shape relative to a vertical at 0 degrees.

    SHAPE['geometry']['tone']
        (*str*) The tone of the mask ('p' or 'n')

    SHAPE['geometry']['vertices']
        (*list*) Pairs of [x,y] vertices that define the perimeter of a shape.

    SHAPE['geometry']['width']
        (*float*) Maximum size of the shape in the x-direction.

    SHAPE['loss_dB_per_m']
        (*float*) [dB/m] Absorption coefficient for power loss in the region defined by the shape.

    SHAPE['mask']
        (*float* or *list*) Width of the a mask for etching a 'planar' shape. Also accepts a list to define both the width and the x-offset of the mask.

    SHAPE['name']
        (*str*) User-defined name of the shape. This name will be used to reference this shape in subsequent functions.

    SHAPE['priority']
        (*float*) A value that defines the order in which the shape is drawn relative to other shapes. A higher value give a higher priority, putting the shape in front of other shapes with lower priority.

    SHAPE['roughness_rms']
        (*list*) A list of two values describing the rms roughness on the vertical and horizontal edges of the shape.

        Alias: ``st_dev_nm``

    SHAPE['metadata']
        (*dict*) A dictionary of metadata associated with the shape

    SHAPE['metadata']['confinement']
        (*list*) Confinement factor for each mode in the corresponding shape.

    SHAPE['metadata']['edges']
        (*list*) Definitions of edges for the corresponding shape where the scattering loss is calculated. These edges can be correlated to the loss values from ``SHAPE['metadata']['scattering_all_edges']``.

    SHAPE['metadata']['scattering_all_edges']
        (*list*) Calculated scattering loss for each edge of the shape, defined by ``SHAPE['metadata']['edges']``.

    SHAPE['metadata']['scattering_horizontal_edges']
        (*list*) Calculated scattering loss for each horizontal edge of the shape.

    SHAPE['metadata']['scattering_sum']
        (*list*) Total calculated scattering loss for all edges of the shape.

    SHAPE['metadata']['scattering_vertical_edges']
        (*list*) Calculated scattering loss for each vertical edge of the shape.



Release Notes
^^^^^^^^^^^^^

**1.0.7**

* New

  * :data:`optimize` finds the parameters of a simulation you have already set up that give the best value of a quantity you choose, within bounds and constraints, available with EMode\ :sup:`3D`. The parameters are named with the keys of :data:`sweep`: a setting, one profile's setting (``'setting, <profile>, <name>'``), a shape property (``'shape, <name>, <property>'``), a section property (``'section, <name>, <property>'``) or an argument of a :data:`monitor_coupling` beam (``'beam, <name>'``). The ``Parameter``, ``Objective`` and ``Constraint`` classes of emodeconnection declare them as data. An objective is an S-matrix element's power or phase, a monitor coupling, a mode's effective index, group index or loss, a pulse's energy or average power in a wavelength band, or a parameter itself, and a list of objectives is their weighted sum. The methods are 'cobyqa' (the default), 'nelder-mead', 'powell', 'differential_evolution', 'l-bfgs-b' and 'slsqp', the last two with finite-difference gradients. Every evaluation starts from the simulation as declared, so its result depends only on its parameters. A cross-section an earlier evaluation solved is not solved again, so optimizing a section length solves the modes once. ``record=`` writes each evaluation to a file as it completes, and the simulation is left solved at the best point. An EMode\ :sup:`2D` session that calls it gets a ``LicenseError``. See :doc:`Optimization </emodeguide/optimization>`.
  * Poling design with every domain free. ``Parameter('poling, <section>, domain_lengths', bounds=(min, max))`` makes the length of each domain of a poled section a variable of :data:`optimize`, within a fabrication minimum and maximum, and ``'poling, <section>, total_length'`` can be constrained. With 'l-bfgs-b' or 'slsqp' and a ``'band_energy'`` or ``'band_average'`` objective, the gradient with respect to every domain comes from one adjoint propagation, so an evaluation with its gradient costs one and a half to two and a half propagations, whatever the number of domains. :class:`Poling` has a new form, ``Poling(domain_lengths=[...])``. The website has a new example, 'Nonlinear-EME: PPLN Inverse Design', which optimizes the poling of the 'Nonlinear-EME: Supercontinuum' device for the 750 nm band with every domain length free.
  * :data:`evaluate` evaluates a simulation at one point. It restores the simulation's snapshot, sets every parameter, solves what the requested results need and returns a record, so the same parameters give the same results whatever ran before. :data:`snapshot` takes that snapshot, and with ``file_name`` also writes it as an ``.eph`` file that another session can evaluate from. Both are available in every license tier.
  * :data:`converge` finds the resolution, window, PML thickness or number of modes a result needs (``setting='resolution'``, ``'window'``, ``'pml'``, ``'modes'``, or ``'all'`` for each in turn), for one mode's effective index, group index, loss or orthogonality (``target``). It steps the setting, follows the mode by its overlap rather than its place in the mode list, and stops once the estimated error is within ``tolerance`` on two consecutive steps, or reports why it could not (``'oscillating'``, ``'lost mode'`` or ``'budget'``, for example). It prints one row per solve and returns a ``ConvergenceResult``. The profile's settings change only with ``apply=True``. It works with the FDM and the FEM and is available in every license tier. See :data:`converge` and the new example 'Straight Waveguide Convergence'.
  * :data:`sweep` takes several keys at once: with ``key`` and ``values`` as lists it sweeps every combination. A key can name one profile's setting, ``'setting, <profile>, <name>'``.
  * Measured pulses. ``PulsedSource(shape='measured', measurement=PulseMeasurement(...))`` launches a measured spectrum or temporal trace, with or without a retrieved phase (FROG or SPIDER). The samples are fitted first ('smooth', 'sech' or 'gaussian'), and a fit whose quality is below ``min_fit_quality`` (default 0.99) is refused with an error that gives the quality reached. ``background`` subtracts a constant pedestal before the fit, and ``get('pulse_response').measured_fit`` reports the fit. See :class:`PulseMeasurement`.
  * Pulsed propagation follows the tracked modes through an avoided crossing inside the band, adding the crossing partner on its own, carries modes that are guided over only part of the band, and follows the second-harmonic modes a :math:`\chi^{(2)}` section phase-matches. A pulse response reports ``window_gap``, the empty stretch of the periodic time window, and warns when the pulse wraps onto itself.
  * Pulsed propagation searches for the second-harmonic modes an unpoled :math:`\chi^{(2)}` section phase-matches wherever the pump has light as it broadens, not only where the launched pulse has light. When a match lies outside the launched spectrum, a quick run of the pump alone finds where the pump reaches first, which adds its time to :data:`EME`. ``PulsedProcess(modal_search=)`` chooses the search: ``'broadened'`` (the default), ``'launch'`` (the launched spectrum only) or a ``(min, max)`` band of fundamental wavelengths in nm. ``max_harmonic_modes`` (default 3) caps the second-harmonic modes tracked, and ``harmonic_coupling`` (default 0.1) is the weakest coupling tracked, relative to the strongest. ``get('pulse_response').rank_report`` gives, for each slice, the number of field patterns used, the number ``pattern_threshold`` asks for and the share of each tracked mode's field the patterns leave out. The solver warns when ``max_rank`` leaves out more than 1 % of a tracked mode's field.
  * Free-space beams (:data:`free_space_field`). ``waist_position`` places the beam's waist along its path, so the launched beam carries the wavefront curvature and Gouy phase of that distance. ``waist`` and ``waist_position`` take ``(x, y)`` pairs for elliptical and astigmatic beams. ``modes``, with ``powers`` and ``phases``, launches a combination of the port's own modes instead of a beam.
  * ``SMatrix.mode_power`` holds the power each port mode carries, and ``unitarity_error()``, ``power()`` and ``insertion_loss_dB()`` weigh by it, so they read power at a port whose modes carry unequal power, such as a plane-wave section. ``unitarity_error(from_ports=)`` counts only the modes of the ports named.
  * New website examples: 'Straight Waveguide Convergence' (the SiN guide of 'Bend Mode Solvers' without the bend, solved by the FDM and the FEM, with the effective and group index errors against run time), 'EME: MMI' (a 1x2 and a 2x2 MMI, the 2x2's width and length set by :data:`optimize`), 'EME: S-Bend', 'EME: Y-Branch', 'Nonlinear-EME: SFG', 'Ring Resonator Design' and 'SMF-28 Fiber'. The examples page shows a card with a thumbnail for every example.
  * The layout view (``plot(view='layout')``) draws the Index and Shapes panels on the chip, from each shape's placed outline. The 'z-y' panel offers Index and Shapes too. A branching circuit, such as an MZI or a Y-branch, draws each arm's field on its own arm. EME ports are drawn as lines over their windows, and an angled facet is drawn at its tilt.
  * With ``EMODE_HEADLESS=1``, :data:`material_explorer` and :data:`plot_S_matrix` return a ``PlotImage``, as :data:`plot` does, instead of opening a window.
  * ``EMode(quiet=True)`` hides the solver's printed output. Warnings and errors still reach stderr.
  * ``get('n_eff')`` reads the effective index. :data:`permittivity` and :data:`permeability` take a :class:`MaterialSpec` and every other material form :data:`refractive_index` takes. A member of a multi-wavelength profile is named ``'<profile>.<wavelength>'``, as in ``get('effective_index', profile='tfln.1550')``, and an ambiguous name raises an error that names the candidates.
  * ``dn_dT`` and ``eps_r_dc`` can be given per axis for an anisotropic material, so :data:`heat` shifts each axis by its own ``dn_dT``.
  * When every EMode\ :sup:`3D` seat is in use and a session falls back to EMode\ :sup:`2D`, it warns once: "Every EMode3D seat is in use, so this session runs as EMode2D." ``emode login`` on the command line can clear one numbered session, as the login window can.
  * Every installer includes ``THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.html``, which lists the third-party components it contains and their licenses.
  * emodeconnection 1.1.24 carries the client side of this release: the optimizer's and :data:`converge`'s types, ``Confinement``, measured pulses, poling by domain lengths, the second-harmonic options and ``RankReport``, ``SMatrix.mode_power`` and quiet mode.

* Changed

  * The FDM's subpixel averaging follows each interface: the field component normal to it sees the harmonic mean of the materials' permittivities, the tangential ones the arithmetic mean, and a gap or strip thinner than a cell is averaged as a layer. A material face between grid lines no longer gives a first-order error, so effective indices move toward their converged values. A 500 x 220 nm silicon strip's TM mode at 1550 nm on a 25 nm grid moves from 1.8174 to 1.7760, against 1.7735 converged. Structures whose faces sit on grid lines give the same results as before.
  * ``FDM()``, ``FEM()`` and :data:`solve` on a multi-wavelength profile return a ``WavelengthDict`` with every wavelength's result, keyed by wavelength, where they returned only the last wavelength's. A single wavelength still returns a plain dict.
  * Enabling a PML no longer shifts the cell centers of an expansion region. Expansion regions are now built from their cell edges, so results on grids with an expansion region change slightly (by 5e-7 in the 'Angled: LNOI' example's effective index, from this change alone).
  * :data:`confinement` indexes modes by integer on the client, as the server does: ``confinement()['core'][0]`` is the fundamental mode's confinement factor in ``core``. It returns a ``Confinement``, a read-only mapping. :data:`get_shape`'s ``metadata['confinement']`` is keyed by integer too. A client older than emodeconnection 1.1.24 still reads string keys.
  * A window that is not a whole even number of cells is grown to the next even count, with a warning, instead of being trimmed without one, in the FEM too. The cells are added at the top, so y = 0 stays a grid line, or evenly above and below when the solve folds y, so the fold's wall is a grid line. ``get('window_width')`` and ``get('window_height')`` read the meshed size.
  * Symmetry folds are decided from the whole cross-section: a symmetric pair of masks folds, a shape of the background's material no longer prevents a fold, and an EME chain folds only where every section agrees. A fold's wall must lie on a grid line: where it cannot, a fold that 'TE' or 'TM' implies is dropped, and an explicit 'S' or 'A' warns. A heat or electrostatic change that breaks the mirror symmetry unfolds the solve, with a warning.
  * The cylindrical bend's FDM operator is reciprocal: a bend's modes are orthogonal under the solver's reciprocity product to 6e-14 (3e-3 before), and a bend toward +x and the same bend toward -x give one effective index. Bend effective indices move by up to about 8e-5, the first-order error removed, which halved with the cell size.
  * EME of a crystal turned in the plane, such as an x-cut lithium niobate bend, conserves power and is reciprocal. Lossy modes keep their exact backward partners, and the junction is solved for the turned crystal's mirrored orientation, which is turned the other way. An x-cut half ring keeps 0.999992 of its power at the default settings, where it lost about 1.6 %. The 'EME: TFLN Ring Resonator' example's spectrum now shows a second mode family beside the fundamental's resonances.
  * An angled facet's field is rotated onto the facet plane with the right sign. A 30 degree facet now matches the Fresnel coefficients (R\ :sub:`s` 0.0827, 0.0195 before), and every angled-facet result moves. The 'EME: Angled Facet' example is regenerated.
  * ``alpha`` keeps its sign, and a solve warns when a mode of a passive structure gains power under a PML. The apparent gain is the window's truncation error and falls as the PML and window converge.
  * The heat solve takes the background material's thermal conductivity, where it used a fixed 1e-9.
  * Only the first automatically stacked shape, the substrate, extends down past the bottom of the window. A shape given an explicit y ``position`` never does, even when its bottom is at y = 0.
  * The section keys ``etch_depth`` and ``sidewall_angle`` are no longer :data:`sweep` keys. A sweep over them raises an error.
  * An unknown keyword argument raises an error that names it and the valid ones, before the function runs.
  * emodeconnection 1.1.24 sends only the settings of an argument that differ from their defaults, so it works with EMode 1.0.6. An option new in 1.0.7, used with an older EMode, is refused before anything is sent, with an error that names the option. When a client sends a setting or a type EMode does not know, EMode ignores the setting with a warning, or answers with an error and keeps the session, where it stopped before.
  * Every installer, the Intel Mac one included, meshes FEM cross-sections with ``triangle`` 20250106.
  * Examples whose numbers moved, each regenerated: 'Multi-physics: Phase Shifter' (V\ :sub:`pi`\ L 5.91 V·cm, 5.39 on the 1.0.6 page, from the electrostatic and electro-optic fixes below), 'Multi-physics: Heater' (the power for a pi phase shift is 14.2 mW, 13.2 on the 1.0.6 page, from the heat fixes below), 'Nonlinear-EME: SHG' (its pump moves to 1971.958 nm to stay phase-matched on its 10 nm grid under the new averaging, straight conversion 18.53 %, 17.72 % in 1.0.6), 'Bend Mode Solvers' (the 'TE' fold is back, and the two FDM bend methods give the same effective index on every grid) and 'Nonlinear-EME: Supercontinuum' (the pulse follows TE0's TM partner and a :math:`\chi^{(2)}` harmonic).

* Fixed

  * With ``bend_method='TO'``, the FDM's bend loss was wrong: the 'Bend Mode Solvers' bend read 0.0003 dB/m or less against the cylindrical method's 0.0174, and about 27 % high with PMLs on the side walls only. The PML saw an almost unbent guide. The two methods now agree to about 1 %, and the loss no longer changes with the PML thickness.
  * With ``bend_method='TO'``, a symmetry fold changed the modes (the 'Bend Mode Solvers' bend read 1.677891 with 'TE' and 1.665974 unfolded at 20 nm), and on an off-center SiN bend the TO and cylindrical methods differed by 1e-3 at 40 nm. The shapes and the bend were sampled a quarter of a cell off. Folded and unfolded solves now agree to 1e-5, and the two methods to 1.5e-5 at 10 nm. The page's earlier finding that TO converges faster was this error cancelling the discretization error at 25 nm.
  * A mode plot of a bend solved with ``bend_method='TO'`` ran one PML thickness past the grid. Its axes and PML hatch now match the cylindrical method's, and both methods draw the PML only with ``window_display=True``.
  * :data:`group_index` compared mode k of the solve with mode k of the solve at the shifted wavelength, so a PML mode that moved in the list gave nonsense, such as about -150 on a bend with ``bend_method='TO'``. It now pairs modes by overlap and seeds the shifted solve. A mode it cannot pair reads NaN, with a warning.
  * The FDM's permittivity was rounded to single precision, which put up to 1e-3 of noise into :data:`group_index`. The FEM's :data:`group_index` remeshed the shifted solve, which could put 6e-4 of error into it.
  * With a PML on a leaky substrate, the FDM could sort the guided mode behind PML modes, so a one-mode solve returned an absorber mode. Modes confined to the window now come first, and a solve that returns only PML modes asks for more.
  * With a PML, a guided mode whose effective index carried a small spurious gain could come back on the backward branch, with a negative effective index.
  * The FEM ignored ``pml_thickness``, ``num_pml_layers`` and ``pml_kappa_max``. It now honors all three, as the FDM does.
  * A south symmetry fold with a PML on only one of the north and south walls crashed the FDM. A PML on a folded wall is now dropped with a warning naming the wall, and the kept wall's PML is mirrored.
  * In an anisotropic solve with a PML, the off-diagonal terms dropped the PML's phase, so a 10-layer PML read a turned bend's loss 4 % low.
  * A lossy crystal turned in the plane was solved as a gain medium, and one of its modes grew along the guide.
  * An earlier solve could change which lossy modes a later anisotropic solve returned, so the results depended on the order of the solves.
  * The TE fraction of a hybrid mode could exceed 1. It is now a power fraction.
  * A symmetric pair of masks never folded, an ellipse was not quite symmetric so a round core never folded, and a :data:`settings` change on a meshed profile reset its boundary condition to '00', which silently unfolded a 'TE' solve.
  * A symmetry fold on a window with an odd number of cells put the mirror wall in the middle of a cell, which mirrored that cell and widened the core.
  * A folded mode on an 'S' or 'A' wall was weighted as a full cell at the wall, so a junction between folded sections could create up to 2.4 % power.
  * Cell-centered fields at a window's high wall were left at zero, so the two walls differed by up to 8e-3 of the peak field.
  * :data:`heat` gave fill cells beside an etched core the dn/dT of a ``heat_only`` substrate, 21 times too large. The heat change and the electro-optic change now take each permittivity component at its own grid point, the electro-optic change takes each material's own static field at a material wall, and a fold checks the heat or electrostatic change against its mirror image.
  * The electrostatic solve summed its bilinear form into one number over the whole mesh, so it ignored ``eps_r_dc``, and it left each electrode's outline free, so V\ :sub:`pi`\ L followed the electrode's mesh size. The Phase Shifter example is now converged with its mesh.
  * :data:`settings` with ``wavelength=`` did not reach labeled profiles, so :data:`EME` re-solved sections at their old wavelength, and :data:`sweep` set a setting on the default profile only. A wavelength :data:`sweep` of an EME chain now moves the labeled profiles the chain is built on, a sweep of another setting of such a chain warns naming the profiles that keep their own value, and :data:`EME` warns when a chain's profiles are at another wavelength than the default profile.
  * A taper's equal slices could act as a grating and reflect in phase, which refinement could not see (a Y-branch splitter's taper reflected 2.5e-2, against 2.05e-4 converged). A slice over which the cross-section changes is now cut under a fraction of half the guided wavelength (the section setting ``slice_phase_limit``) where that reflection matters, and a long, slow taper keeps about ``schedule_max_slices`` slices.
  * A taper's sidewall scattering loss dropped to zero on slices whose cross-section had already been solved, and changed with the slice count.
  * Pulsed propagation now applies sidewall scattering loss on sections with ``EME_settings(apply_scattering=True)``, each tracked mode at its own rate, and a smooth cross-section with ``apply_scattering=True`` no longer makes a pulsed :data:`EME` raise.
  * ``Poling(inverted_first=True)`` never reached the pulsed solver.
  * A ``PulsedSource`` on a port other than the first was launched into the first, and a second ``PulsedProcess`` with different modes was ignored. Both now raise an error naming the argument.
  * The 'Nonlinear-EME: Supercontinuum' example under-resolved an avoided crossing between 800 and 1100 nm. Its pulse now follows the crossing.
  * The continuous-wave :math:`\chi^{(2)}` solve's fixed absolute tolerance swamped a weak generated field, so a 1 µW pump's conversion read far too high. The tolerance now follows the fields (``solver_atol=None``, the new default), and strong pumps solve as before.
  * The :math:`\chi^{(2)}` coupling cache ignored a shape's scattering values, so two sections that differed only in roughness gave the same conversion.
  * A junction of a crystal turned in the plane was not reciprocal or passive with lossy modes (a TFLN ring's bend junction amplified, largest singular value 2.40), an x-cut bend's refinement did not finish with more than 4 modes, and an FEM-sliced x-cut bend appeared to lose 1.2 % of its power in pi/8.
  * ``mode_power`` and the junctions used different products at a slot-like port (up to 2 % apart), and a tilted facet's trace dropped its staggered-grid fields. Both now use the product the junctions conserve.
  * A facet's power budget weighted the reflection with the forward trace's power instead of the backward trace's.
  * A confined port window's crop dropped a row or column of the parent's cells, so an off-lattice window read up to 1.2e-3 low.
  * The interpolated wavelength sweep zeroed modes it could not track even at the center wavelength, held a lost mode's junction entries (which could gain power), divided by zero on a chain with windowed ports (on lossy modes with no real index), and over-warned on resonators. Its S-matrices now carry ``mode_power``.
  * ``SMatrix.unitarity_error`` was meaningless for plane-wave sections. It now measures power conservation in each mode's own power frame.
  * On Linux, Windows and the Intel Mac, a re-solved port window whose cut wall lay in uniform cladding failed with a misleading "uniform refractive index profile" error. The solver shift is now moved off the eigenvalue and the matrix refactored.
  * ``FDM(scattering=True)`` on a multi-wavelength profile raised "profile has not been solved yet". :data:`mesh` and :data:`label_profile` raised on an unsolved multi-wavelength profile.
  * ``settings(res=...)`` raised instead of setting both resolutions.
  * ``reset(profile=)`` acted on the default profile only, and ``clear_field_data(profile=)`` ignored its profile and raised on a file holding a multi-wavelength profile.
  * ``save(save_all_fields=True)`` saved no fields. A file saved with it now reopens with its fields, without solving.
  * :data:`shape` rejected per-edge lists of ``roughness_rms`` and ``correlation_length``.
  * In the plot window, choosing a profile other than the default from the menu left the data menu unchanged, so a solved profile's field components were not offered.
  * Saving a plot from the toolbar as an unsupported file type failed with an internal error instead of showing a message.
  * An Outline panel of the layout view drew an empty colorbar.
  * :data:`material_explorer` and :data:`plot_S_matrix` changed later :data:`plot` figures through matplotlib's global settings.
  * :data:`plot` dropped a port label when its window ended outside the panel, logged a warning about "port None" for a chain with a bend, and in the simulation view drew a bend's outline curved, with the sections after it off the panel.
  * A license manager outage while a session was running could crash its license check-in or open the login window.
  * When no license was available, the client reported "EMode failed to launch".
  * A run with ``EMODE_HEADLESS=1`` opened the login window when EMode was not logged in, or after an upgrade, when the stored login was from the earlier version, and a solver started from a script could stop without a message. It now reports that EMode is not logged in and how to log in: run ``emode login``, or set ``EMODE_EMAIL`` and ``EMODE_PASSWORD`` and run ``emode login --write``.

* Faster

  * Meshing is 6 to 22 times faster.
  * Junction overlaps are one matrix product over all the modes instead of one integral per pair of modes. At 200 modes they take 0.17 s instead of 14.5 s.
  * Sampling an FEM field at points is about 1000 times faster, so FEM field plots and junctions between FEM sections no longer stall. An FEM EME taper builds about 20 % faster.
  * :data:`EME` decides each section's fold from its geometry before solving, so a chain whose sections differ in their folds is solved once.
  * The pulsed Kerr, Raman and two-photon absorption terms need 4.5 to 6.6 times less memory, and the full Raman response is 3.2 times faster. The 'Nonlinear-EME: Supercontinuum' example's :data:`EME` takes 115 s instead of 300 s.
  * An x-cut bend's refinement with 8 modes takes under a minute, where it did not finish in 10 minutes.

**1.0.6**

* Changed

  * On Apple silicon, the sparse direct solver is rslab 1.1.2 (from 1.1.0).
  * The Intel Mac installer continues, although the 1.0.5 notes announced 1.0.5 as its last release.
  * Improved EME junctions between mode-solved cross-sections: they conserve power and converge as modes are added, especially at large mode numbers, and across the mode solvers and their meshes. Results can move slightly from 1.0.5.
  * A taper or GDS section now starts refinement from slices placed where its cross-section changes (``EME_settings(initial_slices='auto')``, the new default), read from its rasterized refractive index: none along a straight run, evenly along a linear taper, densely inside a short fast feature, and at every corner of a GDS outline. Refinement still runs afterward and decides the final slicing, so results change only within its tolerance, and it takes fewer rounds. ``EME_settings(initial_slices='single')`` restores the one-slice start of earlier versions.
  * ``EME()`` and ``plot()`` use less memory.

* New

  * ``plot(normalization='section')`` scales each section of a 'z-x' or 'z-y' panel (a straight, a taper, a free-space gap) by its own peak, so a section that carries little of the launched field, such as the free-space gap after an angled facet, is still visible. The 'Norm' selector in the plot window offers it too. Brightness is then not comparable across sections.
  * ``plot(view='layout')``, the new default, draws the 'z-x' panel as the chip layout: every section where its connections place it, a bend as an arc and the sections after it turned with it, the field following the guide, both axes in um. ``view='simulation'`` is the unrolled display of earlier versions, and the 'Physical space' checkbox switches between them.
  * ``check_layout()`` reports overlapping sections, a section whose outline crosses itself, how far each loop of connected sections misses closing, and sections no connection reaches. ``EME()`` runs it first and refuses an overlap or a loop that misses by more than ``minimum_z_step`` before solving anything, and warns about a self-intersecting outline.
  * ``sweep(key='wavelength', values=..., result='S_matrix', method='interpolated')`` sweeps a circuit's S-matrix over hundreds of wavelengths for the cost of a few: the circuit is refined once, each cross-section is solved at ``num_nodes`` wavelengths (default 8), and the S-matrix at every requested wavelength is rebuilt from propagation constants and junctions interpolated between them. ``sweep_data`` reports the node count and the interpolation residual at a held-out node, with a warning above ``interpolation_tolerance``.
  * ``bend_section(name, profile, radius, sweep_angle, method)`` declares a circular bend (``sweep_angle`` in radians, positive toward +x), solved with the bend in cylindrical coordinates (``method='cylindrical'``, the default) or by transformation optics (``method='TO'``). Sections declared after it continue from its end. An anisotropic crystal turns with the guide: a bend in x-cut lithium niobate is sliced along its heading, and a section placed after a turn sees the crystal turned. A bend of an isotropic material is one mode solve. ``copy_section`` raises when a copy's placement would show the crystal differently from its source, rather than reusing the wrong S-matrix.
  * Monitors: ``monitor(name, w, y, angle, length, resolution)`` declares a plane inside the chain (output only, not a port), ``monitor_field(name)`` returns the solved field on it for 1 W launched with the power through it, and ``monitor_coupling(name, mode_field_diameter, angle)`` its coupling to a tilted Gaussian beam such as a fiber mode, the figure a grating coupler is designed for. By reciprocity the same number is the coupling from the fiber into the waveguide. ``sweep(result='monitor_coupling', monitor=, beam=)`` sweeps the beam's angle, size or position without solving again, or any other key with a solve at each value, and ``plot()`` draws each monitor's plane on the 'z-y' panel. The website has a new example, 'EME: Grating Coupler'.
  * A new website example, 'Bend Mode Solvers': the SiN bend of 'Bending: SiN' solved by the FDM with ``bend_method='cylindrical'`` and ``'TO'`` on four grids and by the FEM on six fixed meshes, with each solve's effective index, its error against the finest FEM mesh, its bend loss and its runtime, and plots of the effective-index and bend-loss errors against runtime.
  * The 'Bending: SiN' example uses the window and PMLs of 'Bend Mode Solvers': PMLs on the bend's outer, top and bottom walls (1 µm, ``pml_kappa_max=1``), 2 µm of cladding and 1.5 µm of trench, and a ``max_effective_index`` just above the guided mode.
  * A new website example, 'EME: TFLN Ring Resonator': a racetrack ring in x-cut thin-film lithium niobate, closed with ``connect_ports``, its coupler's bus and ring arms windowed ports, the through-port spectrum over several free spectral ranges from ``sweep(method='interpolated')``, with the free spectral range, extinction and loaded quality factor of each resonance, and the field built up around the ring on resonance, drawn on the chip.
  * Pulsed nonlinear propagation through an EME chain (EMode3D). ``settings(excitation=PulsedSource(...))`` declares a femtosecond pulse, ``straight_section(nonlinear=PulsedProcess(...))`` or ``taper_section(...)`` a section's nonlinearity and poling (``Poling``: a period, a period varying along the section, or explicit domain walls), and ``EME()`` refines the chain, solves each slice at a set of sample wavelengths and propagates the pulse through every slice and junction. ``get('pulse_response')`` returns the spectrum of every tracked mode along the chain, with ``band_energy()`` and ``band_power()`` for the energy and average power in a wavelength band. ``pulse_propagate(poling=...)`` reruns the propagation with another poling without solving any mode again. ``gds_section(nonlinear=PulsedProcess(...))`` declares a pulse's nonlinearity on a GDS section too. The website has a new example, 'Nonlinear-EME: Supercontinuum', and the EME guide a section on pulsed propagation. Each section's chi(2), Kerr (chi(3)), Raman and two-photon absorption come from its materials: ``PulsedProcess(chi3=True)`` takes chi(3) from every material's ``n2`` and raises naming a material that has none, the Raman response is that of the material holding most of the Kerr overlap, and two-photon absorption (on by default where a material has a coefficient, ``tpa=False`` to turn it off) acts only on photon pairs above the bandgap. The run warns when the pulse will drift far enough to wrap around the time window, when energy reached the window's edges, and when the band leaves a material's index model, and it refuses a band where an index model has no finite value (silicon's fit has a pole at 1135 nm).
  * Nonlinear material data for the pulsed solver: ``n2`` for SiO2, SiN, LN and LN_MgO, the Raman response of fused silica (Blow and Wood) and lithium niobate (its four A1(TO) lines, Bache and Schiek), two-photon absorption coefficients for Si, AlGaAs, LN and LN_MgO, and bandgaps for those and for SiO2, SiN and GaAs, each with its reference in ``property_refs``. A user material takes the same through ``MaterialProperties(n2=, raman=, tpa=, bandgap=)``, with ``raman=(fraction, [(weight, position, half_width), ...])`` in cm^-1.
  * ``settings(bend_method='TO')`` solves a bend by transformation optics: the straight cross-section is solved with its material transformed by the bend's conformal map, instead of adding the bend factor 1 + x / R to the solver (``bend_method='cylindrical'``, the default). It works with the FDM and the FEM, in 2D and 3D sessions alike (the transformed tensor of an isotropic material is diagonal), and agrees with the cylindrical method to about 6e-4 in the effective index and 5 % in bend loss at R = 10 um. With a PML, set ``max_effective_index`` just above the guided mode: a TO bend's spectrum starts with PML modes. ``report()`` names the method next to the solver.

* Fixed

  * With ``EMODE_NONINTERACTIVE=1``, a ``plot()`` could hang. It no longer shows a window in that mode.
  * On Apple silicon, a circuit with large free-space ports could run out of memory. The sparse solver now solves the port modes in small blocks.
  * Under a PML, a lossy absorber mode could come out as mode 0, ahead of the guided mode. Guided modes now come first, and ``remove_pml_modes_bool`` is more reliable.
  * In a lossy medium, some lossy modes grew along the guide instead of decaying, so an EME chain could amplify. Every mode of a passive structure now decays.
  * ``sweep(key='wavelength', solve_type='EME')`` never returned its data.
  * A function whose first argument is not ``key``, such as ``monitor_field('plane')``, failed when that argument was given positionally.
  * ``monitor_field()`` and ``monitor_coupling()`` failed on a chain built with ``copy_section``, such as a grating.
  * A wavelength scan with the FEM solved each wavelength on a different mesh, which added about 1e-5 of noise to the effective index. Wavelength scans now share one mesh (the new setting ``fem_mesh_wavelength`` chooses its wavelength).
  * A mirrored section (``copy_section(mirror=True)``) and a bend toward -x were laid out in the wrong place.
  * The 'z-x' outline left out shapes given by a ``width`` rather than a ``mask``.
  * A symmetry wall in x, including the one ``boundary_condition='TE'`` or ``'TM'`` adds, folded a bend about x, which a bend does not allow. A bend now keeps only the vertical fold, and an explicit x wall is replaced by ``'0'`` with a warning.
  * ``plot()`` of a circuit with a loop (a ring closed with ``connect_ports``) failed. It now draws the ring's layout, cross-sections and field. ``EME()`` of a ring with no open port no longer fails.
  * Windowed ports (``Port(window=...)``): several windows on one side of a section now conserve power and are reciprocal, connected or not, each window keeps only the modes its content guides, and each is placed on its own window in the layout. Results with windowed ports move slightly.
  * A section after a bend could meet it off-center when anything upstream was offset. Sections now meet centered along any path.
  * A refined taper or GDS section with interface roughness and ``EME_settings(apply_scattering=True)`` raised an error.

* Faster

  * Refinement bisects a slice at an already-solved cross-section near its midpoint when there is one (``EME_settings(snap_window=0.25)``, a fraction of the slice, 0 to disable), so a taper or GDS section that passes through widths another one solved reuses those solves.
  * Refinement reuses a solved cross-section wherever the geometry repeats it: the mirror-image half of a taper declared as two sections, or a GDS cell that tapers up and back down. Interpolated and cut geometry is rounded to about 1e-6 nm, so the two halves no longer differ in the last bits and miss the cache (one slice in six re-solved on a mirrored taper).

**1.0.5: October 2, 2026**

* New

  * On Apple silicon, EMode's sparse direct solver is now rslab, a supernodal LU and complex-symmetric LDL\ :sup:`T` solver compiled into EMode. Mode solves return the same effective indices as with Intel MKL PARDISO. A mode solve with a PML is about 2.5 to 4.5 times faster (measured on an Apple silicon Mac against the previous release under Rosetta), and a solve without one takes the same time.
  * EMode runs natively on Apple silicon Macs, without Rosetta. There are now two Mac installers, ``EMode-<version>-Mac.pkg`` for Apple silicon and ``EMode-<version>-Mac-x86.pkg`` for Intel Macs. The Intel installer keeps MKL PARDISO. This is the last release with an Intel installer, and earlier versions stay available for download.
  * New :data:`settings` options, per profile: ``solver_threads`` caps the number of threads the sparse solver uses (0, the default, lets it choose, up to every core), and ``sparse_solver`` picks the solver (``'auto'``, ``'rslab'`` or ``'pardiso'``). The Linux, Windows and Intel Mac installers keep MKL PARDISO as their default, since it is still faster than rslab on x86 processors, and include rslab as ``sparse_solver='rslab'``. The ``EMODE_SOLVER_THREADS`` environment variable limits the thread count for every profile that does not set its own, and the 16-thread cap on the MKL thread count is gone.
  * The heat and electrostatic solves use the same solver.
  * Every installer except the Intel Mac one now meshes FEM cross-sections with the same version of the ``triangle`` mesher, so heat and electrostatic results no longer differ slightly between platforms. On Linux and Windows the mesh changes a little: the :doc:`Phase Shifter </examples/Phase_Shifter>` example's V\ :sub:`pi`\ L moves from 5.39 to 5.10 V·cm.
  * Full-vector finite-element mode solver, available with EMode\ :sup:`3D`. :data:`FEM` solves a cross-section on a triangle mesh that follows every material interface, with second-order elements, and refines the mesh where the modes need it. Boundaries, PMLs, expansion regions, bends, lossy and anisotropic materials (including crystals tilted out of the cross-section with ``theta``), and heater and electro-optic perturbations work as they do in the FDM, and FEM and FDM sections can meet at a junction. ``plot(mesh_display=True)`` draws the triangle mesh. See the new :doc:`FEM: SOI </examples/FEM_SOI>` example.
  * New :data:`solve` runs either mode solver. ``solver_method='FDM'`` or ``'FEM'`` is the same as calling :data:`FDM` or :data:`FEM`, and ``'default'`` follows the new ``solver`` setting.
  * New :data:`settings` option ``solver`` picks the mode solver for :data:`solve`, :data:`EME` and :data:`sweep`. Its default, ``'default'``, is the FDM in every session, so existing scripts solve as before. The FEM runs only when asked for, with ``solver='FEM'``, :data:`FEM` or ``solve(solver_method='FEM')``. Calling :data:`FDM` or :data:`FEM` sets ``solver`` to that method. The ``fem_*`` settings control the FEM mesh and its refinement.
  * :data:`report` names the mode solver on its wavelength line, for example ``Wavelength: 1550.0 nm    Solver: FEM``, and a saved CSV records it too.
  * Biaxial crystals. :data:`KTP` and :data:`LBO` are in the material database, each with three principal indices, its :math:`\chi^{(2)}` tensor and, for KTP, its electro-optic tensor. A third orientation angle, ``psi`` (in :class:`MaterialSpec` and :data:`add_material`), turns a crystal about its own z axis before ``theta`` and ``phi``, so a biaxial crystal can take any orientation. Omitted, ``psi`` is 0 and existing simulations are unchanged. See :class:`MaterialSpec` for the convention.
  * New :data:`settings` option ``include_scattering``: with ``include_scattering=True``, every solve of the profile (by :data:`FDM`, :data:`FEM`, :data:`solve`, :data:`EME` or :data:`sweep`) also computes the interfacial scattering loss of each rough shape. ``FDM(scattering=True)`` still does this for a single solve.
  * ``nonlinear=False`` on :data:`straight_section` or :data:`taper_section` removes a declared :math:`\chi^{(2)}` process, so the section propagates linearly again.
* Fixed

  * **Material loss now attenuates.** A lossy material (``loss=`` in dB/m, or a database material with an extinction coefficient) amplified the mode in :data:`EME`: a 200 µm lossy strip transmitted 110% of its power. Lossy modes now have an effective index with a negative imaginary part, and :data:`EME` attenuates them by exactly the reported loss. :data:`refractive_index`, :data:`permittivity` and plots still show n + jk. Profiles solved by an earlier release keep their old sign until they are solved again.
  * **Symmetric boundaries unfold correctly.** A mode solved with an 'S' or 'A' boundary was unfolded onto the full window with the same sign for every field component, but some components are odd under the mirror. Junctions between a folded and an unfolded section, the :math:`\chi^{(2)}` coupling of folded solves, plane-wave junctions and plots of unfolded fields were all affected. Each component now takes its physical mirror parity.
  * **A windowed port on a symmetry-folded profile couples correctly.** A port with ``window=`` on a profile solved with an 'S' or 'A' boundary left the mirrored half of its window at zero, so its junction was wrong wherever the window crossed the symmetry plane. Two ports folded the same way at different transverse offsets had the same problem.
  * The :math:`\chi^{(2)}` coupling of symmetry-folded solves (SHG, SFG, DFG, SPDC) used the pump's symmetry for a signal folded differently from the pump. It now matches a full-window solve.
  * :data:`chi2_spectrum` left the profiles it re-solved with no scattering data, so ``get('scattering_loss')`` and :data:`report` read zero after a scan. The re-solved profiles now keep their per-mode scattering loss.
  * **An FDM solve asked for more modes than a structure guides returns its lossy modes.** Past the guided and radiation modes, the solve returned modes with an effective index near 0, and at higher mode counts it failed with "array must not contain infs or NaNs". The next modes are now the lossy ones, with an imaginary effective index, ordered from least to most decay. Guided modes are unchanged.
  * The FDM solve returns the same modes on every run. Degenerate modes used to come back as a different mixture each time.
  * **FDM '0' walls are metal on all four sides.** The bottom wall was a magnetic wall half a cell outside the window, and ``field_to_solve='Ht'`` returned modes the ``'Et'`` solve did not. Both now return a metal waveguide's modes. Modes kept away from the walls by a cladding or a PML are unchanged. Modes that reach a wall move: the :doc:`EME: Taper </examples/EME_Taper>` example's printed indices change by up to 3e-4.
  * A taper whose etch mask is offset from the waveguide center re-centered the mask on every interpolated slice, so the geometry jumped to the center mid-taper. A misspelled :data:`shape` keyword now raises an error instead of being ignored.
  * A :data:`shape` stacked on a layer that came out empty, such as a fully etched layer, was placed half that layer's height too high. It now sits directly on top of it.
  * ``FDM(section=..., propagation_distance=...)`` failed on a straight or bend section, or any section whose cross-section does not change along its length.
  * :data:`group_index` crashed on an FDM profile.
  * A junction between two differently gridded sections (a confined port, a PML against a plain window, a different resolution or offset) resampled both modes onto a common grid smaller than either and shifted by half a cell. A confined port's S-matrix was off by up to 6e-2. The common grid now covers both sections exactly.
  * :data:`get` reads back every setting :data:`settings` accepts, including older aliases such as ``radius``. Before, only ``wavelength``, ``background_material`` and ``BC`` worked. :data:`inspect` lists every name :data:`get` can read and takes ``profile=``.
  * :data:`overlap` stores its result on the profile named by ``profile_b`` instead of always on the default profile, and no longer fails when the default profile has several wavelengths. The new ``get('overlaps')`` keeps one record per pair of modes, so overlaps no longer overwrite each other.
  * :data:`label_profile` works on a multi-wavelength profile.
  * ``FDM(verbose=False)`` still printed its progress. It is now quiet.
  * The ``mode_filter`` and ``fLanczos`` arguments of :data:`FDM` had no effect. They now reach the solver, and a bad value raises an error.
  * The ``eme_scattering`` option of :data:`settings` never had an effect. It is deprecated: it is still accepted, with a warning that it does nothing. Use ``EME_settings(apply_scattering=True)`` to apply scattering loss in :data:`EME`.
  * The ``permeability`` and ``fill_permeability`` arguments of :data:`shape` raised an unclear error. The error now explains that a shape's permeability comes from its material, as in ``material=MaterialProperties(n=1.5, mu=2.0)``.
  * A simulation name that is not a valid file name on every platform, such as ``'run:1'``, is rejected by :data:`init` and :data:`open` with an error that names the problem, instead of producing a simulation file that cannot be written on Windows.
  * :data:`FDM` failed on a multi-wavelength profile, from a wavelength list in :data:`settings` or from :data:`create_profile_set`. Each wavelength is now solved at its own wavelength and :data:`get` returns the results keyed by wavelength. :data:`EME` on a wavelength list in :data:`settings` failed too.
  * On a multi-wavelength profile, the results of :data:`get`, :data:`effective_area`, :data:`group_index`, :data:`orthogonality`, :data:`scattering`, :data:`confinement` and :data:`report` could not be indexed by wavelength: ``result[1550.0]`` raised a KeyError. They are now a read-only dict keyed by wavelength, in which ``result[1550]`` and ``result[1550.0]`` are the same entry. :data:`confinement` returns its dictionary of confinement factors per shape directly, as documented, instead of inside a one-element list, so a script that used ``confinement()[0]`` should drop the ``[0]``.
  * A material given by its permittivity, ``MaterialSpec(material=MaterialProperties(eps=...))``, ignored its ``theta`` and ``phi``, while its ``d`` tensor was rotated by them. Its permittivity now turns with it.
  * :data:`shape` with a single value for ``roughness_rms`` or ``correlation_length`` raised an error, although the documentation says a single value applies to all interfaces. It now does, and a list of any length other than two raises an error that names the argument.
  * A lossy anisotropic material rotated off its principal axes (``loss`` with ``theta``, ``phi`` or ``psi``) had its loss applied to every element of its index tensor, which made the loss depend on polarization. The loss is now applied to the diagonal only, as for the unrotated material.
  * :data:`heat` followed by a mode solve failed with an IndexError when a rotated anisotropic material had a nonzero ``dn_dT``. The heated index of such a material is now its index tensor shifted by ``dn_dT`` times the temperature change.
  * :data:`refractive_index` with an array of wavelengths failed for a rotated anisotropic material, and for exactly three wavelengths returned a wrong result. It now returns one 3x3 tensor per wavelength.

**1.0.4: September 24, 2026**

* New

  * Second-order nonlinear EME, available with EMode3D. A :data:`straight_section` or :data:`taper_section` takes ``nonlinear=`` with an ``SHGProcess``, ``SFGProcess``, or ``DFGProcess`` naming the process wavelengths. Quasi-phase matching is declared with ``poling_period`` (plus ``duty_cycle`` and ``qpm_order``) on the process, or built by hand from alternating ``inverted=True`` sections, the two routes agree.
  * A CW pump is declared with ``settings(excitation=Source(port, wavelength, mode, power, phase))``. :data:`EME` still returns the small-signal S-matrix, and now also solves the power-dependent response, available as a ``CircuitResponse`` from ``get('response')``, outgoing and incoming amplitudes at every port, radiated power per wavelength, and convergence. ``get('sources')`` returns the declared excitation.
  * :data:`chi2_spectrum` returns a nonlinear conversion spectrum (signal out over pump in, at every wavelength asked for) from a handful of mode solves. A :math:`\chi^{(2)}` spectrum oscillates too fast with the phase mismatch to interpolate, but what the coupled-mode equations consume (the coupling and the propagation constants) varies smoothly, so the modes are solved only where the mode list is still moving and the response is then evaluated point by point from interpolated coupling. Against a directly solved 13-point spectrum across a phase-matching peak, five solves reproduce every point to four decimals, sidelobes included. Quasi-phase-matched sections are included: the grating enters as a wavevector shift and a Fourier coefficient, neither of which depends on wavelength, so a poled section keeps its exact grating while its phase mismatch moves with the interpolated propagation constants.
  * ``sweep(key='wavelength', values=..., adaptive=True)`` does the same for an ordinary sweep. ``values`` keeps its meaning (the wavelengths you want results at) and ``adaptive`` changes only where the solver runs: modes are matched between neighboring solves through a phase-corrected overlap, and a bisection in wavelength adds solves until the mode list stops moving by more than ``tolerance``. Any stretch it could not resolve is reported in ``unconverged`` instead of raising.
  * Free-space excitation: :data:`free_space_field` declares a Gaussian beam launched into a port. The beam is projected onto that port's modes and drives the field plot through ``plot(excitation=name)`` or the plot window's Mode menu. :data:`free_space_field_diagnostics` returns the fraction of the beam's power the port's modes capture, and the solver warns when it is below 90%. ``tilt`` is the angle inside the medium the beam travels through.
  * Angled facet ports: :func:`make_angled_facet_port` tilts a port's cross-section about a hinge line, so a facet's reflection back into the guided mode falls off with tilt as it does physically (see :ref:`ports`). A facet cannot sit on a :data:`pwd_section` or on a profile with a PML. ``sweep(key='section, NAME, facet_angle')`` sweeps that tilt.
  * The solver warns at a facet junction when the waveguide's ``num_modes`` is too small to hold the deflected reflection and R + T under-runs.
  * Junctions whose two sides carry different numbers of modes (every junction between a waveguide section and a :data:`pwd_section`) now solve the mode-matching equations for the reflected and transmitted amplitudes jointly instead of eliminating the reflected ones first. The two closures coincide when the counts match, so taper and GDS staircases are unchanged. At a waveguide-to-free-space junction the reflection into the fundamental moves by 10-15% (down), the answer no longer depends on the order the two sections were declared, and declaring an angled facet at zero tilt no longer changes it.
  * Per-junction settings: a :data:`connect_ports` entry accepts a third element, ``JunctionOverride(junction_normalization=...)``, applying to that junction alone.
  * Field plots: the color scale is normalized to the excitation plane's field family, with a 'Norm' selector (vector or component), the log scale spans -60 dB to 0, an 'abs sum' cross-axis reduction.
  * ``plot(profile=...)`` renders a stored profile on a simulation that has EME sections declared. Previously the plotter always followed the sections.
  * :data:`get_fields` with no ``key`` returns all six E and H components.
  * :data:`material_explorer` with ``file_name=`` saves the figure without opening a window, like :data:`plot`.
  * Setting ``EMODE_NONINTERACTIVE=1`` makes every :data:`plot` build its figure and return instead of blocking on the window. ``EMODE_EMAIL`` and ``EMODE_PASSWORD`` log in without the login window, for unattended runs.
  * EMode prints a notice when it checks out a license and a newer release is available. It turns itself on once a release's installers are downloadable.
  * The default MKL thread count is capped at 16 (an explicit ``MKL_NUM_THREADS`` overrides this setting).
  * Second-order nonlinear coefficients (``d``) added for GaP, AlN, and InGaP, and for the new materials GaN, LiTaO3, and ZnSe, each with a citation, the BBO, GaAs, AlGaAs, LN, and LN_MgO entries are corrected and cited. :data:`d_matrix` with ``reference=True`` returns the citation. ``get('<material>')`` now includes ``property_refs``, the source of every non-optical and nonlinear value.
  * Electro-optic (Pockels) coefficients ``r`` for LN, LN_MgO, GaAs, InP, AlN, and GaN. :data:`electrostatic` derives the DC field from the solved potential, and :data:`FDM` then solves the biased waveguide through the r tensor (``include_static``), so a phase shifter's V\ :sub:`pi`\ L comes straight out of :data:`report`.
  * Thermal and electrical properties (``thermal_conductivity``, ``dn_dT``, ``eps_r_dc``, and ``resistivity`` for metals) filled in for every database material, plus the heater and electrode metals Au, Al, Cu, Ti, W, Cr, TiN, and NiCr with their optical constants at 1550 nm. The :doc:`Material Database </emodeguide/materials>` page tabulates every material's non-optical properties, :math:`\chi^{(2)}` and electro-optic coefficients, and their sources.
  * :data:`report` and :data:`plot` mark modes that live in the PML: the report gains a ``PML`` column and the plot's mode menu reads ``3, TE, PML``. The designation is available as ``PML_indices`` and ``window_confinement``.
  * New setting ``pml_seed_bool``: a PML simulation is first solved without its PML, and the eigensolver is then seeded with that fundamental mode, so the guided mode lands at index 0 without a hand-tuned ``max_effective_index``.
  * New website examples: :doc:`Nonlinear-EME: SHG </examples/EME_SHG>` (GaAs-on-insulator second-harmonic generation, straight and tapered, with both devices' conversion-efficiency spectra), :doc:`Nonlinear-EME: PPLN </examples/EME_PPLN>` (a periodically poled thin-film lithium niobate waveguide doubling a telecom TE pump, with propagation loss from sidewall and surface roughness), :doc:`EME: Angled Facet </examples/EME_Angled_Facet>` (a lensed-fiber Gaussian into an angled-facet taper, swept over facet tilt), :doc:`Heater </examples/Heater>` (a Pt heater above an SOI waveguide, with the power for a :math:`\pi` phase shift), and :doc:`Phase Shifter </examples/Phase_Shifter>` (Au electrodes beside an x-cut LNOI waveguide, with V\ :sub:`pi`\ L).
  * The :doc:`Variable Descriptions </emodeguide/variables>` page now explains how the simulation file is organized (top-level keys vs. the ``profiles`` dictionary, default and named profiles, multi-wavelength profile sets) and groups variables by where they live. :data:`inspect` is documented.

  * New website examples: :doc:`Adaptive Scan </examples/Adaptive_Scan>` (``sweep(adaptive=True)``, a fine wavelength spectrum from a sparse set of solves) and :doc:`Nonlinear-EME: DFG </examples/EME_DFG>`, difference-frequency generation in periodically poled lithium niobate, with two simultaneous ``Source`` excitations and a three-wavelength profile set.
  * A sweep or a :data:`chi2_spectrum` no longer prints the mesh and eigensolve of every wavelength it solves. One line for the scan replaces one pair per solve.
  * A :math:`\chi^{(2)}` section warns when its mode basis still contains PML modes: their large imaginary propagation constants make the coupled-mode solve stiff, and the warning names ``remove_pml_modes_bool``, which drops them.
  * ``get('response').power_vs_z(wavelength)`` returns the forward power against position along a :math:`\chi^{(2)}` section, from one solve. The coupled-amplitude ODE already integrates along z and used to discard the result, so a pump or second-harmonic power curve cost one full :data:`EME` per length. The forward amplitudes are now recorded after the driven solve converges and returned with the response, stitched across the slices of a refined taper so the curve reads as one. ``amplitude_vs_z`` gives the per-mode complex amplitudes behind it. Sampling is controlled by ``z_samples`` on the process (default 100 points per slice, 0 to switch it off).
  * :data:`plot` with ``plane='z-x'`` on a :math:`\chi^{(2)}` section draws the driven field. It uses the declared ``excitation`` rather than a unit mode, since conversion depends on pump power, and renders each slice from the amplitudes recorded along it, so the generated wavelength builds along the guide instead of stepping at slice boundaries. ``wavelength=`` picks which wavelength to show. Without a declared excitation the field shown is the small-signal response and the solver says so.
  * The coupled-amplitude ODE's default tolerances are ``solver_rtol=1e-6`` and ``solver_atol=1e-9``, with ``RK45`` as the default method. Pass ``solver_rtol``, ``solver_atol`` or ``solver_method`` on the process to override any of them. The explicit Runge-Kutta methods (``RK45``, ``RK23``, ``DOP853``) are the usable choices. The coupled amplitudes are complex, and SciPy's implicit solvers (``LSODA``, ``Radau``, ``BDF``) reject a complex initial condition.
* Fixed

  * :data:`scattering` corrupted the profile it had just reported on, so every later :data:`get` on that simulation failed. The same path also wrote into a material object returned by ``get('<material>')``.
  * ``get('scattering_loss')`` (and ``sweep(result='scattering_loss')``) returned the per-shape metadata dictionary instead of the loss, and raised an error when more than one shape carried roughness.
