Open a Simulation
-----------------

How to open an existing EMode simulation.

*This code example is licensed under the* `BSD 3-Clause License <../_static/LICENSE.html>`_.

.. tabs::

    .. code-tab:: python
        :caption: Python

        import emodeconnection as emc

        ## Run an initial session with a unique simulation name.

        # Set simulation parameters
        wavelength = 1970 # [nm] wavelength
        dx, dy = 10, 5 # [nm] resolution
        trench = 1200 # [nm] waveguide side trench width
        t_clad = 1200 # [nm] waveguide top/bot clad
        b_clad = 1500 # [nm] waveguide top/bot clad
        w_core = 1734 # [nm] waveguide core width
        h_core = 150 # [nm] waveguide core height
        h_slab = 20 # [nm] slab thickness in etched areas
        angle = 17 # [degrees] waveguide sidewall angle

        width = w_core + trench*2 # [nm] window width
        height = h_core + b_clad + t_clad # [nm] window height
        num_modes = 1 # [nm] number of modes
        boundary = 'TE'

        # Connect and initialize EMode
        em = emc.EMode(simulation_name = 'GaAs_SHG')

        # Settings
        em.settings(
            wavelength = wavelength,
            x_resolution = dx, y_resolution = dy,
            window_width = width, window_height = height,
            boundary_condition = boundary, num_modes = num_modes,
            background_material = "Air")

        # Draw shapes
        em.shape(name = "BOX", material = "SiO2", height = b_clad)
        em.shape(name = "core", material = "GaAs", sidewall_angle = angle,
            mask = w_core, height = h_core, etch_depth = h_core - h_slab)

        # Launch FDM solver
        em.FDM()
        em.report()
        em.close()

        ## The previous simulated can be opened again, modified, and saved with a new name.

        # Open existing simulation file
        em = emc.EMode(simulation_name = 'GaAs_SHG',
            open_existing = True, new_name = 'GaAs_SHG-TM')

        # Get the previous wavelength setting and convert it to the second harmonic wavelength
        wavelength = em.get('wavelength')/2
        n_eff = em.get('effective_index')

        # Update the settings
        em.settings(wavelength = wavelength,
            boundary_condition = 'TM', num_modes = 2,
            max_effective_index = n_eff[0])

        # Launch FDM solver
        em.FDM()
        em.report()
        em.close()

        ## When opening an existing file to only retrieve and plot data, a new simulation name is not needed since the simulation data will not be modified.

        # Plot from existing simulation file - pump mode
        em = emc.EMode(simulation_name = 'GaAs_SHG', open_existing = True)

        E_p = em.get_fields(key = ['Ex', 'Ey', 'Ez'])
        em.plot()
        em.close()

        # Plot from existing simulation file - signal mode
        em = emc.EMode(simulation_name = 'GaAs_SHG-TM', open_existing = True)

        E_s = em.get_fields(key = ['Ex', 'Ey', 'Ez'])
        TM_indices = em.get('TM_indices')
        em.plot(component = 'Ey', mode = TM_indices[0])
        em.close()

Dispersion Sweep
----------------

The sweep function is demonstrated to calculate dispersion of a waveguide. See for a comparison: J. A. Black, R. Streater, K. F. Lamee, D. R. Carlson, S.-P. Yu, and S. B. Papp, "Group-velocity-dispersion engineering of tantala integrated photonics," Opt. Lett. 46, 817 (2021).

*This code example is licensed under the* `BSD 3-Clause License <../_static/LICENSE.html>`_.

.. tabs::

    .. code-tab:: python
        :caption: Python

        import emodeconnection as emc
        import numpy as np

        ## Set simulation parameters
        dx, dy = 10, 10 # [nm] resolution
        h_core = 750 # [nm] waveguide core height
        b_clad = 2500 # [nm] waveguide top and bottom clad
        h_clad = 1500 # [nm] waveguide top and bottom clad
        w_core = h_core*1.25 # [nm] waveguide core width
        w_trench = 2500 # [nm] waveguide side trench width
        num_modes = 1 # [-] number of modes
        boundary = 'TE'

        wav_nm_ = np.arange(1000, 2001, 50) # [nm]

        ## Connect and initialize EMode
        em = emc.EMode(simulation_name = 'dispersion')

        ## Settings
        em.settings(
            x_resolution = dx, y_resolution = dy,
            window_width = w_core + w_trench*2,
            window_height = h_core + b_clad + h_clad,
            num_modes = num_modes, boundary_condition = boundary,
            background_material = 'Air')

        ## Draw shapes
        em.shape(name = 'BOX', material = 'SiO2', height = b_clad)
        em.shape(name = 'core', material = 'Ta2O5', width = w_core,
            height = h_core)

        ## Run wavelength sweep
        data = em.sweep(key = 'wavelength', values = wav_nm_,
            result = ['effective_index'])

        ## Close EMode
        em.close()

A separate script can be used to plot the results.

.. tabs::

    .. code-tab:: python
        :caption: Python

        import emodeconnection as emc
        from emodeconnection import constants
        import numpy as np
        from scipy.interpolate import UnivariateSpline

        ## Extract sweep results without an EMode license
        data = emc.get(variable = 'sweep_data', simulation_name = 'dispersion')

        ## Calculate dispersion
        ind = np.argsort(data['values'])
        n_eff_spl = UnivariateSpline(
            data['values'][ind], data['effective_index'][ind], s=0, k=4)

        n_eff_spl_2d = n_eff_spl.derivative(n = 2)
        wav_nm_fit = np.arange(800, 2501, 1) # [nm]
        D = -wav_nm_fit/constants.c*n_eff_spl_2d(wav_nm_fit)*1e12/1e-3 # [ps/nm/km]

        ## Plot
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
        from matplotlib import rc as mplrc

        fw, LW = 8/2.54, 0.5
        mplrc('font',**{'family':'sans-serif','size':7})
        mplrc('axes', linewidth=LW, axisbelow=True)
        mplrc('xtick', bottom=True, top=True, direction='in')
        mplrc('ytick', left=True, right=True, direction='in')
        mplrc('xtick.major', size=3, width=LW)
        mplrc('xtick.minor', size=1.5, width=LW)
        mplrc('ytick.major', size=3, width=LW)
        mplrc('figure',figsize=[fw, fw/2**0.5])

        fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1)
        ax.set_xlabel(u'Wavelength (\u03bcm)')
        ax.set_ylabel('GVD (ps/nm/km)', color = 'tab:blue')
        ax.axes.set_xscale('log')
        ax2 = ax.twinx()
        ax2.set_ylabel('Effective index', color = 'tab:red')
        ax.grid(visible=True, which='major', axis='both', linewidth=LW/2, color='gray', alpha=0.25)

        ax.plot(wav_nm_fit, D,
            color = 'tab:blue', marker = '', linestyle = '-',
            lw = LW*1.5)

        ax2.plot(wav_nm_fit, n_eff_spl(wav_nm_fit),
            color = 'tab:red', marker = '', linestyle = '--',
            lw = LW*1.5)

        ax2.plot(data['values'], data['effective_index'],
            color = 'tab:red', marker = 'o', linestyle = '',
            ms = 1.5, mec = 'k', mew = 0.2)

        ax.set_xlim([800, 2500])
        xticks_nm = np.array([1000, 1500, 2000, 2500])
        xticks_nm_minor = np.arange(800, 2500.1, 100)
        ax.set_xticks(xticks_nm_minor, labels=''*len(xticks_nm_minor), minor=True)
        ax.set_xticks(xticks_nm)
        ax.set_xticklabels(['%0.1f' % (x*1e-3) for x in xticks_nm])
        ax.set_ylim([0, 600])
        ax2.set_ylim([
            np.min(data['effective_index'])*0.98,
            np.max(data['effective_index'])*1.02])

        ax3 = ax.twiny()
        ax3.axes.set_xscale('log')
        ax3.set_xlim(ax.get_xlim())
        ax3.set_xlabel('Frequency (THz)')
        ax3.set_xticks(xticks_nm)
        ax3.set_xticklabels(['%0.0f' % x for x in constants.c/xticks_nm*1e-3])
        ax.set_zorder(ax2.get_zorder()+1)
        ax.patch.set_visible(False)

        fig.savefig('dispersion.png', dpi = 600, bbox_inches = 'tight')

.. figure:: https://docs.emodephotonix.com/_images/dispersion.png
    :width: 500
    :align: center
    :figwidth: 500



Adaptive Scan
-------------

Highlighted features: ``sweep(adaptive=True)`` for a fine wavelength spectrum from a sparse set of solves, and the ``tolerance`` that sets how many.

*This code example is licensed under the* `BSD 3-Clause License <../_static/LICENSE.html>`_.

.. tabs::

    .. code-tab:: python
        :caption: Python

        import sys
        import emodeconnection as emc
        import numpy as np
        from matplotlib import pyplot as plt

        ## Adaptive wavelength scanning: report a fine spectrum from a few solves.
        ## The scan places solves only where the mode list is still moving and
        ## interpolates the rest, so the cost follows how fast the modes change rather
        ## than how many points are asked for.

        ## Set simulation parameters
        dx, dy = 20, 10  # [nm] resolution: 22 cells across the core, symmetric about the fold
        w_core, h_core = 800, 220  # [nm] Si core
        clearance = 1500  # [nm] cladding on each side
        num_modes = 2  # [-] both guided across the band below

        wav_lo, wav_hi = 1500, 1600  # [nm]
        wavelengths = np.linspace(wav_lo, wav_hi, 201)  # [nm] where results are wanted

        ## Connect and initialize EMode
        em = emc.EMode(emode_cmd=sys.argv[1:], simulation_name='adaptive_scan')

        em.settings(
            wavelength=(wav_lo + wav_hi) / 2, x_resolution=dx, y_resolution=dy,
            window_width=w_core + 2 * clearance, window_height=h_core + 2 * clearance,
            num_modes=num_modes, boundary_condition='SS', background_material='SiO2')

        em.shape(name='clad', material='SiO2', height=clearance)
        em.shape(name='core', material='Si', width=w_core, height=h_core)

        ## How many solves the scan costs is set by `tolerance`, the largest mode-list
        ## change tolerated between neighboring solves -- not by the number of points.
        for tolerance in (1e-2, 1e-3, 5e-4):
            scan = em.sweep(key='wavelength', values=wavelengths, adaptive=True,
                            tolerance=tolerance, result=['effective_index'])
            n_solves = len(scan['solved_wavelengths'])
            print(f'tolerance {tolerance:.0e}: {n_solves:3d} solves for {len(wavelengths)} points'
                  f'  ({len(wavelengths) / n_solves:.0f}x fewer)')
            if scan['unconverged']:
                print(f'  unresolved intervals: {len(scan["unconverged"])}')

        ## The last scan above is the one kept. Mark where it actually solved.
        solved = np.sort(np.asarray(scan['solved_wavelengths']))
        n_eff = np.real(np.asarray(scan['effective_index']))

        em.settings(wavelength=1550)
        em.FDM()
        em.plot(component='Ex', mode=0)

        em.close()

        plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4.5))
        for m in range(num_modes):
            line, = plt.plot(scan['values'], n_eff[m], label=f'mode {m}')
            ## Bisection places the solves, so they are not generally grid points;
            ## mark them on the interpolant at the nearest reported wavelength.
            picked = np.clip(np.searchsorted(scan['values'], solved), 0, len(scan['values']) - 1)
            plt.plot(scan['values'][picked], n_eff[m][picked], 'o', ms=5,
                     color=line.get_color(), markerfacecolor='none')
        plt.xlabel('Wavelength (nm)')
        plt.ylabel('Effective index')
        plt.title(f'Adaptive scan: {len(solved)} solves, {len(scan["values"])} points reported')
        plt.legend()
        plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig('adaptive_scan.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

        ## Interpolation between solves is linear, so a scan is for reading values off,
        ## not for differentiating twice: a dispersion curve wants solves at every point.

Console output::

    EMode3D 1.0.7 - email

    tolerance 1e-02:   5 solves for 201 points  (40x fewer)
    Adaptive wavelength scan over 1500-1600 nm... completed in 7.1 sec
    tolerance 1e-03:   9 solves for 201 points  (22x fewer)
    Adaptive wavelength scan over 1500-1600 nm... completed in 16.3 sec

EME: Taper
----------

The simplest EMode example of an EME simulation.

*This code example is licensed under the* `BSD 3-Clause License <../_static/LICENSE.html>`_.

.. tabs::

    .. code-tab:: python
        :caption: Python

        import emodeconnection as emc

        ## Set simulation parameters
        wavelength = 1550 # [nm] wavelength
        dx, dy = 20, 10 # [nm] resolution: 22 cells across the core, symmetric about the fold
        h_core = 220 # [nm] waveguide core height
        h_clad = 1000 # [nm] waveguide top and bottom clad

        window_width = 4000
        window_height = h_core + h_clad*2

        num_modes = 10 # [-] number of modes
        BC = 'TE'

        ## Connect and initialize EMode
        em = emc.EMode(verbose = True)

        ## Settings
        em.settings(
            wavelength = wavelength, x_resolution = dx, y_resolution = dy,
            window_width = window_width, window_height = window_height,
            num_modes = num_modes, boundary_condition = BC,
            background_material = 'SiO2')

        ## Draw shapes
        em.shape(name = 'BOX', material = 'SiO2',
            height = h_clad)
        em.shape(name = 'core', material = 'Si',
            height = h_core, etch_depth = h_core)

        ## Launch FDM solver and label profiles
        em.shape(name = 'core', mask = 1000)
        em.FDM(profile = 'a')
        em.report()
        em.plot()

        em.shape(name = 'core', mask = 2000)
        em.FDM(profile = 'b')
        em.report()
        em.plot()

        ## Draw EME sections
        em.straight_section(
            profile = 'a',
            length = 2000)

        em.taper_section(
            profile = 'a', profile_end = 'b',
            length = 8000)

        em.straight_section(
            profile = 'b',
            length = 2000)

        ## Run EME and plot results
        em.EME()
        em.plot()
        em.plot_S_matrix()

        ## Close EMode
        em.close()

EME: Sweep
----------

In practice, a taper length needs to be optimized to ensure proper modal transmission and low loss. This example shows how the sweep function can be used to visualize the transmission of an EME taper simulation.

*This code example is licensed under the* `BSD 3-Clause License <../_static/LICENSE.html>`_.

.. tabs::

    .. code-tab:: python
        :caption: Python

        import emodeconnection as emc
        import numpy as np

        ## Set simulation parameters
        wavelength = 1550 # [nm] wavelength
        dx, dy = 20, 10 # [nm] resolution: 22 cells across the core, symmetric about the fold
        h_core = 220 # [nm] waveguide core height
        h_clad = 1000 # [nm] waveguide top and bottom clad

        window_width = 4000
        window_height = h_core + h_clad*2

        num_modes = 10 # [-] number of modes
        BC = 'TE'

        ## Connect and initialize EMode
        em = emc.EMode(simulation_name = 'taper', verbose = True)

        ## Settings
        em.settings(
            wavelength = wavelength, x_resolution = dx, y_resolution = dy,
            window_width = window_width, window_height = window_height,
            num_modes = num_modes, boundary_condition = BC,
            background_material = 'SiO2')

        ## Draw shapes
        em.shape(name = 'BOX', material = 'SiO2',
            height = h_clad)
        em.shape(name = 'core', material = 'Si',
        height = h_core, etch_depth = h_core)

        ## Launch FDM solver and label profiles
        em.shape(name = 'core', mask = 1000)
        em.label_profile(name = 'a') # skips solving the modes here

        em.shape(name = 'core', mask = 2000)
        em.label_profile(name = 'b') # skips solving the modes here

        ## Draw EME sections
        em.straight_section(
            profile = 'a',
            length = 2000)

        em.taper_section(name = 'taper',
            profile = 'a', profile_end = 'b',
            length = 8000)

        em.straight_section(
            profile = 'b',
            length = 2000)

        ## Run EME sweep
        data = em.sweep(key = 'section, taper, length',
            values = np.arange(0, 8001, 250),
            result = ['S_matrix'])

        ## Close EMode
        em.close()

While no figures are generated in the EMode script, a separate script can be used to plot the results.

.. tabs::

    .. code-tab:: python
        :caption: Python

        import emodeconnection as emc
        import numpy as np

        ## Extract sweep results without an EMode license
        data = emc.get(variable = 'sweep_data', simulation_name = 'taper')

        ## Plot
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
        from matplotlib import rc as mplrc

        fw, LW = 8/2.54, 0.5
        mplrc('font',**{'family':'sans-serif','size':7})
        mplrc('axes', linewidth=LW, axisbelow=True)
        mplrc('xtick', bottom=True, top=True, direction='in')
        mplrc('ytick', left=True, right=True, direction='in')
        mplrc('xtick.major', size=3, width=LW)
        mplrc('ytick.major', size=3, width=LW)
        mplrc('figure',figsize=[fw, fw/2**0.5])

        fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1)
        ax.set_xlabel('Taper length (nm)')
        ax.set_ylabel('Transmission (%)')
        ax.grid(visible=True, which='major', axis='both', linewidth=LW/2, color='gray', alpha=0.25)

        transmission = np.array([s.transmission() for s in data['S_matrix']])
        lines = []
        for kk in range(transmission.shape[-1]):
            line, = ax.plot(data['values'],
                100*np.abs(transmission[:,kk,0])**2,
                marker = '', linestyle = '-', lw = LW*1.5,
                label = r'Mode 0$\rightarrow$%d' % kk)
    
            lines.append(line)

        ax.set_xlim([
            np.min(data['values']),
            np.max(data['values'])])

        lg = ax.legend(handles = lines[0:1], loc = 'center right')
        lg.get_frame().set_linewidth(LW/2)
        lg.get_frame().set_edgecolor('k')
        ax.set_ylim([70, 101])
        fig.savefig('taper_1.png', dpi=600, bbox_inches='tight')

        lg = ax.legend(handles = lines[1:10], loc = 'upper right')
        lg.get_frame().set_linewidth(LW/2)
        lg.get_frame().set_edgecolor('k')
        ax.set_ylim([-1, 25])
        fig.savefig('taper_2.png', dpi=600, bbox_inches='tight')

EME: GDS
--------

To simulate more complex structures, a GDS import function is used to support any geometry that can be created on a mask GDS file. This example shows how an s-bend structure can be created in a GDS file, imported to EMode, and simulated as part of a directional coupler.

*This code example is licensed under the* `BSD 3-Clause License <../_static/LICENSE.html>`_.

First, the GDS is created.

.. tabs::

    .. code-tab:: python
        :caption: Python

        from phidl import CrossSection, Device
        import phidl.path as pp
        from phidl import quickplot as qp
        from phidl import set_quickplot_options
        from matplotlib import pyplot as plt

        ## Parameters
        width_wg = 0.6 # [um]
        gap_input = 2.0 # [um]
        gap_output = 0.3 # [um]
        L_bend = 6.0 # [um]

        ## Create the first CrossSection
        X1 = CrossSection()
        X1.add(width = width_wg,
            offset = -gap_input/2 - width_wg/2, layer = 1,
            name = 'wg1', ports = ('in1', 'out1'))

        X1.add(width = width_wg,
            offset = gap_input/2 + width_wg/2, layer = 1,
            name = 'wg2')

        ## Create the second CrossSection
        X2 = CrossSection()
        X2.add(width = width_wg,
            offset = -gap_output/2 - width_wg/2, layer = 1,
            name = 'wg1', ports = ('in2', 'out2'))

        X2.add(width = width_wg,
            offset = gap_output/2 + width_wg/2, layer = 1,
            name = 'wg2')

        ## Transition from first to second CrossSection
        Xtrans = pp.transition(cross_section1 = X1, cross_section2 = X2, width_type = 'sine')
        P3 = pp.straight(length = L_bend)
        WG_trans = P3.extrude(Xtrans)

        ## Place all CrossSection extrusions
        D = Device()
        wgt = D << WG_trans

        ## Quickplot to view and save the layout
        set_quickplot_options(show_ports = False, show_subports = False)
        qp(D)

        ax = plt.gca()
        ax.set_xlabel('x (\u03BCm)')
        ax.set_ylabel('y (\u03BCm)')
        # quickplot pads the view by 10 % of the bounding box; clip back to the
        # geometry. 'box' rather than the default 'datalim' so equal aspect is kept by
        # resizing the axes instead of re-widening the limits we just set.
        ax.set_aspect('equal', adjustable = 'box')
        ax.set_xlim(D.bbox[0][0], D.bbox[1][0])
        ax.set_ylim(D.bbox[0][1], D.bbox[1][1])

        plt.savefig('sbend.png', dpi = 300, bbox_inches = 'tight')

        ## Save gds file
        D.write_gds('sbend.gds')

.. figure:: https://docs.emodephotonix.com/_images/sbend.png
    :width: 500
    :align: center
    :figwidth: 500

Next, the directional coupler device is created and simulated for a short coupler length. The sweep function is used to optimize  the coupler length for 100 % coupling, and the propagation is re-plotted.

.. tabs::

    .. code-tab:: python
        :caption: Python

        import emodeconnection as emc
        from matplotlib import pyplot as plt
        import numpy as np

        ## Set simulation parameters
        wavelength = 1550 # [nm] wavelength
        dx, dy = 20, 10 # [nm] resolution: 22 cells across the core, symmetric about the fold
        h_core = 220 # [nm] waveguide core height
        h_clad = 1200 # [nm] waveguide top and bottom clad
        width_wg = 600 # [nm]
        gap = 300 # [nm]
        input_gap = 2000 # [nm]

        window_height = h_core + h_clad*2

        num_modes = 2 # [-] number of modes
        BC = 'TE-v'

        ## Connect and initialize EMode
        em = emc.EMode()

        ## Settings
        em.settings(
            wavelength = wavelength, x_resolution = dx, y_resolution = dy,
            window_height = window_height, num_modes = num_modes,
            boundary_condition = BC, background_material = 'SiO2')

        ## Draw shapes
        em.shape(name = 'BOX', material = 'SiO2',
            height = h_clad)

        em.shape(name = 'core', material = 'Si',
            height = h_core, etch_depth = h_core)

        ## Create profiles
        em.settings(window_width = 6200)
        em.label_profile(name = 'slab')

        em.settings(window_width = 2600)
        em.shape(name = 'core', mask = width_wg)
        em.label_profile(name = 'io_waveguide')

        em.settings(window_width = 2600)
        em.shape(name = 'core', mask = [width_wg, width_wg],
            mask_offset = [-gap/2-width_wg/2, gap/2+width_wg/2])
        em.label_profile(name = 'coupler')

        ## Draw EME sections
        em.straight_section(name = 'input',
            profile = 'io_waveguide', length = 1000,
            offset = input_gap/2 + width_wg/2)

        em.gds_section(name = 'sbend',
            gds_path = 'sbend.gds', profile = 'slab',
            layer_map = {'core': 1},
            length = 10e3) # modify length of gds

        em.straight_section(name = 'coupler',
            profile = 'coupler', length = 30e3)

        em.copy_section(section_name = 'sbend', mirror = True)

        em.straight_section(name = 'output',
            profile = 'io_waveguide', length = 1000,
            offset = -input_gap/2 - width_wg/2)

        ## Run EME and plot results
        em.EME()
        em.plot()

        ## Sweep the coupler length and plot results
        data = em.sweep(key = 'section, coupler, length',
            values = np.arange(0, 200.1e3, 10000),
            result = ['S_matrix'])

        transmission = np.array([s.transmission() for s in data['S_matrix']])
        plt.plot(data['values']*1e-3, np.abs(transmission[:,0,0])**2*100)
        plt.xlabel("Coupler length (\u03BCm)")
        plt.ylabel("Transmission (%)")
        plt.autoscale(enable = True, axis = 'x', tight = True)
        plt.ylim([0,100])
        plt.savefig('transmission_plot.png', dpi = 300, bbox_inches = 'tight')

        ## Plot final design for 100 % coupler
        em.straight_section(name = 'coupler', length = 180e3)
        em.EME()
        em.plot()

        ## Close EMode
        em.close()

EME: Angled Facet
-----------------

Coupling a lensed-fiber Gaussian beam through a tapered, angled-facet output, and how much an
angled facet suppresses back-reflection.

*This code example is licensed under the* `BSD 3-Clause License <../_static/LICENSE.html>`_.

.. tabs::

    .. code-tab:: python
        :caption: Python

        import sys
        import numpy as np
        import emodeconnection as emc
        from emodeconnection import make_angled_facet_port
        from matplotlib import pyplot as plt

        ## Set simulation parameters
        wavelength = 780  # [nm] wavelength
        dx, dy = 20, 20  # [nm] resolution
        h_core = 300  # [nm] waveguide core height (SiN)
        clad = 1000  # [nm] waveguide cladding (SiO2)
        w_narrow = 1200  # [nm] narrow (input) waveguide width
        w_wide = 3000  # [nm] wide (facet) waveguide width
        window_width = w_wide + clad * 2  # [nm]
        window_height = h_core + clad * 2  # [nm]
        core_center = (0, window_height / 2)  # [nm]
        num_modes = 10  # [-]
        BC = '00'

        ## Part 1: Tilting the facet throws the reflection
        ## into higher order modes, so the fundamental mode
        ## reflection falls sharply with angle.
        em = emc.EMode(emode_cmd=sys.argv[1:], simulation_name='facet_sweep')

        em.settings(
            wavelength=wavelength, x_resolution=dx, y_resolution=dy,
            window_width=window_width, window_height=window_height,
            num_modes=num_modes, boundary_condition=BC,
            background_material='SiO2')

        em.shape(name='BOX', material='SiO2', height=clad)
        em.shape(name='core', material='Ta2O5', height=h_core, etch_depth=h_core, mask=w_wide)
        em.label_profile(name='wide')

        ## The facet re-references the waveguide's right-hand port to a tilted plane.
        ## Renaming it from 'right' to 'out' must be carried into connect_ports.
        em.straight_section(
            name='wg', profile='wide', length=2e3,
            ports=[make_angled_facet_port('out', 'right', pivot_angle=0)])

        em.pwd_section(
            name='gap', length=1e3, material='Air',
            window=(window_width * 2, window_height * 2),
            offset=core_center, num_modes=1024)

        em.connect_ports(pairs=[('wg.out', 'gap.left')])

        ## Sweep the facet tilt and keep the S-matrix at each angle.
        tilts = np.arange(0, 12.1, 1)  # [deg]
        data = em.sweep(key='section, wg, facet_angle', values=tilts, result='S_matrix')

        ## Reflection from the fundamental into every guided mode: the tilt steers power
        ## into the higher-order modes. R + T is printed as a check that the modal basis is large enough.
        reflection = np.array([np.abs(s.reflection(0))[:num_modes, 0] ** 2
                               for s in data['S_matrix']])
        for tilt, s in zip(tilts, data['S_matrix']):
            budget = (np.abs(s.reflection(0))[:, 0] ** 2).sum() + \
                     (np.abs(s.transmission(0, 1))[:, 0] ** 2).sum()
            print(f'tilt {tilt:4.1f} deg: R + T = {budget * 100:5.1f} %')

        for m in range(num_modes):
            plt.plot(tilts, 10*np.log10(reflection[:, m]), marker='o', ms=3, label=f'mode {m}')
        plt.xlabel('Facet tilt (degrees)')
        plt.ylabel('Reflection from the fundamental (dB)')
        # plt.yscale('log')
        plt.ylim(top=0, bottom=-60)
        plt.autoscale(enable=True, axis='x', tight=True)
        plt.legend(fontsize=8, ncol=2)
        plt.grid(True, which='both', alpha=0.3)
        plt.savefig('facet_reflection_vs_tilt.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

        em.close()

        ## Part 2: a lensed fiber coupling in, through an adiabatic taper to an angled
        ## output facet. A free-space field launches a Gaussian beam at the input.
        em2 = emc.EMode(emode_cmd=sys.argv[1:], simulation_name='facet_coupling')

        em2.settings(
            wavelength=wavelength, x_resolution=dx, y_resolution=dy,
            window_width=window_width*2, window_height=window_height,
            num_modes=num_modes, boundary_condition=BC,
            background_material='SiO2')

        em2.shape(name='BOX', material='SiO2', height=clad)
        em2.shape(name='core', material='Ta2O5', height=h_core, etch_depth=h_core, mask=w_narrow)
        em2.label_profile(name='narrow')
        em2.shape(name='core', mask=w_wide)
        em2.label_profile(name='wide')

        em2.pwd_section(
            name='fiber_gap', length=200, material='Air',
            window=(window_width * 2, window_height * 2), offset=core_center, num_modes=1024)

        em2.taper_section(
            name='taper', profile='narrow', profile_end='wide', length=20e3,
            ports=[make_angled_facet_port('out', 'right', pivot_angle=10)])

        em2.pwd_section(
            name='out_gap', length=2e3, material='Air',
            window=(window_width * 2, window_height * 2),
            offset=core_center, num_modes=1024)

        em2.connect_ports(pairs=[('taper.out', 'out_gap.left')])

        ## gaussian_field takes the field 1/e radius, which is the intensity FWHM
        ## divided by sqrt(2 ln 2)
        fwhm = 600  # [nm]
        waist = fwhm / np.sqrt(2 * np.log(2))

        em2.free_space_field(
            name='fiber', port='fiber_gap.left',
            # name='fiber', port='left',
            waist=waist, center=core_center, wavelength=wavelength)

        em2.EME()

        ## How much of the beam's power the input port's modes capture; the rest radiates
        ## away uncoupled and is not in the S-matrix.
        report = em2.free_space_field_diagnostics(name='fiber')
        print(report)

        ## 'section' scales each section by its own peak, so the beam spreading in
        ## the free-space gaps stays visible next to the much brighter guided mode
        em2.plot(
            excitation='fiber', component='Ex', plot_function='abs', plane='z-x',
            normalization='section')

        ## Close EMode
        em2.close()

EME: Grating Coupler
--------------------

A shallow-etch silicon grating coupler: how much of the guided light it sends up toward a fiber, how
much is lost to the substrate, and the fiber angle that couples best.

The grating is uniform across its width, so it is solved as a slab, with a window two cells wide and
periodic in x. A PML above and below absorbs the light the grating radiates once it has left the
window. That light is carried by the lossy modes of each cross-section, so the basis needs many of
them (100 here). The junctions between the etched and unetched cross-sections conserve power at any
number of modes, so what is transmitted, reflected and radiated adds up to the power launched.

A monitor, a plane inside the circuit, samples the field 1 um above the silicon.
``monitor_coupling()`` gives its overlap with a tilted Gaussian beam (a 10.4 um fiber mode here),
and a ``sweep()`` over the beam's angle reuses the solved field, so it costs no further solve. By
reciprocity the same number is the coupling from the fiber into the waveguide.

*This code example is licensed under the* `BSD 3-Clause License <../_static/LICENSE.html>`_.

.. tabs::

    .. code-tab:: python
        :caption: Python

        import sys
        import numpy as np
        import emodeconnection as emc
        from matplotlib import pyplot as plt

        ## Set simulation parameters
        wavelength = 1550  # [nm] wavelength
        dx, dy = 20, 20  # [nm] resolution
        h_core = 220  # [nm] silicon thickness
        etch = 70  # [nm] grating etch depth
        period = 630  # [nm] grating period
        fill = 0.5  # [-] unetched fraction of each period
        num_periods = 20  # [-]
        h_box = 2000  # [nm] buried oxide
        h_air = 2000  # [nm] air above the silicon
        lead = 2000  # [nm] unetched waveguide before and after the grating
        mfd = 10.4e3  # [nm] fiber mode field diameter
        num_modes = 100  # [-] enough for the radiated light, see below

        ## The grating is uniform along x, so it is solved as a slab: a window two
        ## cells wide and periodic in x. A PML above and below absorbs the light the
        ## grating radiates once it has left the window, so the lossy modes in the
        ## basis carry the radiation.
        em = emc.EMode(emode_cmd=sys.argv[1:], simulation_name='grating_coupler')

        em.settings(
            wavelength=wavelength, x_resolution=dx, y_resolution=dy,
            window_width=2 * dx, window_height=h_box + h_core + h_air,
            num_modes=num_modes, boundary_condition='0P',
            pml_NSEW_bool=[1, 1, 0, 0], num_pml_layers=10,
            background_material='Air')

        em.shape(name='BOX', material='SiO2', height=h_box)
        em.shape(name='core', material='Si', height=h_core)
        em.label_profile(name='unetched')

        em.shape(name='core', material='Si', height=h_core - etch)
        em.label_profile(name='etched')

        ## Draw EME sections: a lead, the periods, and a lead out
        em.straight_section(name='lead_in', profile='unetched', length=lead)
        em.straight_section(name='gap', profile='etched', length=period * (1 - fill))
        em.straight_section(name='tooth', profile='unetched', length=period * fill)
        for _ in range(num_periods - 1):
            em.copy_section(section_name='gap')
            em.copy_section(section_name='tooth')
        em.straight_section(name='lead_out', profile='unetched', length=lead)

        em.EME()

        ## A monitor 1 um above the silicon, centered on the grating
        z_center = lead + num_periods * period / 2
        em.monitor(name='fiber_plane', w=z_center, y=h_box + h_core + 1000)

        ## Where the power goes, for 1 W in the fundamental mode
        S = em.get('S_matrix')
        T = np.abs(S.transmission(0, 1)[0, 0]) ** 2
        R = np.abs(S.reflection(0)[0, 0]) ** 2
        up = em.monitor_field('fiber_plane').power_through_plane
        print(f'transmitted: {T * 100:.1f} %')
        print(f'reflected: {R * 100:.1f} %')
        print(f'radiated up through the monitor: {up * 100:.1f} %')
        print(f'the rest, mostly into the substrate: {(1 - T - R - up) * 100:.1f} %')

        ## Coupling to a fiber at each tilt: the solved field is reused, only the
        ## overlap with the tilted Gaussian is evaluated again
        angles = np.arange(0, 25.1, 1)  # [deg]
        data = em.sweep(key='angle', values=angles, result='monitor_coupling',
                        monitor='fiber_plane', beam=dict(mode_field_diameter=mfd))
        coupling = np.asarray(data['monitor_coupling'])
        best = angles[np.argmax(coupling)]
        print(f'best fiber angle: {best:.0f} deg, coupling {10 * np.log10(coupling.max()):.2f} dB')

        plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
        plt.plot(angles, 10 * np.log10(coupling), marker='o', ms=3)
        plt.xlabel('Fiber angle (degrees)')
        plt.ylabel('Coupling to the fiber (dB)')
        plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        plt.savefig('grating_coupling_vs_angle.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

        ## The field along the grating: the guided mode decays as it radiates, up
        ## toward the fiber and down into the substrate, at the grating's angle
        em.plot(component='Ex', plane='z-y', plot_function='real')

        em.close()

EME: S-Bend
-----------

An S-bend moves a waveguide sideways. Here a 500 x 220 nm Si wire in SiO2 at 1550 nm is shifted by 2 um with two ``bend_section``\ s of the same radius and opposite ``sweep_angle``. The S-bend is solved at several radii, with the two bends joined and with a short straight between them.

Highlighted features: ``bend_section`` with a signed ``sweep_angle``, and ``plot(view='layout')`` drawing the field where the layout places each section.

A bend pushes its mode toward the outside of the curve, so the loss comes from the mode mismatch at each junction, and at the joint between the two bends the mode has to move from one side of the guide to the other. The loss falls quickly as the radius grows. At the tightest radius a short straight between the bends lowers the loss noticeably, since the mode passes through a centered straight mode on its way across. At larger radii the mode barely moves, and the straight makes little difference.

The windows have metal walls and no PML, so the power a junction scatters stays in the window's modes and the example measures the junction loss, not radiation. A bend tight enough to radiate needs a PML on its outer wall, as in :doc:`Bend Mode Solvers <Bend_Solvers>`.

*This code example is licensed under the* `BSD 3-Clause License <../_static/LICENSE.html>`_.

.. tabs::

    .. code-tab:: python
        :caption: Python

        import sys
        import time
        import numpy as np
        import emodeconnection as emc
        from matplotlib import pyplot as plt

        ## An S-bend that shifts a Si wire sideways by 2 um, built from two circular
        ## bends of opposite curvature. Its loss is compared for three radii, and with
        ## and without a short straight between the two bends.

        ## Set simulation parameters
        wavelength = 1550  # [nm] wavelength
        dx, dy = 20, 20  # [nm] resolution
        w_core = 500  # [nm] waveguide core width
        h_core = 220  # [nm] waveguide core height
        h_clad = 1090  # [nm] cladding below and above the core
        window_width = 4000  # [nm]
        window_height = h_core + 2*h_clad  # [nm]
        num_modes = 32  # [-] number of modes

        shift = 2000  # [nm] lateral offset of the S-bend
        radii = [20000, 10000, 5000]  # [nm] bend radii, the last one is plotted
        lead = 1000  # [nm] straight input and output
        straight_lengths = [0, 1000]  # [nm] straight between the two bends, 0 for none

        def solve_sbends(straight_length):
            """Solve the S-bend at every radius, with `straight_length` between its bends."""
            name = 'sbend' if straight_length == 0 else 'sbend_straight'
            em = emc.EMode(emode_cmd=sys.argv[1:], simulation_name=name)
            em.settings(
                wavelength=wavelength, x_resolution=dx, y_resolution=dy,
                window_width=window_width, window_height=window_height,
                num_modes=num_modes, boundary_condition='00', background_material='SiO2')
            em.shape(name='BOX', material='SiO2', height=h_clad)
            em.shape(name='core', material='Si', height=h_core, etch_depth=h_core, mask=w_core)
            em.label_profile(name='wg')

            rows = []
            for radius in radii:
                ## Two arcs of opposite sweep shift the guide by `shift`
                ## over 2*R*sin(angle) along z, plus the straight between them
                angle = np.arccos(1 - shift / (2 * radius))  # [rad]
                em.straight_section(name='input', profile='wg', length=lead)
                em.bend_section(name='bend_1', profile='wg', radius=radius, sweep_angle=angle)
                if straight_length > 0:
                    em.straight_section(name='middle', profile='wg', length=straight_length)
                em.bend_section(name='bend_2', profile='wg', radius=radius, sweep_angle=-angle)
                em.straight_section(name='output', profile='wg', length=lead)

                start = time.time()
                S = em.EME()
                elapsed = time.time() - start

                ## Transmission of the fundamental mode, and the power that leaves
                ## through every mode of both ports (each mode weighted by its power)
                T = np.abs(S.block('right', 'left')[0, 0]) ** 2
                launched = S.block(['left', 'right'], 'left')[:, 0]
                balance = np.sum(S.mode_power * np.abs(launched) ** 2) / S.mode_power[0]
                z_length = 2 * radius * np.sin(angle) + straight_length
                rows.append((radius, angle, z_length, T, balance, elapsed))

            if straight_length == 0:
                ## The field of the tightest S-bend, drawn where the layout places it
                em.plot(component='Ex', plot_function='abs', plane='z-x', view='layout',
                        file_name='sbend_field', file_type='png')
            em.close()
            return rows

        results = {s: solve_sbends(s) for s in straight_lengths}

        ## Print the loss of every S-bend
        print(f'\n{"between":>8s}{"R (um)":>8s}{"angle (rad)":>13s}{"z length (um)":>15s}'
              f'{"T":>10s}{"loss (dB)":>11s}{"power out":>11s}{"time (s)":>10s}')
        for straight_length, rows in results.items():
            for radius, angle, z_length, T, balance, elapsed in rows:
                print(f'{straight_length * 1e-3:>5.1f} um{radius * 1e-3:>8.1f}{angle:>13.4f}'
                      f'{z_length * 1e-3:>15.3f}{T:>10.6f}{-10 * np.log10(T):>11.4f}'
                      f'{balance:>11.5f}{elapsed:>10.1f}')

        ## Plot the loss against the bend radius
        plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4.5))
        for straight_length, rows in results.items():
            label = 'bends joined' if straight_length == 0 else f'{straight_length * 1e-3:.0f} um straight between'
            plt.semilogy([r[0] * 1e-3 for r in rows], [-10 * np.log10(r[3]) for r in rows],
                         marker='o', label=label)
        plt.xlabel('Bend radius (μm)')
        plt.ylabel('S-bend loss (dB)')
        plt.title(f'S-bend with a {shift * 1e-3:.0f} μm offset')
        plt.legend()
        plt.grid(True, which='both', alpha=0.3)
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig('sbend_loss_vs_radius.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

EME: Y-Branch
-------------

A Y-branch splits one guide into two. Here a 500 x 220 nm Si wire in SiO2 at 1550 nm splits into two 500 nm cores that separate over 15 um. The splitter is drawn as two halves of the input core that widen and move apart, so it is a ``taper_section`` between two profiles of two cores each. Each output guide is its own section, wired to a window over its core on the splitter's end, so the circuit branches rather than running from one end to the other. A real tip cannot come to a point, so the two halves start 100 nm apart, about the smallest gap a lithography process resolves.

Highlighted features: a ``Port`` with a ``window`` on each core of a taper's end, ``connect_ports`` to wire a branching circuit, and ``plot(view='layout')``, which reconstructs the field arm by arm, draws each arm where the layout places it, and marks the ports with thick lines.

The light splits evenly between the two outputs, by symmetry. Most of the loss comes from the blunt tip: the input mode meets an abrupt gap where its field is strongest, which scatters and reflects part of the light, so a finite tip costs a few tenths of a dB that an ideal sharp tip would not. A narrower gap lowers the loss, which is why fabricated Y-branches push the tip to the limit of the process. The abrupt step also scatters into many modes, so the splitter keeps more modes than a smooth taper would need.

The splitter is a staircase of cross-sections, and its slicing decides how much it reflects. The tip, where the mode changes fastest, is sliced finely. Elsewhere the steps are kept shorter than half a wavelength in the guide, since steps of equal length a little longer than that form a grating whose reflections add up. Solving the splitter on its own, with every mode kept, checks that the slicing is fine enough.

The window has metal walls and ``boundary_condition='00'``. The structure is symmetric about x = 0, but a pair of masks is not yet recognized as symmetric, so a fold is not applied to it.

*This code example is licensed under the* `BSD 3-Clause License <../_static/LICENSE.html>`_.

.. tabs::

    .. code-tab:: python
        :caption: Python

        import sys
        import time
        import numpy as np
        import emodeconnection as emc
        from emodeconnection import Port, Bounds

        ## A Si wire Y-branch: one 500 nm guide splits into two that separate to
        ## 2.5 um apart over 15 um, and each continues as its own output guide. The
        ## splitter is a taper between two profiles of two cores, and each output
        ## guide is wired to its own window on the splitter's end.

        ## Set simulation parameters
        wavelength = 1550  # [nm] wavelength
        dx, dy = 50, 50  # [nm] resolution
        w_core = 500  # [nm] waveguide core width
        h_core = 220  # [nm] waveguide core height
        h_clad = 1090  # [nm] cladding below and above the core
        d_arm = 1250  # [nm] each output guide's distance from the axis
        tip_gap = 100  # [nm] the gap between the two halves at the tip, the smallest a lithography resolves
        window_width = 4 * d_arm  # [nm] the splitter's window, two output windows wide
        window_height = h_core + 2*h_clad  # [nm]
        num_modes = 24  # [-] number of modes in the splitter

        tip_length = 1500  # [nm] where the two halves are closest
        split_length = 15000  # [nm] the whole splitter, tip included
        arm_length = 3000  # [nm]
        num_arm_modes = 4  # [-] number of modes in each output guide

        ## A real tip cannot come to a point, so the two halves start tip_gap apart.
        ## At the tip the two halves have just come apart, and the mode changes faster
        ## than anywhere else, so the tip gets its own, more finely sliced, section. The
        ## two sections of the splitter are each sliced into steps shorter than half a
        ## wavelength in the guide, so the steps cannot reflect in phase.
        tip_settings = {'schedule_change_per_slice': 0.001, 'schedule_max_slices': 320}
        split_settings = {'schedule_change_per_slice': 0.005, 'schedule_max_slices': 320}

        def halves(z):
            """Width and center of each of the two cores, a distance z along the splitter.

            At the tip the two halves fill the input guide's width but for a gap of
            tip_gap between them, and they widen and move apart linearly from there.
            """
            t = z / split_length
            w0, c0 = (w_core - tip_gap)/2, (w_core + tip_gap)/4
            return w0 + t * (w_core - w0), c0 + t * (d_arm - c0)

        def start(name):
            """Open a session with the input guide and the splitter's three cross-sections."""
            em = emc.EMode(emode_cmd=sys.argv[1:], simulation_name=name)
            em.settings(
                wavelength=wavelength, x_resolution=dx, y_resolution=dy,
                window_width=window_width, window_height=window_height,
                num_modes=num_modes, boundary_condition='00', background_material='SiO2')
            em.shape(name='BOX', material='SiO2', height=h_clad)
            em.shape(name='core', material='Si', height=h_core, etch_depth=h_core, mask=w_core)
            em.label_profile(name='input')

            ## At z = 0 the input guide meets the blunt tip: two halves tip_gap apart
            for label, z in (('y_start', 0), ('y_tip', tip_length), ('y_end', split_length)):
                width, center = halves(z)
                em.shape(name='core', mask=[width, width], mask_offset=[-center, center])
                em.label_profile(name=label)

            em.straight_section(name='input', profile='input', length=1000)
            em.taper_section(name='tip', profile='y_start', profile_end='y_tip',
                             length=tip_length, settings=tip_settings)
            return em

        ## Part 1: the splitter on its own, ending on the full window. Every mode of the
        ## window is kept, so the power that leaves through its two ports is the check
        ## that the splitter is resolved.
        em = start('y_splitter')
        em.taper_section(name='split', profile='y_tip', profile_end='y_end',
                         length=split_length - tip_length, settings=split_settings)
        start_time = time.time()
        S = em.EME()
        splitter_time = time.time() - start_time
        launched = S.block(['left', 'right'], 'left')[:, 0]
        splitter_balance = np.sum(S.mode_power * np.abs(launched) ** 2) / S.mode_power[0]
        splitter_T = np.abs(S.block('right', 'left')[0, 0]) ** 2
        em.close()

        ## Part 2: the Y-branch. A window over each core on the splitter's end is its
        ## own port, and each output guide is connected to one of them.
        em = start('y_branch')
        window = lambda x: Bounds(window_width=2 * d_arm, window_height=window_height, offset=(x, 0.0))
        em.taper_section(
            name='split', profile='y_tip', profile_end='y_end',
            length=split_length - tip_length, settings=split_settings,
            ports=[Port(name='arm_1', side='right', window=window(d_arm)),
                   Port(name='arm_2', side='right', window=window(-d_arm))])

        em.settings(window_width=2 * d_arm, num_modes=num_arm_modes)
        em.shape(name='core', mask=w_core, mask_offset=0)
        em.label_profile(name='arm')
        em.straight_section(name='arm_1', profile='arm', length=arm_length)
        em.straight_section(name='arm_2', profile='arm', length=arm_length)
        em.connect_ports(pairs=[('input.right', 'tip.left'), ('tip.right', 'split.left'),
                                ('split.arm_1', 'arm_1.left'), ('split.arm_2', 'arm_2.left')])

        start_time = time.time()
        S = em.EME()
        branch_time = time.time() - start_time

        ## Transmission into the fundamental mode of each output guide, the reflection
        ## into every mode of the input, and the power that leaves through every port
        T_1 = np.abs(S.block('arm_1.right', 'input.left')[0, 0]) ** 2
        T_2 = np.abs(S.block('arm_2.right', 'input.left')[0, 0]) ** 2
        ## mode_power holds the power each mode carries, in the order of the rows of S
        column = S.port_slices[S.port_index('input.left')].start
        launched = np.abs(S.data[:, column]) ** 2 * S.mode_power / S.mode_power[column]
        power_out = np.sum(launched)
        reflection = np.sum(launched[S.port_slices[S.port_index('input.left')]])

        print(f'\nsplitter alone: T into the even mode {splitter_T:.5f}, '
              f'power out {splitter_balance:.5f}, {splitter_time:.1f} s')
        print(f'Y-branch: {branch_time:.1f} s')
        print(f'output 1: {T_1:.5f}')
        print(f'output 2: {T_2:.5f}')
        print(f'split ratio (1/total): {T_1 / (T_1 + T_2):.5f}')
        print(f'excess loss: {-10 * np.log10(T_1 + T_2):.4f} dB')
        print(f'reflection: {reflection:.1e}')
        print(f'power out of every port: {power_out:.5f}')

        ## The field, drawn where the layout places each section, with the ports
        em.plot(component='Ex', plot_function='abs', plane='z-x', view='layout',
                file_name='y_branch_field', file_type='png')
        em.close()

     completed in 40.0 sec

EME: TFLN Ring Resonator
------------------------

A racetrack ring resonator in x-cut thin-film lithium niobate: the through-port spectrum over a few
free spectral ranges, with the free spectral range, extinction and loaded quality factor of each
resonance, and the field around the ring on resonance.

The ring is a straight coupler, where the bus and the ring run side by side, two half-circle
``bend_section``\ s and a straight back side, closed on itself with ``connect_ports``. Windowed ports
give the coupler's bus and ring arms their own ports, so the ring can be closed while the bus stays
open. ``check_layout()`` confirms the loop closes before anything is solved.

The crystal is fixed on the chip, so along each bend the guide sees it turn: the extraordinary axis
lies across the guide at the ends of a half circle and along it in the middle. Each bend is sliced
along its heading and every slice is solved in its own frame. The crystal turns in steps from slice
to slice, which costs a little power in each half circle, so the bends are refined more finely than
the default (``overlap_variation=0.003``).

The spectrum comes from ``sweep(method='interpolated')``: the circuit is refined once, its
cross-sections are solved at a few wavelengths, and the S-matrix at each of the 2000 wavelengths is
rebuilt from them, so the sweep costs a few solves rather than 2000. The resonance wavelengths agree
with the same refined circuit solved directly to better than 0.001 nm. The depth of a resonance is more
sensitive, since near critical coupling it amplifies small differences in the coupling and the
round-trip loss.

The circuit is then refined and solved directly at the middle resonance, with the wavelength set on
both labeled profiles, and ``plot(view='layout')`` draws the field of each section where the layout
places it: the light the bus couples in builds up around the ring. Refined at that wavelength, the
circuit's resonance moves by about 0.02 nm, a quarter of its width, so the ring is close to its peak.

*This code example is licensed under the* `BSD 3-Clause License <../_static/LICENSE.html>`_.

.. tabs::

    .. code-tab:: python
        :caption: Python

        import sys
        import numpy as np
        import emodeconnection as emc
        from emodeconnection import MaterialSpec, Port, Bounds
        from matplotlib import pyplot as plt

        ## Set simulation parameters
        wavelength = 1550  # [nm] center wavelength
        dx, dy = 50, 50  # [nm] resolution
        h_film = 600  # [nm] lithium niobate film thickness
        etch = 400  # [nm] ridge etch depth
        w_core = 1200  # [nm] ridge width
        h_box = 1000  # [nm] buried oxide
        window_height = 2600  # [nm]
        gap = 300  # [nm] bus to ring gap
        radius = 30e3  # [nm] bend radius
        coupler_length = 20e3  # [nm] straight coupling length
        num_modes = 4  # [-]

        ## The ring is a racetrack: a straight coupler where the bus and the ring
        ## run side by side, two half-circle bends and a straight back side. The
        ## x-cut crystal stays fixed on the chip, so along each bend the guide sees
        ## it turn, and every slice of a bend is solved in its own frame.
        em = emc.EMode(emode_cmd=sys.argv[1:], simulation_name='tfln_ring')

        x_cut = MaterialSpec(material='LN_MgO', theta=np.pi / 2)

        em.settings(
            wavelength=wavelength, x_resolution=dx, y_resolution=dy,
            window_width=4000, window_height=window_height,
            num_modes=num_modes, boundary_condition='00',
            background_material='Air')

        em.shape(name='BOX', material='SiO2', height=h_box)
        em.shape(name='core', material=x_cut, height=h_film, etch_depth=etch, mask=w_core)
        em.label_profile(name='ring')

        ## The coupler's cross-section holds both guides, each centered in its own
        ## half of the window
        d = (gap + w_core) / 2  # [nm] each guide's distance from the center
        em.settings(window_width=4 * d + 2000, num_modes=2 * num_modes)
        em.shape(name='core', mask=[w_core, w_core], mask_offset=[-d, d])
        em.label_profile(name='pair')

        ## A window on each side of the coupler gives the bus and the ring their own
        ## ports, so the ring can be closed while the bus stays open
        window = lambda x: Bounds(window_width=2 * d, window_height=window_height, offset=(x, 0.0))
        em.straight_section(
            name='coupler', profile='pair', length=coupler_length,
            ports=[Port(name='bus_in', side='left', window=window(-d)),
                   Port(name='ring_in', side='left', window=window(d)),
                   Port(name='bus_out', side='right', window=window(-d)),
                   Port(name='ring_out', side='right', window=window(d))])

        ## The bends are refined more finely than the default: the crystal turns in
        ## steps from slice to slice, and the default slicing loses about 1.6 % of
        ## the power in each half circle to that staircase
        bend_settings = {'overlap_variation': 0.003}
        em.bend_section(name='bend_1', profile='ring', radius=radius,
                        sweep_angle=np.pi, settings=bend_settings)
        em.straight_section(name='back', profile='ring', length=coupler_length)
        em.bend_section(name='bend_2', profile='ring', radius=radius,
                        sweep_angle=np.pi, settings=bend_settings)

        em.connect_ports(pairs=[('coupler.ring_out', 'bend_1.left'),
                                ('bend_1.right', 'back.left'),
                                ('back.right', 'bend_2.left'),
                                ('bend_2.right', 'coupler.ring_in')])

        ## The loop has to close on itself before anything is solved
        report = em.check_layout()
        distance, angle = report.max_closure()
        print(f'the loop closes to {distance:.1e} nm and {angle:.1e} rad')

        em.EME()

        ## The through-port spectrum over a few free spectral ranges. The circuit is
        ## refined once, its cross-sections are solved at a few wavelengths, and the
        ## S-matrix at every wavelength below is rebuilt from them.
        wavelengths = np.arange(1546.0, 1556.0, 0.005)  # [nm]
        data = em.sweep(key='wavelength', values=wavelengths, result='S_matrix',
                        method='interpolated', num_nodes=6,
                        wavelength_range=(wavelengths[0], wavelengths[-1]))
        T = np.array([np.abs(S.block('coupler.bus_out', 'coupler.bus_in')[0, 0]) ** 2
                      for S in data['S_matrix']])

        ## The resonances, their spacing, depth and loaded quality factor
        dips = np.where((T[1:-1] < T[:-2]) & (T[1:-1] < T[2:]) & (T[1:-1] < 0.9))[0] + 1
        fsr = np.mean(np.diff(wavelengths[dips]))
        print(f'free spectral range: {fsr:.2f} nm')
        for k in dips:
            half = (1 + T[k]) / 2
            lo, hi = k, k
            while lo > 0 and T[lo] < half:
                lo -= 1
            while hi < len(T) - 1 and T[hi] < half:
                hi += 1
            width = wavelengths[hi] - wavelengths[lo]
            print(f'resonance at {wavelengths[k]:.3f} nm: extinction {-10 * np.log10(T[k]):.1f} dB, '
                  f'loaded Q {wavelengths[k] / width:.0f}')

        ## The field around the ring on its middle resonance, solved there directly
        ## and drawn where the layout places each section. The sections are built on
        ## the labeled profiles, so the wavelength is set on each of them.
        resonance = wavelengths[dips[len(dips) // 2]]
        for name in ('ring', 'pair'):
            em.settings(profile=name, wavelength=resonance)
        em.EME()
        em.plot(component='Ex', plot_function='abs', plane='z-x', view='layout',
                file_name='tfln_ring_field', file_type='png')

        em.close()

        plt.figure(figsize=(7, 3.5))
        plt.plot(wavelengths, 10 * np.log10(T))
        plt.xlabel('Wavelength (nm)')
        plt.ylabel('Through port (dB)')
        plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        plt.savefig('tfln_ring_spectrum.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

EME: MMI
--------

Two multimode interference (MMI) couplers in silicon at 1550 nm: a 1x2 splitter whose length is
swept around the self-imaging estimate, and a 2x2 coupler whose width and length are optimized
together for a 50/50 split with ``optimize()``.

Both couplers are silicon strips 220 nm thick in silica, built from three straight sections: the
access waveguides, the MMI body and the output waveguides. A window around each access waveguide
gives it its own port, so the S-matrix names each arm, and ``boundary_condition='TE-v'`` folds the
window to halve the solve.

The self-imaging lengths that follow from the beat length :math:`L_\pi` are only estimates for a
high-contrast guide, and the best images form a few percent shorter. A length sweep reuses the
solved modes and solves nothing, so the example sweeps the length first and lets the optimizer
refine from the best image. Light reflected between the two ends of the MMI body makes the split
ripple with the length, and each trough of that ripple is a local optimum, so the optimizer is kept
within one ripple period of its starting point.

The optimized 2x2 splits close to 50/50, with the through port leading the cross port by close to
the ideal 90 degrees, and it keeps a balanced split over several tens of nanometers around 1550 nm.
Every console report also says where the rest of the power goes: the higher-order modes of the
output waveguides, the reflection back into the input, and the light scattered into the cladding.
The access waveguides meet the MMI straight, with no tapers, which a fabricated device adds to lower
the loss.

*This code example is licensed under the* `BSD 3-Clause License <../_static/LICENSE.html>`_.

.. tabs::

    .. code-tab:: python
        :caption: Python

        import sys
        import numpy as np
        import emodeconnection as emc
        from emodeconnection import Port, Bounds, Parameter, Objective
        from matplotlib import pyplot as plt

        ## Set simulation parameters
        wavelength = 1550  # [nm] wavelength
        dx, dy = 25, 25  # [nm] resolution
        h_core = 220  # [nm] silicon thickness
        w_access = 1000  # [nm] access waveguide width at the MMI
        pitch = 1500  # [nm] center-to-center spacing of the access waveguides
        access_length = 2000  # [nm] length of each access section
        w_1x2 = 3000  # [nm] 1x2 MMI width, its outputs at +/- w_1x2 / 4
        w_2x2 = 4500  # [nm] 2x2 MMI width, its ports at +/- w_2x2 / 6
        window_height = 2000  # [nm]
        num_modes = 30  # [-]

        ## The cross-sections are silicon strips in silica, symmetric top to bottom,
        ## so boundary_condition='TE-v' folds the window at its middle and keeps the
        ## TE-like modes, the ones an MMI for TE light is designed with. A window
        ## around each access waveguide gives it its own port.
        d = pitch / 2  # [nm] each access waveguide's distance from the center
        window = lambda x: Bounds(window_width=pitch, window_height=window_height, offset=(x, 0.0))
        arms = lambda side: [Port(name='a', side=side, window=window(-d)),
                             Port(name='b', side=side, window=window(d))]

        def mmi(name, width, num_inputs):
            """Declare an MMI with one or two inputs and two outputs, and return its beat length."""
            em = emc.EMode(emode_cmd=sys.argv[1:], simulation_name=name)
            em.settings(
                wavelength=wavelength, x_resolution=dx, y_resolution=dy,
                window_width=width + 2000, window_height=window_height,
                num_modes=num_modes, boundary_condition='TE-v',
                background_material='SiO2')
            em.shape(name='core', material='Si', height=h_core, etch_depth=h_core,
                     position=[0, window_height / 2], mask=w_access)
            em.label_profile(name='single')
            em.shape(name='core', mask=[w_access, w_access], mask_offset=[-d, d])
            em.label_profile(name='pair')

            ## The MMI body is the default profile, so a 'shape, core, mask' key
            ## changes its width. Its two lowest modes give the beat length L_pi.
            em.shape(name='core', mask=width, mask_offset=0)
            em.FDM()
            n_eff = np.real(np.asarray(em.get('effective_index')))
            beat_length = wavelength / (2 * (n_eff[0] - n_eff[1]))

            if num_inputs == 1:
                em.straight_section(name='in', profile='single', length=access_length)
            else:
                em.straight_section(name='in', profile='pair', length=access_length, ports=arms('left'))
            em.straight_section(name='mmi', profile='_default', length=beat_length)
            em.straight_section(name='out', profile='pair', length=access_length, ports=arms('right'))
            return em, beat_length

        def report(label, S, into):
            """Print where the power launched into port `into` goes."""
            a = np.abs(S.block('out.a', into)[0, 0]) ** 2
            b = np.abs(S.block('out.b', into)[0, 0]) ** 2
            reflected = np.sum(np.abs(S.block(into, into)[:, 0]) ** 2)
            higher = (np.sum(np.abs(S.block('out.a', into)[1:, 0]) ** 2)
                      + np.sum(np.abs(S.block('out.b', into)[1:, 0]) ** 2))
            print(f'{label} power in output a: {a:.4f}')
            print(f'{label} power in output b: {b:.4f}')
            print(f'{label} excess loss: {-10 * np.log10(a + b):.3f} dB')
            print(f'{label} imbalance, a over b: {round(10 * np.log10(a / b), 3) + 0.0:.3f} dB')
            print(f'{label} reflection: {10 * np.log10(reflected):.1f} dB')
            print(f'{label} power in higher-order output modes: {higher:.4f}')
            print(f'{label} power scattered out of the guides: {1 - a - b - reflected - higher:.4f}')

        ## ---------------------------------------------------------------- the 1x2
        ## One input on the axis forms two images at 3 L_pi / 8. That estimate uses
        ## only the two lowest modes, so the length is swept around it. A length
        ## sweep reuses the solved modes and solves nothing.
        em, beat_length = mmi('mmi_1x2', w_1x2, num_inputs=1)
        print(f'1x2 beat length L_pi: {beat_length:.0f} nm')
        print(f'1x2 self-imaging length 3 L_pi / 8: {3 * beat_length / 8:.0f} nm')

        lengths = 3 * beat_length / 8 * np.linspace(0.85, 1.1, 26)  # [nm]
        data = em.sweep(key='section, mmi, length', values=lengths, result='S_matrix')
        T = np.array([np.abs(S.block('out.a', 'in.left')[0, 0]) ** 2
                      + np.abs(S.block('out.b', 'in.left')[0, 0]) ** 2 for S in data['S_matrix']])
        best_length = lengths[np.argmax(T)]
        print(f'1x2 best length: {best_length:.0f} nm')

        em.straight_section(name='mmi', length=best_length)
        em.EME()
        report('1x2', em.get('S_matrix'), 'in.left')
        em.plot(component='Ex', plot_function='abs', plane='z-x', view='layout',
                file_name='mmi_1x2_field', file_type='png')
        em.close()

        plt.figure(figsize=(6, 3.5))
        plt.plot(lengths / 1e3, T)
        plt.axvline(3 * beat_length / 8e3, color='gray', ls='--', label='3 L$_\\pi$ / 8')
        plt.xlabel('MMI length (um)')
        plt.ylabel('Power in both outputs')
        plt.legend()
        plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        plt.savefig('mmi_1x2_length.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

        ## ---------------------------------------------------------------- the 2x2
        ## Inputs at a third of the way from the axis to each edge excite only the
        ## modes that image in pairs, so a 50/50 split forms at L_pi / 2.
        em, beat_length = mmi('mmi_2x2', w_2x2, num_inputs=2)
        x0 = beat_length / 2
        print(f'2x2 beat length L_pi: {beat_length:.0f} nm')
        print(f'2x2 self-imaging length L_pi / 2: {x0:.0f} nm')

        ## How far both outputs are from 0.5, the quantity the optimizer minimizes
        through = Objective('S_power', out='out.a', into='in.a', goal='target', target=0.5)
        cross = Objective('S_power', out='out.b', into='in.a', goal='target', target=0.5)
        distance = lambda S: ((np.abs(S.block('out.a', 'in.a')[0, 0]) ** 2 - 0.5) ** 2
                              + (np.abs(S.block('out.b', 'in.a')[0, 0]) ** 2 - 0.5) ** 2)

        ## Light reflected at the two ends of the MMI body ripples the split with
        ## the length, with a period of about half a wavelength in the guide
        ## (270 nm), and every trough of that ripple is a local minimum. A length
        ## sweep at the starting width, which solves nothing, finds the best image.
        ## The optimizer then adjusts the width and the length together within
        ## 100 nm of it, less than half the ripple's period, so it stays in that
        ## trough.
        lengths = x0 * np.arange(0.9, 1.05, 0.002)  # [nm]
        data = em.sweep(key='section, mmi, length', values=lengths, result='S_matrix')
        start = lengths[np.argmin([distance(S) for S in data['S_matrix']])]
        print(f'2x2 best length at {w_2x2} nm wide: {start:.0f} nm')

        res = em.optimize(
            parameters=[Parameter('shape, core, mask', bounds=(w_2x2 - 300, w_2x2 + 300), x0=w_2x2),
                        Parameter('section, mmi, length', bounds=(start - 100, start + 100), x0=start)],
            objective=[through, cross],
            max_evaluations=80, tolerance=1e-5)
        width, length = res.x
        print(f'2x2 optimizer: {res.status} after {res.evaluations} evaluations in {res.seconds:.0f} s')
        print(f'2x2 optimized width: {width:.1f} nm')
        print(f'2x2 optimized length: {length:.0f} nm')

        ## The simulation is left solved at the best point
        S = em.get('S_matrix')
        report('2x2', S, 'in.a')
        phase_through = np.angle(S.block('out.a', 'in.a')[0, 0], deg=True)
        phase_cross = np.angle(S.block('out.b', 'in.a')[0, 0], deg=True)
        print(f'2x2 through-port phase: {phase_through:.1f} deg')
        print(f'2x2 cross-port phase: {phase_cross:.1f} deg')
        print(f'2x2 phase difference, through minus cross: '
              f'{(phase_through - phase_cross + 180) % 360 - 180:.1f} deg')
        em.plot(component='Ex', plot_function='abs', plane='z-x', view='layout',
                file_name='mmi_2x2_field', file_type='png')

        ## The bandwidth of the optimized 2x2 over 200 nm. The sections are built on
        ## the labeled profile 'pair' and on the default profile, so the wavelength
        ## is set on both before each solve.
        wavelengths = np.linspace(1450, 1650, 11)  # [nm]
        P_through, P_cross = [], []
        for wl in wavelengths:
            em.settings(wavelength=wl)
            em.settings(profile='pair', wavelength=wl)
            em.EME()
            S = em.get('S_matrix')
            P_through.append(np.abs(S.block('out.a', 'in.a')[0, 0]) ** 2)
            P_cross.append(np.abs(S.block('out.b', 'in.a')[0, 0]) ** 2)
        P_through, P_cross = np.array(P_through), np.array(P_cross)

        ## The band where the imbalance stays within 0.5 dB and the excess loss
        ## below 1 dB, read off the solved wavelengths by linear interpolation
        fine = np.linspace(wavelengths[0], wavelengths[-1], 1001)
        imbalance = np.interp(fine, wavelengths, 10 * np.log10(P_through / P_cross))
        excess_loss = np.interp(fine, wavelengths, -10 * np.log10(P_through + P_cross))
        band = fine[(np.abs(imbalance) <= 0.5) & (excess_loss <= 1)]
        print(f'2x2 band, imbalance within 0.5 dB and excess loss below 1 dB, from: {band.min():.0f} nm')
        print(f'2x2 band, imbalance within 0.5 dB and excess loss below 1 dB, to: {band.max():.0f} nm')
        em.close()

        plt.figure(figsize=(6, 3.5))
        plt.plot(wavelengths, 10 * np.log10(P_through), marker='o', ms=3, label='through')
        plt.plot(wavelengths, 10 * np.log10(P_cross), marker='o', ms=3, label='cross')
        plt.plot(wavelengths, 10 * np.log10(P_through + P_cross), color='gray', ls='--', label='total')
        plt.xlabel('Wavelength (nm)')
        plt.ylabel('Transmission (dB)')
        plt.legend()
        plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        plt.savefig('mmi_2x2_spectrum.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
